Yahusha (Jesus) says he came to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous, in the same breath as I will have mercy, and not sacrifice. The publicans at his table who turned had made the offering Sirach describes; the men standing outside objecting to the company had brought their sacrifices and left the turning undone.
4401.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:3 — *to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.* The turning is the offering; Matthew 9:13 calls sinners to that repentance.
4401.old_note: *To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:3 names the wisdom-stream's atonement-substance: turning-from-wickedness IS propitiation. The Pharisaic-counterfeit at Matt 9:11-13 is the categorical-credential-without-heart-turning; Yahusha (Jesus) calls Mattityahu (Matthew) and the publicans-and-sinners to *repentance* (v.13b) precisely because their turning IS the propitiation the wisdom-stream had named.

4402.new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Give to the poor and turn your face from none, and the face of Yahuah (God) will not turn from you. That is the mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice, the word Yahusha (Jesus) sends the Pharisees to go and learn. They were offended that he sat at table with sinners (9:11); Tobit had told his son not to turn his face from any poor man. Mercy toward the one in need is the heart of the Torah, and a system that keeps its credentials clean while turning its face away has lost the thing the commandment was for.
4402.member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice, which the Pharisees at the table had forgotten (Matthew 9:13).
4402.old_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* Tobit 4:7 names the wisdom-stream's alms-and-mercy architecture as the heart-of-the-Torah-substance — giving alms with the eye-not-envious is the heart-Torah Hosea 6:6 names. The Pharisaic-counterfeit at Matt 9:11's indignation over the table-fellowship-with-sinners is the inverse: envy-of-the-mercy-extended-to-the-marginalized in the costume of purity-credential.

4403.new_note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* (Tobit 4:9). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Alms laid up are a treasure against the day of need; Tobit sees the open hand as storing something before Yahuah (God). Yahusha (Jesus) tells the Pharisees to go learn Hosea's word, mercy and not sacrifice. They had stored up sacrifices and credentials; the heart of the Torah was the mercy Tobit's son was told to lay up. The treasure that counts in the day of necessity is the mercy that was done, and the King is calling a religious system back to it.
4403.member_note: Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The treasure laid up by mercy, the thing Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).
4403.old_note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Tobit 4:9 names the alms-as-laid-up-treasure-against-the-day architecture explicitly — alms in the present-age lay up good treasure against the eschatological-day-of-necessity. The Sermon's own *lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven* (Matthew 6:19-20) walks the same architecture in the heart-Torah register; Matt 9:13's *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens dismantling of the Pharisaic-counterfeit.

4404.new_note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* (Tobit 4:10). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Tobit says alms deliver from death, and he says it in the voice of a father who has lived it. The Pharisees at Matthew's table had their sacrifices in order and their mercy withheld, and the King sent them to Hosea: mercy, and not sacrifice. Tobit had already named mercy as the thing that delivers. A religion that keeps its offerings and loses its mercy has kept the shell and lost the life.
4404.member_note: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Mercy is what delivers, and mercy is what Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).
4404.old_note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Tobit 4:10 names the alms-as-deliverance-from-death architecture in the wisdom-stream's eschatological register. The Pharisaic-counterfeit collects sacrifice-credential while withholding the mercy-substance that Tobit names as the actual deliverance-architecture. Matt 9:13's Hosea 6:6 citation walks the same diagnostic at the kingdom-citizens level: the mercy-substance IS the deliverance-substance.

4405.new_note: *For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:* (Tobit 12:9). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Raphael's last word to Tobit and Tobias is that alms deliver from death and purge away all sin, and that those who do alms and righteousness are filled with life. This is mercy given the weight of life and death. In Matthew 9 the King forgives a paralytic (9:2) and sits at table with sinners, and when the Pharisees object he sends them to Hosea: mercy, and not sacrifice. Mercy is what the Torah asked for, mercy is what delivers, and the King and the angel are saying one thing.
4405.member_note: Tobit 12:9 — *alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin.* Mercy with the weight of life and death, the mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).
4405.old_note: *For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life.* Tobit 12:9 (the angel Raphael's closing instruction to Tobit and Tobias) names the alms-purges-away-all-sin architecture explicitly — the wisdom-stream's naming of the mercy-substance as the very forgiveness-substance the King exercises at the paralytic's pronouncement (Matt 9:2) and the Mattityahu (Matthew) table (Matt 9:13). Alms-and-righteousness — heart-Torah — is the deliverance-architecture both passages walk.

4406.new_note: *Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* (Ecclesiasticus 12:4). *And it came to pass, as Yahusha (Jesus) sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.* (Matthew 9:10). Sirach says to give to the godly man and not to help a sinner, and the next verse shows what he means — bread given to the ungodly becomes strength he uses against you. Yahusha (Jesus) sat at meat with publicans and sinners. These are not two stances at war. The sinners at that table had come to him, and he was calling them to repentance, not feeding them in their sin. Sirach guards the hand; the King opens the door; and the Pharisee who turned the one into a wall against persons had misread it and could not see the other.
4406.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 12:4 — *Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* Sirach guards the hand from strengthening the ungodly; the King's table at Matthew 9:10 calls sinners to turn.
4406.reason: Theology correction: the old note said Sirach 12 taught a wrong, categorical exclusion that the King reversed and superseded — pitting a scripture-level book against the gospel and dismissing Sirach's almsgiving counsel. Rewritten so both hold: Sirach warns against strengthening the ungodly in their wickedness with your bread; Yahusha (Jesus) eats with sinners who came to hear and are being called to repentance. The system that turned the caution into a wall around the table is what is corrected, not Sirach.
4406.old_note: *Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12:4 names the wisdom-stream's discriminating-mercy stance that the Pharisaic-counterfeit-righteousness inherited and weaponized: hold-back-mercy-from-the-sinner because the sinner is categorically excluded from the wisdom-stream's mercy-flow. The framework reads Matt 9:10's *many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him* as the King's direct-reversal of the Sirach 12 stance — the categorical-exclusion the wisdom-stream had taught is dismantled at the table the King keeps.

4407.new_note: *Do well to him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold back your bread, and give it not to him, lest he overmaster you thereby: for else you shall receive twice as much evil for all the good you shall have done to him.* (Ecclesiasticus 12:5). *And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?* (Matthew 9:11). Sirach says to do well to the lowly but to hold back your bread from the ungodly, because what you give him he will turn into power over you. The Pharisees asked why the Master ate with publicans and sinners, as if this verse had been broken. It had not. Sirach is warning against strengthening a man in his wickedness; Yahusha (Jesus) was eating with men who had come to hear him and were being called out of theirs. The ungodly in Sirach is the man who stays ungodly with your bread in his hand; the sinner at the King's table is the one who heard and sat down.
4407.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 12:5 — *hold back your bread, and give it not to him, lest he overmaster you thereby.* Bread held back from the one who would overmaster you is not the table the Pharisees question at Matthew 9:11.
4407.reason: Theology correction: the old note said Sirach 12 taught a wrong, categorical exclusion that the King reversed and superseded — pitting a scripture-level book against the gospel and dismissing Sirach's almsgiving counsel. Rewritten so both hold: Sirach warns against strengthening the ungodly in their wickedness with your bread; Yahusha (Jesus) eats with sinners who came to hear and are being called to repentance. The system that turned the caution into a wall around the table is what is corrected, not Sirach.
4407.old_note: *Do well to him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold back your bread, and give it not to him.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12:5 names the wisdom-stream's explicit instruction the Pharisees of Matt 9:11 are operating under — hold-back-the-bread-from-the-ungodly. The Pharisaic *why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?* indictment of Matt 9:11 IS the Sirach 12:5 framework operative; Yahusha (Jesus) is breaking the wisdom-stream's discriminating-bread-fellowship rule by eating with those Sirach 12 instructed his disciples to hold-back-from. The framework reading: not every wisdom-stream teaching is operative in the kingdom-at-hand; the King's direct-mercy supersedes the wisdom-stream's categorical-exclusion stance.

4408.new_note: *Give to the good, and help not the sinner.* (Ecclesiasticus 12:7). *But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13). Sirach says it again: give to the good, help not the sinner. Yahusha (Jesus) says he came not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance, and he sends the Pharisees to learn what mercy and not sacrifice means. The two verses meet at the word repentance. Sirach withholds help from the sinner who stays a sinner; the King calls the sinner to stop being one, and the mercy he names is the call itself. Neither verse feeds a man in his wickedness, and neither shuts the door on the man who turns.
4408.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 12:7 — *Give to the good, and help not the sinner.* Help not the sinner and call sinners to repentance (Matthew 9:13) meet at the word repentance.
4408.reason: Theology correction: the old note said Sirach 12 taught a wrong, categorical exclusion that the King reversed and superseded — pitting a scripture-level book against the gospel and dismissing Sirach's almsgiving counsel. Rewritten so both hold: Sirach warns against strengthening the ungodly in their wickedness with your bread; Yahusha (Jesus) eats with sinners who came to hear and are being called to repentance. The system that turned the caution into a wall around the table is what is corrected, not Sirach.
4408.old_note: *Give to the good, and help not the sinner.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12:7 reiterates the wisdom-stream's categorical-exclusion stance the King reverses at Matt 9:13. Yahusha (Jesus) is *not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance* — the inverse of the Sirach 12 mandate. The wisdom-stream had a wrong-stance on this; the King restores the heart-Torah by going TO the sinners precisely because the wisdom-stream's discriminating-mercy excluded them. The Hosea 6:6 mercy-substance is BROADER than the wisdom-stream's godly-righteous register; it extends to the sinners-to-be-called.

4412.new_note: *Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold:* (Tobit 12:8). *Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast oft, but thy disciples fast not?* (Matthew 9:14). The angel Raphael tells Tobit and his son that prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness, all together, and that a little with righteousness outweighs much without it. John's disciples asked Yahusha (Jesus) why his disciples did not fast as they and the Pharisees did. He does not throw fasting out — he says the days will come when they will fast (9:15) — but he sets it where the angel set it, as one part of a life of mercy and righteousness, not a credential by itself. Fasting alone was never the discipline; fasting with prayer, alms, and righteousness is what the angel taught Tobit and what the King restores.
4412.member_note: Tobit 12:8 — *Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.* Fasting belongs with prayer, alms, and righteousness, not alone; the King keeps it in that place (Matthew 9:14).
4412.old_note: *Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold.* Tobit 12:8 (the angel Raphael's instruction) names the wisdom-stream's prayer-fasting-alms-righteousness triad as the operative-discipline of the godly. Matt 9:14's fasting-question presupposes the Pharisaic-style fasting-as-credential-without-the-mercy-triad operative; Yahusha (Jesus) does not abolish fasting (he affirms it at v.15b *then shall they fast*) but reframes it in the bridegroom-architecture and in the Tobit-mercy-triad. Fasting alone is not the discipline; fasting WITH prayer, alms, and righteousness is the wisdom-stream's teaching the King restores.

4413.new_note: *So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?* (Ecclesiasticus 34:26). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.* (Matthew 9:15). Sirach asks what a man's fast profits him when he fasts for his sins and then goes back and does the same; who will hear his prayer? When John's disciples asked why his disciples did not fast, Yahusha (Jesus) did not do away with fasting; he said the days would come when they would fast. But he placed it after the bridegroom is taken, in the grief of a people who have truly lost something, not as a routine kept while nothing changes. Sirach had already named the difference: a fast that turns from the sin is heard, and a fast that returns to it is noise.
4413.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 34:26 — *a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer?.* Fasting that turns is heard; *then shall they fast* (Matthew 9:15) is fasting with the loss truly felt.
4413.old_note: *So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 34:26 names the wisdom-stream's fasting-without-repentance-is-vain diagnostic explicitly — the faster who fasts for his sins and continues in them is not heard. The Pharisaic-counterfeit form at Matt 9:14 is fasting-as-credential while the categorical-exclusion-of-sinners and the mercy-withholding continues; Sirach 34:26 had named the diagnostic centuries before. The King's bridegroom-frame at Matt 9:15 reframes fasting in the wedding-substance; the post-ascension assembly fasts (*then shall they fast*) but in the mercy-substance Sirach 34:26 implied as the precondition.

4414.new_note: *Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.* (Ecclesiasticus 9:10). *Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.* (Matthew 9:17). Sirach honors the old friend and the old wine; the new has to age before it is worth drinking. Yahusha (Jesus) is not quarreling with that. The question put to him in Matthew 9 was about fasting, and his answer is about the vessel: new wine poured into a brittle old skin bursts it and both are lost. The Torah is neither the wine nor the skin; it is the vineyard the wine comes from. The skin that cannot stretch is the body of added tradition, and the wine the King pours will itself grow old and be drunk with pleasure, exactly as Sirach says new wine does.
4414.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 9:10 — *a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.* Sirach's new wine that ages well sits beside the new wine and new bottles of Matthew 9:17.
4414.reason: Theology correction: the old note read Sirach's old-friend loyalty as itself the Pharisaic old wineskin that bursts — pitting the wisdom book against the gospel. Rewritten so the two agree: the Torah is neither wine nor skin, the brittle skin is added tradition, and Sirach's own line (new wine ages into pleasure) supports rather than opposes the King.
4414.old_note: *Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 9:10 names the wisdom-stream's old-vs-new wine register — the wisdom-stream holds the old friend (and the old wine) as more trustworthy than the new. The framework reads Matt 9:17's new-wine / new-bottles parable in inverse register: the wisdom-stream's old-is-better register is precisely the Pharisaic-rabbinic-system's self-justification — the old-tradition-fences cannot be ruptured by the new heart-Torah-walking. The framework angle is that the wisdom-stream RECOGNIZES the new-vs-old containment question as a real question; the gospel REFRAMES it by naming the heart-Torah-substance the new-heart container holds and the Pharisaic-old-bottle cannot. The Torah itself is NEITHER the wine NOR the wineskin; the Pharisaic-system's wisdom-stream-old-friend-loyalty is the old wineskin that bursts when the heart-Torah-life enters.

4415.new_note: *My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* (Ecclesiasticus 38:9). *And, behold, a woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the hem of his garment:* (Matthew 9:20). Sirach tells the sick man not to be negligent but to pray to Yahuah (God), who will make him whole. The woman with the issue of blood had been sick twelve years, and she came behind Yahusha (Jesus) and touched the hem of his garment, and he turned and told her that her faith had made her whole. She was not going around Sirach's counsel; she was doing it. The one who spoke and walked with the fathers was standing in the crowd in flesh, and reaching for his garment was her prayer to Yahuah (God).
4415.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 38:9 — *pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* The woman who touched the hem (Matthew 9:20) made that prayer with her hand.
4415.reason: Theology correction: the old note called the woman's touch an 'inversion' or 'bypass' of Sirach's pray-first counsel. Rewritten: Yahusha (Jesus) is the Formed one who spoke in the Tanakh, so reaching for him is the prayer Sirach prescribes, not a way around it.
4415.old_note: *My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 38:9 names the wisdom-stream's prescribed-healing-architecture: pray to the Most High first; he will make you whole. The bleeding-woman of Matt 9:20-22 walks an inversion of the Sirach-38 architecture in one register and a fulfillment in another. The framework reads the inversion: she does not pray-then-wait for the indirect-healing-flow Sirach prescribes; she touches the King's garment directly because the King is the Formed-Voice through whom the Most High's healing-flow operates in present-tense-direct.

4416.new_note: *Then give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.* (Ecclesiasticus 38:12). *But Yahusha (Jesus) turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.* (Matthew 9:22). Sirach does not slight the physician; he says Yahuah (God) created him and tells the sick man to keep him close. The woman with the issue of blood did exactly that for twelve years, and Mark 5:26 adds that she spent all she had on physicians and only grew worse. When she reached for the hem of his garment she was reaching past the physician to the one who made the physician, and Yahusha (Jesus) does not rebuke the years she spent under their care; he names her faith as what made her whole. The physician is a gift from his hand, and the healing was always his.
4416.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 38:12 — *give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him.* The bleeding woman gave place to physicians for twelve years; at Matthew 9:22 she reached past them to the one who made them, and her faith made her whole.
4416.old_note: *Then give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 38:12 names the wisdom-stream's give-place-to-the-physician prescription. The bleeding-woman of Matt 9:20-22 had given place to physicians for twelve years (Mark 5:26 records the Sirach-38 prescription faithfully followed and failed); the King's direct-cleansing-source-touch reverses the defiling-flow that the physician-chain could not heal — and Yahusha (Jesus) names her faith (not her physician-adherence) as the architecture of her wholeness at v.22.

4417.new_note: *For they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give for ease and remedy to prolong life.* (Ecclesiasticus 38:14). *But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.* (Matthew 9:25). Sirach says the physician himself prays to Yahuah (God) that the remedy in his hand would prosper, because the healing never belonged to the remedy. In the ruler's house the remedies have run out; the girl is dead, and no physician prays over a corpse. Yahusha (Jesus) walks in and takes her by the hand, and the one the physician prays to is the one standing in the room. The physician asks for the prospering; here the giver of it does the work with his own hand.
4417.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 38:14 — *they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give.* The physician prays that his remedy would prosper; at Matthew 9:25 the one he prays to takes the dead girl by the hand himself.
4417.old_note: *For they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give for ease and remedy to prolong life.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 38:14 names the wisdom-stream's physician-prays-to-the-Most-High architecture — the physician's success is itself dependent on the Most High's prosper-the-remedy authority. At Matt 9:25 the King takes the dead girl's hand directly; the physician-chain has reached its limit (the girl is dead), and the prosper-the-remedy authority Sirach 38 names as flowing through the physician-prayer-chain is now exercised directly by the Formed-in-flesh.

4418.new_note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). *He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.* (Matthew 9:24). Power of life and death belongs to Yahuah (God): he leads to the gates of hell, the grave, and brings up again. In the ruler's house the King looked at a dead girl and said she was not dead but sleeping, and the mourners laughed at him. Then he took her by the hand and she arose. The one who brings up again from the gates of the grave was standing in the room in flesh, and death in his presence is sleep because he is the one who wakes it. The righteous dead are asleep the same way, and the hand that took the girl's hand is the one that will bring them up.
4418.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The maid not dead but sleeping (Matthew 9:24) is raised by the one who leads to the grave and brings up again.
4418.old_note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the Most High's power-of-life-and-death: he leads to the gates of hell, and brings up again. Matt 9:24's *the maid is not dead, but sleepeth* and 9:25's raising-of-Yair's-daughter walk the same architecture in flesh-presence: the King who exercises the power-of-life-and-death IS the Formed through whom that power operates. The wisdom-stream had named the Most High's authority over death; the King at Matt 9:25 IS that authority in flesh.

4419.new_note: *A man indeed killeth through his malice: and the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not; neither the soul received up comes again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:14). *But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.* (Matthew 9:25). The verse draws the line a man cannot cross: he can kill, but once the spirit has gone forth he cannot call it back. Then Yahusha (Jesus) takes a dead girl by the hand and she arises. What Wisdom of Solomon had just said belongs to Yahuah (God) alone — the power of life and death, leading down and bringing up again (16:13) — is done in a house in Capernaum by a man with his hand on a child. That is who he is: not the formless Father, but the one through whom the Father's power has always acted, now standing in flesh.
4419.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:14 — *the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not.* What no man can do, the King does with his hand on a dead girl (Matthew 9:25).
4419.old_note: *A man indeed killeth through his malice: and the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not; neither the soul received up comes again.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:14 names the wisdom-stream's mortal-man-cannot-bring-back diagnostic explicitly — the spirit that is gone returns not; the soul received up comes not again BY MAN. The framework reads Matt 9:25 against the diagnostic: the King brings back the spirit that has gone, raises the daughter the wisdom-stream had named no-mortal-can-raise. The Formed-in-flesh exercises the prerogative the wisdom-stream had named as the Most High's alone — confirming the Formed-from-the-Formless framework on the nature of Yahusha (Jesus).

4420.new_note: *And the lion, whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring, and speaking to the eagle, and rebuking her for her unrighteousness with all the words which you have heard; This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them and for their wickedness to the end: he shall reprove them, and shall upbraid them with their cruelty.* (2 Esdras 12:31–32). *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27). Ezra's lion comes up roaring out of the wood and rebukes the eagle, which he had been told is the fourth kingdom Daniel saw (2 Esdras 12:11), and the angel then names the lion: the anointed, kept by the Highest to the end. Two blind men on the road name the same figure by his line, Son of David. The anointed one Ezra saw as a lion, the blind men perceived with no eyes, and they cried out to him as present. The Messiah (Christ) kept for the end was walking past them.
4420.member_note: 2 Esdras 12:31 — *the lion, whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring.* The lion named as the anointed is the Son of David the blind men cry to at Matthew 9:27.
4420.old_note: *And the lion, whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring, and speaking to the eagle, and rebuking her for her unrighteousness with all the words which you have heard...* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 12:31 names the lion-rising-out-of-the-wood vision the Most High's angel-interpreter identifies as the Messiah-from-the-seed-of-David at v.32. The framework reads the lion-symbol as the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-register naming of the Davidic-Messianic restoration-figure — the lion who rebukes the eagle (the fourth-beast-empire of Daniel 7) is the Messiah-anointed who Matt 9:27's blind men confess as *Son of David.*

4421.new_note: *This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them and for their wickedness to the end: he shall reprove them, and shall upbraid them with their cruelty.* (2 Esdras 12:32). *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27). The angel tells Ezra what the lion is: the anointed, kept by the Highest to the end, who will reprove the wicked for their cruelty. Two blind men cry to Yahusha (Jesus) as Son of David, the line the anointed king comes from. The one kept to the end to reprove the proud is the one who stops in the road for the blind who ask for mercy. The same anointed, seen by Ezra in a vision and met on a road.
4421.member_note: 2 Esdras 12:32 — *This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them.* The anointed kept to the end is the Son of David met on the road at Matthew 9:27.
4421.old_note: *This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them and for their wickedness to the end: he shall reprove them, and shall upbraid them with their cruelty.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 12:32 names the lion-figure as the anointed (the Messiah / Christ) the Most High has kept against the end-of-the-age — the figure who shall reprove and upbraid the cruelty of the wicked. The framework's Davidic-Messianic register at Matt 9:27 has its wisdom-stream apocalyptic-witness here: the Messiah-anointed from-the-seed-of-David is the figure the blind men confess in present-tense, and the figure 2 Esdras names as kept for the end. The same figure; the apocalyptic-stream named him; the in-flesh-King walks him.

4422.new_note: *For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning.* (2 Esdras 12:34). *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27). The anointed does two things in Ezra's vision: he reproves the eagle, and he delivers the rest of the people with mercy, those pressed upon the borders, and makes them joyful until the day of judgment. The blind men ask the Son of David for exactly that, mercy. The remnant pressed at the borders are the scattered of Yashar'el (Israel), and the first work of the Messiah (Christ) toward them is mercy, as it was for the two who cried out. He saw the multitudes as sheep having no shepherd and was moved for them (Matthew 9:36).
4422.member_note: 2 Esdras 12:34 — *the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders.* The blind men ask the Son of David for that same mercy at Matthew 9:27.
4422.old_note: *For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 12:34 names the Davidic-Messiah's deliver-with-mercy architecture explicitly — the Messiah delivers the remnant of the people with mercy, those who have been pressed upon the borders (the scattered seed). The framework's gathering-thesis lands at full weight in this verse: the Messiah-from-the-seed-of-David delivers the scattered-and-pressed remnant with mercy — Hosea 6:6's mercy-substance + the gathering of Matt 9:36 + the Davidic-Messianic recognition of Matt 9:27 are one architecture.

4423.new_note: *For my son the Messiah shall be revealed with those that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.* (2 Esdras 7:28). *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27). Ezra is told that the Most High's own son, the Messiah, will be revealed, with those that are with him. Two blind men who cannot see him cry out to him on the road as the Son of David and ask for mercy. What was spoken to Ezra as something still coming, they confess as someone present. The one the Most High calls my son and the one the blind men call Son of David are the same man standing in the road.
4423.member_note: 2 Esdras 7:28 — *my son the Messiah shall be revealed with those that be with him.* The blind men of Matthew 9:27 confess as present the one Ezra was told would be revealed.
4423.reason: The old note carried a textual remark that the seeded text's 'Yahusha (Jesus)' at this verse was corrected to 'the Messiah'. The live text already reads 'my son the Messiah', so nothing needed fixing; I left the remark out since the reader cannot see it. The 'within four hundred years' clause is not addressed by the note.
4423.old_note: *For my son the Messiah shall be revealed with those that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7:28 names the Messianic-revelation explicitly — the Most High's son the Messiah shall be revealed. (The seeded text's "Yahusha (Jesus)" naming at this verse is a Christian-era interpolation corrected by this migration to the underlying Syriac's *the Messiah*.) The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-register confirmation of the Davidic-Messianic figure Matt 9:27's blind men confess in present-tense — the Messiah whose revelation 4 Ezra had named as future is the figure the blind men perceive as present.

4429.new_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37). The souls of the righteous in their chambers ask how long, and when comes the fruit of the floor, the threshing floor where the reward is given. The King looks out over the multitudes and says the harvest is plenteous and the labourers few. Both speak of one harvest. The souls are asking when the floor will be filled; the King is sending men into the field to fill it, and the next verse in 2 Esdras gives the answer the souls received, when the number of seeds is filled. The waiting dead and the working living are looking toward the same floor from opposite sides of it.
4429.member_note: 2 Esdras 4:35 — *How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?.* The living are sent into the harvest the sleeping righteous wait for (Matthew 9:37).
4429.reason: Old note said the harvest the souls asked about 'is now plenteous' at the King's arrival. The floor of reward in 2 Esdras is the threshing at the end, not Galilee, so I wrote the field being gathered toward that floor rather than the floor having come.
4429.old_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:35 names the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-fruit-of-the-floor (= harvest) question explicitly — the souls of the righteous in their chambers ask how long until the harvest comes. Matt 9:37's *the harvest truly is plenteous* names the answer in present-tense at the King's arrival: the harvest the souls had asked about is now plenteous; the wisdom-stream's anticipation is met in the King's seeing of the multitudes.

4430.new_note: *And to these things Uriel the archangel gave them answer, and said, Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the balance.* (2 Esdras 4:36). *Pray ye therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.* (Matthew 9:38). Uriel's answer to the waiting souls is a number: the harvest comes when the number of seeds is filled, and he has weighed the world in the balance. The King's answer to a plenteous harvest with few labourers is a prayer: ask Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest to send forth labourers. The number is his and the timing is his, but the gathering is done by hands he sends, and the labourers he sends are how the seeds are filled up to the number. Esdras was shown why the end waits; the disciples were told what to do while it does.
4430.member_note: 2 Esdras 4:36 — *Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the balance.* The labourers sent into the harvest (Matthew 9:38) are how the number is filled.
4430.old_note: *And to these things Uriel the archangel gave them answer, and said, Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the balance.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:36 names the harvest-comes-when-the-number-of-seeds-is-filled architecture — the harvest is timed to the fulness of the seed-count. Matt 9:38's prayer-for-labourers is the kingdom-citizens' participation in the seed-filling: the labourers being sent into the harvest are the means by which the number of seeds is gathered to fulness. The wisdom-stream named the timing-architecture; the King at Matt 9:38 enlists the disciples in its execution.

4433.new_note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). Ezra is told plainly who the peaceable multitude of his vision is: the ten tribes Shalmaneser carried out of their own land and over the waters, who never came back. Those are the people the King means when he sends the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel). A sheep is lost when it has wandered where the shepherd cannot see it, and the northern house had been lost in another land for seven centuries by the time Yahusha (Jesus) spoke these words. The mission of the twelve was aimed at the same body Ezra was shown.
4433.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:40 — *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) the twelve are sent to at Matthew 10:6.
4433.old_note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:40 names the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-register identification of the ten tribes carried into Assyrian captivity over the waters into another land. Matt 10:6's *lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* names the same body — the scattered northern house Yahuah (the LORD) divorced through the Assyrian captivity, the lost sheep the prophets had named and promised the gathering for. The wisdom-stream had identified the same ten-tribes-carried-into-captivity body at the apocalyptic-register; the King at Matt 10:6 sends the twelve to that body.

4434.new_note: *But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.* (2 Esdras 13:41–42). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). The tribes did not simply vanish into the heathen. Ezra is told they took counsel to leave the multitude and go further out, into a country where no one lived, so that they could keep the statutes they had never kept in their own land. The carrying away became, for a remnant of them, a going out to keep Torah. Centuries later the King sends the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the same body, in the lands it went out to. The commandments they carried into the far country are what the sheep are being called back to, and Yahusha (Jesus) sends his messengers after them rather than waiting for them to find the way home alone.
4434.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:41 — *they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country.* The remnant went out to keep the statutes; the twelve are sent after them (Matthew 10:6).
4434.reason: Old note quoted 13:41-42 together and its point (keeping the statutes) sits in v.42, so both verses are quoted and cited as 13:41-42.
4434.old_note: *But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, that they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:41-42 names the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-register narrative of the scattered ten tribes leaving the heathen-multitude and going to a further country to keep the Torah-statutes they had not kept in the land — the post-Assyrian-captivity remnant carrying covenant-identity into the dispersion. Matt 10:6's mission-scope to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) is to the same body — the scattered seed who carried covenant-identity into the further-country territories.

4435.new_note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* (2 Esdras 13:47). *But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23). The Most High stayed the river once so the tribes could cross out, and Ezra is promised he will stay it again so they can cross back, in the latter time. That return is the end of the story the vision tells. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve they will not finish going over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) before the Son of Adam comes; the work he sends them on is not completed in their lifetime but runs until his coming. Set together, the two say the same thing: the going after the lost sheep and the gathering of the ten tribes are one work, begun with the sending and finished when the Highest opens the way home and the King returns.
4435.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:47 — *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through.* The way home opens at the latter time; the mission runs till the Son of Adam comes (Matthew 10:23).
4435.old_note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:47 names the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-register architecture of the gathering-of-the-ten-tribes back through the parted-stream at the latter-time arrival of the Messiah-son. Matt 10:23's *ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come* opens the gathering-mission's present-age-tense as the STANDING MISSION across centuries that the wisdom-stream had named as terminating in the latter-time gathering of the scattered tribes home. The mission Yahusha (Jesus) commissions at Matt 10 and the gathering 4 Ezra 13 names are one architecture continuing across the present age until the King returns.

4436.new_note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* (Tobit 13:5). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). Tobit lays out the whole order in one breath: Yahuah (God) scourges his people for their iniquities, has mercy again, and gathers them out of all the nations he scattered them into. The scourge was the scattering. The mercy is the gathering. When Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve, he points them at the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the very people Tobit said would be gathered, and the sending is that mercy beginning to move. The gathering Tobit prayed for as a thing still to come is the mission the King commissions.
4436.member_note: Tobit 13:5 — *he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations.* The gathering Tobit prayed for is the mission to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Matthew 10:6).
4436.reason: Dropped the old note's side reference to Hosea 6:6 / Matthew 9:13; its text was not given and the point stands without it.
4436.old_note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* Tobit 13:5 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the scourge-and-mercy-and-gathering architecture: Yahuah (God) scatters for iniquity, has mercy again, gathers from all the nations of the scattering. Matt 10:6's mission-scope to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) is the gathering-mission Tobit had named as Yahuah (God)'s future-tense covenant-action. The mercy-substance at Hosea 6:6 (Matt 9:13) is the same mercy-substance gathering the scattered at Matt 10:6.

4437.new_note: *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them. There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Elohim (God), and he is Yahuah (God) our Father for ever.* (Tobit 13:3–4). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Tobit sings this from the land of the captivity, and the instruction is not to hide among the Gentiles but to confess Yahuah (God) in front of them, to declare his greatness in the very places he scattered his children into. Yahusha (Jesus) is sending the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in this same chapter, and he gives them the same charge with a promise attached: confess me before men, and I will confess you before my Father. The scattered confess him where they were scattered, and the King names them before the Father. The confession Tobit called for and the confession Yahusha (Jesus) rewards are one confession, made by the same scattered people in the same territories.
4437.member_note: Tobit 13:3 — *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them.* The scattered confess him where they were scattered, and the King confesses them before his Father (Matthew 10:32).
4437.reason: Quoted Tobit 13:3–4 together, as the old note did; the point runs across both verses (confess before the Gentiles, declare his greatness there).
4437.old_note: *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them. There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Elohim (God), and he is Yahuah (God) our Father for ever.* Tobit 13:3-4 names the wisdom-stream's direct instruction: the children of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered among the Gentiles are to CONFESS Yahuah (God) BEFORE THE GENTILES — to declare his greatness in the territories of the scattering. Matt 10:32's *whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens level: the scattered seed in the dispersion confess the King before the men of the territories where they are scattered; the King confesses them before the Father.

4438.new_note: *And that again Yahuah (God) will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land, where they shall build a temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled; and afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously, and the house of Yahuah (God) shall be built in it for ever with a glorious building, as the prophets have spoken thereof.* (Tobit 14:5). *But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23). Tobit, dying, tells his son there will be two returns, not one. First a return to the land and a temple not like the first, which is the house Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah raised after Babylon, a return of Yahudah (Judah) only. Then, after the time of that age is fulfilled, a return from all places of the captivity, Jerusalem built gloriously and the house of Yahuah (God) built in it for ever, as the prophets spoke. That second return has not happened. Between the two stands the work Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve into, and he tells them it will not be finished before the Son of Adam comes. The mission to the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) runs through this age toward the return Tobit saw at the end of it.
4438.member_note: Tobit 14:5 — *afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously.* Two returns, the second still to come; the mission runs till the Son of Adam comes (Matthew 10:23).
4438.old_note: *And that again Yahuah (God) will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land, where they shall build a temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled; and afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) gloriously.* Tobit 14:5 names the wisdom-stream's multi-stage gathering-architecture explicitly: a FIRST return-to-the-land for the temple-rebuilding (the post-Babylon return under Zerubavel/Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nechemyah/Nehemiah), AND THEN a LATTER return *from all places of their captivity* at the fulness-of-the-age. Matt 10:23's *till the Son of Adam be come* opens the gathering-mission's present-age-tense as the standing-work until the Son of Adam returns; Tobit 14:5 names the same multi-stage architecture from the wisdom-stream side. The first stage was the partial Yahudah (Judah)-return; the latter is the still-future gathering-from-all-places-of-the-captivity.

4442.new_note: *My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:1). *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22). Sirach opens his second chapter by telling the one who comes to serve Yahuah (God) to expect temptation and get his soul ready for it, and the next line says how: set your heart aright, and constantly endure. Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve out with the same preparation. They will be hated for his name, and the one who endures to the end is the one who is saved. Neither voice promises the servant an easy road; both tie the outcome to endurance. The disciple's endurance is not something new the gospel invented; it is what serving Yahuah (God) has always asked, and Sirach had been saying so for generations before the twelve were sent.
4442.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 2:1 — *if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.* The endurance to the end Yahusha (Jesus) asks of the twelve at Matthew 10:22.
4442.old_note: *My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation. Set your heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 2:1-2 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the disciple-preparing-for-trial: prepare-the-soul, set-the-heart-aright, CONSTANTLY ENDURE. Matt 10:22's *he that endureth to the end shall be saved* walks the same wisdom-stream architecture at the kingdom-citizens level. The endurance is not innovation; the wisdom-stream had been naming the disciple-of-Yahuah (God) as the one-who-constantly-endures-through-trouble for centuries before the King commissions the twelve.

4443.new_note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22). Sirach says the furnace is where acceptable men are proved, the way fire proves gold. Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve into that furnace with his eyes open: hated of all men for his name, and saved by enduring to the end. The hatred is not a sign the mission failed; it is the fire doing what fire does, and the disciple who comes through it is shown to be what Sirach calls acceptable. Adversity in the service of Yahuah (God) is the trial, not the verdict.
4443.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 2:5 — *gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* The furnace the twelve are sent into at Matthew 10:22.
4443.old_note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 2:5 names the wisdom-stream's adversity-as-refining-furnace architecture: gold-tried-in-fire is the figure for the testing of the acceptable-disciple in the furnace of adversity. Matt 10:22's endure-to-the-end is the same architecture: the trial is the testing-furnace; the disciple endures and is shown acceptable. The wisdom-stream has been carrying the diagnostic since Sirach's composition; the King at Matt 10:22 names the same diagnostic at the gathering-mission-disciples level.

4444.new_note: *Saying, We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men: for as his majesty is, so is his mercy.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:18). *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28). Those who fear Yahuah (God), Sirach says, would rather fall into his hands than into the hands of men, because his mercy is as great as his majesty. Yahusha (Jesus) gives the twelve the same choice with the stakes spelled out: men can kill the body and no more, while Yahuah (God) is able to destroy both soul and body in hell, so fear him and not them. Both verses move the fear off men and onto Yahuah (God), and both find that the safer place. The one whose hands hold the final judgment is the same one whose mercy matches his majesty, which is why falling into his hands is the choice of the one who fears him.
4444.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 2:18 — *We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men.* The fear moved off men and onto Yahuah (God) at Matthew 10:28.
4444.old_note: *Saying, We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men: for as his majesty is, so is his mercy.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 2:18 names the wisdom-stream's direct fear-redirect architecture: the disciple who fears Yahuah (God) chooses to fall into HIS hands rather than into the hands of men. Matt 10:28's *fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in gehenna* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens level. The wisdom-stream had named the fear-of-Yahuah-supersedes-fear-of-men disposition; the King at Matt 10:28 names the same disposition with the eschatological-stakes made explicit.

4445.new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28). Men can kill the body. Wisdom says what they cannot touch: the souls of the righteous, which are in the hand of Yahuah (God). Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples the same thing before sending them out among wolves — do not fear the ones who can kill the body but cannot kill the soul. The persecutor's reach stops where the Father's hand begins. The righteous who died under the ungodly in Wisdom 2 were not lost; they were kept.
4445.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *there shall no torment touch them.* The persecutor kills the body but cannot kill the soul held in the Father's hand (Matthew 10:28).
4445.old_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the souls-of-the-righteous-in-Yahuah (God)'s-hand architecture: the souls of the righteous are in Yahuah (God)'s hand; no torment touches them. Matt 10:28's *fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens level — the persecutors can reach the body but cannot reach the soul, because the soul of the righteous is held in the Father's hand. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture; the King at Matt 10:28 names the operative-fact at the persecution-encounter.

4446.new_note: *And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:5). *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22). Wisdom calls the suffering of the righteous a proving: Yahuah (God) chastens a little, tests the metal, and finds them worthy of himself. Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples the same thing from the other side — you will be hated of all men for my name's sake, and the one who endures to the end will be saved. The hatred is the furnace; the enduring is what the furnace proves. The reward is great because the trial was real, and the Father is the one who did the proving.
4446.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:5 — *Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.* The proving is the hatred of all men; *he that endureth to the end shall be saved* (Matthew 10:22).
4446.old_note: *And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:5 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the suffering-as-proving-test: Yahuah (God) proves the righteous through chastisement and finds them worthy. Matt 10:22's endure-to-the-end perseverance-frame walks the same architecture: the persecution-chastisement is the proving-test; the disciple who endures is found worthy at the Father's recognition. The wisdom-stream's suffering-as-proving and the King's endure-to-be-saved name the same diagnostic from two angles.

4447.new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Wisdom looks to the day when the righteous man, whose labours his afflicters counted as nothing, stands in front of them in great boldness. The King gives his disciples the way into that day: confess him before men now, and he will confess them before the Father then. The confession is made in the face of the same people doing the afflicting, and the boldness Solomon saw is the boldness of the one being named by the Son in front of the Father while those who despised him look on.
4447.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The one who confesses the King before his afflicters (Matthew 10:32) is the one who stands in boldness before them on that day.
4447.old_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the vindication-of-the-righteous at the eschatological-judgment: the righteous man stands in great boldness before the face of those who afflicted him. Matt 10:32's *whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven* walks the same architecture at the apostolic-mission level: the lived-confession before the persecutors is recognized by the King at the Father's eschatological-judgment, and the persecutors who afflicted the confessor are themselves confronted at the same judgment. The wisdom-stream had named the vindication-pattern; the King at Matt 10:32 names the operative-confession that leads into it.

4458.new_note: *Then I answered and said, How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?* (2 Esdras 4:33). *And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?* (Matthew 11:3). Esdras, shown the end and the threshing, asks the question anyone in distress asks: how, and when, and why are our years few and evil. John, in Herod's prison, sends to ask Yahusha (Jesus), art thou he that should come, or do we look for another. John had preached the axe at the root and the fan in the hand, and the fire had not fallen while he sat in chains. Neither question is unbelief. Both are the faithful asking the one who knows the times why the times are not yet what he said they would be.
4458.member_note: 2 Esdras 4:33 — *How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?.* John's question from prison (Matthew 11:3) is the same question from the same distress.
4458.old_note: *Then I answered and said, How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:33 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the prophet's-question-from-distress about the timing-of-the-end. Matt 11:3's *art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?* walks the same architecture at the prison-of-the-forerunner level. Yochanan (John) had preached the prophetic-compression of the kingdom-at-hand AND the dreadful-day-of-Yahuah (the LORD) as one motion (Matt 3:7-12's axe-at-the-root / unquenchable-fire); the motion has not landed the way he proclaimed it; the question is the gap becoming visible. The wisdom-stream had named the prophet's-question-about-timing pattern; Yochanan (John) at Matt 11:3 walks the same legitimate-clarification-seek under the inaugurated-but-not-yet tension.

4459.new_note: *And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him, for you have much exceeded.* (2 Esdras 4:34). *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.* (Matthew 11:6). The angel's answer to Esdras is not a date; it is, do not hasten above the Most High, the times are his and your hurry cannot move them. The King's answer to John is not a date either; after naming the works being done he adds, blessed is he who is not offended in me. Both answers ask the same thing of the one waiting: that he not stumble over the gap between what was promised and what he can see from where he sits. The blessing is on the one who trusts the timing of Yahuah (God) when the timing is the hardest part.
4459.member_note: 2 Esdras 4:34 — *Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him.* Blessed is he who is not offended in the waiting (Matthew 11:6).
4459.old_note: *And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him, for you have much exceeded.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:34 names the wisdom-stream's direct angelic-answer to the prophet's timing-question: do not hasten above the Most High; the timing is his. Matt 11:6's *blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me* names the same disposition at the kingdom-citizens level — the blessing on the one who holds the credential, trusts the timeline, and does not fall away in the gap between the inaugurated-and-not-yet-consummated. The wisdom-stream had named the disposition the angel commended; the King at Matt 11:6 names it at the apostolic-mission level.

4460.new_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.* (Matthew 11:6). The righteous dead ask from their chambers how long they must hope this way. John saw the same souls under the altar asking how long, O Yahuah (Lord), and they were told to rest a little while longer (Revelation 6:9–11). The King's word to John the Baptist in his prison is the word for everyone who waits: blessed is he who is not offended in me. The dead wait in their chambers, the living wait in their chains, and the blessing is on both for not letting the length of the wait turn into offense at the one who set its length.
4460.member_note: 2 Esdras 4:35 — *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers.* The one who waits without being offended is blessed (Matthew 11:6).
4460.old_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:35 names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the souls-of-the-righteous-in-their-chambers-asking-how-long. The framework reads the verse against Revelation 6:9-11's *souls under the altar* crying *how long, O Yahuah (Lord)?* — the same pattern at the New Testament restatement. Matt 11:6's blessing on the one who is not offended walks the same architecture: the disposition that endures the timing-gap without falling away is the disposition the wisdom-stream had named, the disposition Revelation 6 names again, and the disposition the King commends at Matt 11:6.

4464.new_note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:10). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). When Yahusha (Jesus) says John is the Elias who was to come, he is pointing at a job description everyone in the crowd knew. Sirach had written it out: Elijah is ordained to reprove, to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob. All of Jacob, all twelve tribes, the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah) together. John began that work at the Jordan; the full restoring of the tribes waits on the great and dreadful day Malachi set it beside (Malachi 4:5). *If ye will receive it* is the hard part, because receiving it means receiving that the gathering of a scattered people is what Elijah comes to do.
4464.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to restore the tribes of Jacob.* Yahusha (Jesus) names John as Elias at Matthew 11:14, and Sirach says what Elijah comes to do: restore the tribes of Jacob, all twelve.
4464.old_note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:10 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the Eliyahu-pattern: ordained-for-reproofs, pacify-the-wrath-of-judgment, turn-the-heart-of-the-father-to-the-son, AND *restore the tribes of Jacob* — the twelve-tribe-gathering substance the framework's Red Line #11 names as the destination of the gathering-of-the-scattered-seed. Matt 11:14's *if ye will receive it, this is Eliyahu (Elijah), which was for to come* identifies Yochanan (John) as the Eliyahu-pattern fulfillment; Sirach 48:10 names the same Eliyahu-pattern at the wisdom-stream register, with the *restore the tribes of Jacob* clause locking the twelve-tribe-restoration architecture as integral to the Eliyahu-mission. The framework reads Yochanan (John) as the inaugural-Eliyahu-pattern-fulfillment; the dreadful-day-of-Yahuah (the LORD) full-restoration-of-the-tribes-of-Jacob is reserved for the second-coming.

4465.new_note: *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* (1 Maccabees 2:58). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). Mattathias remembers Elijah (Elias) for one thing: he was zealous and fervent for the law, and he was taken up into heaven. That is how the faithful in Yashar'el (Israel) remembered him, as the man who stood for the commandments of Yahuah (God) against a kingdom that had traded them for Baal. When Yahusha (Jesus) says of John, this is Elijah (Elias) which was for to come, the likeness is that same zeal: John in the wilderness calling the leadership a generation of vipers, John in prison for telling Herod his marriage was unlawful. Elijah's zeal for the law is what Malachi promised would come before the great day, and it came first in John.
4465.member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:58 — *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* John came in that same zeal; this is Elias which was for to come (Matthew 11:14).
4465.old_note: *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* 1 Maccabees 2:58 names the wisdom-stream's witness to the Eliyahu-zealous-for-the-Torah architecture: Eliyahu's zeal for the Torah is what the wisdom-stream remembers as the operative-substance of his mission. Matt 11:14's Eliyahu-pattern-identification of Yochanan (John) walks the same architecture — Yochanan (John) was the wilderness-camel-hair Nazirite-disciplined prophet whose zeal for the Father's-ways called the Pharisees and Sadducees *generation of vipers* (Matt 3:7) and whose imprisonment came from his public-condemnation of Herod Antipas's adultery (Matt 14:3-4). The wisdom-stream had named the Eliyahu-zealous-for-Torah disposition; the inaugural-Eliyahu-fulfillment in Yochanan (John) walks the same disposition at the messenger-before-the-King's-face register.

4469.new_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The system faulted John for fasting and Yahusha (Jesus) for eating, which tells you the complaints were not the reason. Wisdom of Solomon gave the reason long before: the righteous one is clean contrary to our doings and upbraids us with our offending the law, so let us lie in wait for him. The glutton and winebibber charge is a cover for the grievance the ungodly admit among themselves, that his life exposes their departure from the Torah. *Wisdom is justified of her children* because wisdom's own book had already written the accusers' script.
4469.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* The contradictory complaints of Matthew 11:19 hide the real grievance Wisdom 2:12 names: the righteous one reproves their lawbreaking.
4469.old_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 names the wisdom-stream's direct prophecy of the system's-rejection-of-the-righteous-one architecture: let-us-lie-in-wait, because-he-upbraids-us-with-our-offending-the-law. The framework reads the verse as the prophetic-pre-figuration of the Pharisaic-system's rejection of both Yochanan (John) and Yahusha (Jesus) at Matt 11:18-19. The system's opposite-direction-complaints (Yochanan-too-austere; Yahusha-friend-of-publicans) are cover-stories over the prior decision Wisdom 2 had named in advance — the righteous-one who reproves with the Torah is intolerable to a system invested in its own departure from it.

4470.new_note: *He is grievous to us even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:15). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The ungodly in Wisdom cannot even stand to look at the righteous man, because his life is cut to another pattern than theirs. That is the complaint behind the slander in Matthew: the Son of Adam sat at table with publicans and sinners, and the religious system of his day could only read a life of another fashion as gluttony and drunkenness. The charge changes its words from one age to the next, but it is the same offense — a righteous life reproves the ones watching it, and they answer by calling it unrighteous. Wisdom is justified of her children all the same.
4470.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 — *his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* The life of another fashion is what the slander of Matthew 11:19 was aimed at — a glutton and winebibber for sitting with sinners.
4470.old_note: *He is grievous to us even to behold: for his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the system's-aesthetic-rejection of the righteous-one: his-life-is-not-like-other-men's, his-ways-of-another-fashion. The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream pre-figuration of the *gluttonous-man, winebibber, friend-of-publicans-and-sinners* slander at Matt 11:19 — the system's moral-character-attack on the King for the table-fellowship-with-sinners (Matt 9:10-13) is the operative-form of the system's-aesthetic-rejection Wisdom 2:15 had named. The system's register-of-rejection changes; the architecture does not.

4471.new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The ungodly in Wisdom finish where they were always headed: condemn him to a shameful death. In Matthew 11 they are only at the beginning — calling him a glutton and a winebibber for sitting with sinners. The road runs from there to Matthew 12, where his works are credited to Beelzebub, and on to the trial and the cross in Matthew 26 and 27. A system that cannot deny what it sees moves from slander to false accusation to execution. Wisdom had named the end of that road before the gospel showed its first step.
4471.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* The end of the road whose first step is the slander of Matthew 11:19.
4471.old_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 names the wisdom-stream's direct prophecy of the system's-condemnation-of-the-righteous-one to a shameful death — the verbal-anchor for the trajectory the Matt 11:19 slander-escalation points toward (the Matt 12:24 Beelzebul-attribution, the Matt 26-27 cross-trial-and-execution). Matt 11:19's slander is the inaugural-form of the architecture Wisdom 2:20 had named at its full terminus: the system that cannot deny the visible-fact moves through slander, moves through false-attribution, moves toward condemnation to a shameful death. The wisdom-stream had named the full architecture; Matt 11:19 names the early-step.

4472.new_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Wisdom calls out: come to me, all you who desire me, and fill yourselves with my fruits. Yahusha (Jesus) came eating and drinking, and the ones who came to him were the publicans and the sinners, while the system called him a glutton and a winebibber — and then he says wisdom is justified of her children. The children of wisdom are the ones who heard the call and came to be filled. The invitation Sirach wrote down is the one the Son of Adam spoke in Galilee, and his table was where the filling happened.
4472.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me.* Wisdom's invitation; *wisdom is justified of her children* who came (Matthew 11:19).
4472.old_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:19 names the wisdom-stream's direct *come-unto-me* invitation-substance: wisdom-as-feminine-figure-of-the-Tanakh's personification-tradition calling all-the-desirous to come and be filled.
