Matt 11:19's *wisdom is justified of her children* closing (the inverse-of-the-system's-rejection naming the kingdom-citizens-whose-ears-the-Father-has-opened-recognize-the-substance) walks the same wisdom-personification-tradition. The wisdom-stream had named wisdom's come-unto-me invitation; Matt 11:19 names the children-of-wisdom who responded.

4473.new_note: *He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* (Baruch 3:36). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Baruch says the whole way of knowledge was found out by Elohim (God) and then given, not to the world at large but to Jacob his servant and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved. Wisdom has a people she was given to. Yahusha (Jesus), reproached for eating with publicans and sinners, says wisdom is justified of her children: the ones who recognize her are her own. The children of wisdom in Matthew 11 are the covenant seed Baruch names, the people the knowledge was given to, and when the one who gave it stood among them in flesh they knew his voice even when the leaders did not. Her children are the proof she was given to Jacob.
4473.member_note: Baruch 3:36 — *has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* Wisdom's children at Matthew 11:19 are the people she was given to.
4473.old_note: *He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* Baruch 3:36 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-given-to-Yashar'el (Israel) architecture: Yahuah (God) found-out the way of knowledge and gave it to Ya'aqov (Jacob) his servant and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved. The framework reads the verse against Red Line #11's scattered-seed-covenant-substance: the wisdom-given is given to the covenant-seed; the wisdom-children at Matt 11:19 are the kingdom-citizens-whose-ears-the-Father-has-opened — the covenant-seed responding to the wisdom-given. Matt 11:19's wisdom-justified-of-her-children walks the same architecture: the wisdom-given to Ya'aqov (Jacob)-and-Yashar'el (Israel) at Baruch 3:36 is the substance the kingdom-citizens-of-wisdom recognize.

4474.new_note: *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* (Baruch 4:1). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Baruch names what the wisdom given to Jacob is: the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), the law that endures for ever, which gives life to those who keep it and death to those who leave it. Wisdom is not a mood or a philosophy; she is the Torah. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says wisdom is justified of her children, her children are the ones who keep the commandments. John says the same thing from the other side: *He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him* (1 John 2:4). The law that endureth for ever has not been set aside by the one who spoke it at Sinai and walked in Galilee; wisdom's children are known by keeping it.
4474.member_note: Baruch 4:1 — *the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life.* Wisdom is the Torah; her children keep it (Matthew 11:19).
4474.old_note: *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* Baruch 4:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct identification of the wisdom-given-to-Yashar'el (Israel) as *the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever.* The framework reads the verse as a load-bearing wisdom-stream anchor against the institutional-Christian antinomian-reading of the New Testament: the wisdom-given is the Torah; the Torah endures forever; those who keep it come to life; those who leave it die. Matt 11:19's *wisdom is justified of her children* names the kingdom-citizens-who-keep-the-commandments-of-Yahuah (God) — the same body the 1 John 2:3-4 *keep-his-commandments-or-the-truth-is-not-in-him* filter identifies.

4475.new_note: *Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:5). *Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.* (Matthew 11:21). A sharp judgment belongs to those in high places. Chorazin and Bethsaida were set in a high place: the mighty works were done in their streets, and they did not repent. Tyre and Sidon, cities the prophets thundered against, would have been in sackcloth long ago if they had seen the same works. The more that is shown to a city or a man, the sharper the reckoning, and Solomon had written that rule before the King applied it to the towns he had been healing in.
4475.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 — *a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* Chorazin and Bethsaida (Matthew 11:21) saw the mighty works and did not repent; the more shown, the sharper the judgment.
4475.old_note: *Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the graduated-judgment-of-the-credentialed: a sharp judgment to those in high places. Matt 11:21-22's *more tolerable for Tyre and Tsidon (Sidon) at the day of judgment, than for you* names the same graduated-judgment-architecture at the cities-that-saw-the-credential register. The wisdom-stream had named the principle: position-of-credential-or-authority brings sharper-judgment than position-without. The King at Matt 11:21-22 names the operative-application: the Galilean-cities-of-the-credentialing bear sharper-judgment than Tyre and Tsidon (Sidon) of the prophetic-indictments.

4476.new_note: *For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:6). *But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.* (Matthew 11:22). Mercy soon pardons the lowly; the mighty are mightily tormented. The King says it over the towns that saw his works: more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment than for you. The judgment is real and it has degrees. Those who were shown little answer for little; those who were shown the kingdom working in their own streets answer for that. It is not one flat torment for everyone and it is not nothing; it is weighed.
4476.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 — *mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* More tolerable for Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 11:22): the judgment is real and weighed by what each was shown.
4476.old_note: *For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the graduated-accountability-by-degree-of-credentialing: mercy soon-pardons-the-meanest; the mighty are mightily-tormented. The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream anchor of the *more tolerable for Sodom* / *more tolerable for Tyre and Tsidon (Sidon)* architecture the King names at Matt 11:22 + 11:24. The judgment is real; the degrees are real; the degree-graduation by credentialing-density is the operative-fact the wisdom-stream had named and the King now names at the apostolic-mission level. The framework's reading rules out both the inherited eternal-conscious-torment monolith and the universalism-flatten — the day-of-judgment is real with real-graduated-degrees.

4477.new_note: *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:8). *And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* (Matthew 11:23). A sore trial comes upon the mighty. Capernaum was mighty in the one way that counts in this chapter: it was exalted unto heaven, the King's own city where he lived and healed and taught. The sore trial for a city like that is to be brought down to hell, the grave, the place of the dead, lower than Sodom. The hell here is the pit the city goes down into, not the endless fire the pulpit reads into the word. Sodom would have stood if it had seen what Capernaum saw.
4477.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 — *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* Capernaum, exalted unto heaven and brought down to the grave (Matthew 11:23), is the mighty under the sore trial.
4477.old_note: *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the sore-trial-upon-the-mighty: the credentialed-and-the-mighty face the sore-trial. Matt 11:23's *thou, Kfar-Nachum (Capernaum), which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell* names the operative-application: Kfar-Nachum (Capernaum) the *exalted-unto-heaven* (the King's ministry-base, the Matt 9:1 *his own city,* the home-base of the gathering-mission) is the *mighty* upon whom the sore-trial falls. The wisdom-stream had named the principle; the King at Matt 11:23 names the cities under it. The *hell* (*hadēs* / *Sheol*, the underworld-of-the-dead) is the eschatological-judgment-station, not the inherited Christian eternal-conscious-torment overlay.

4480.new_note: *Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:7). *But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.* (Matthew 11:24). The waste land still smoking, the fruit that never ripens, the pillar of salt standing as a monument of an unbelieving soul: Sodom was still preaching in Solomon's day. The King uses that monument as the floor. If the works done in Capernaum had been done in Sodom, Sodom would still be standing, and so it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for the town that saw the kingdom at work in its own streets and did not turn. The smoking land is the witness against the unbelieving soul; the city with the mighty works has a sharper witness against it.
4480.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 — *a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* Sodom, the standing monument of unbelief, is the floor the King measures Capernaum against (Matthew 11:24).
4480.old_note: *Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Sodom-judgment as enduring-monument: the smoking-waste-land, the plants-bearing-fruit-that-never-come-to-ripeness, the standing-pillar-of-salt as monument-of-an-unbelieving-soul. The framework reads the verse against Matt 11:24's *more tolerable for the land of Sodom* — Sodom is the enduring-monument the King invokes as the floor against which the Galilean-cities-of-the-credentialing are weighed. The wisdom-stream had named Sodom as the abiding-witness-to-judgment; the King at Matt 11:24 deploys the architecture to locate the cities-that-saw-the-credential at the sharper-judgment-end of the graduated-accountability-scale.

4485.new_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Sirach says favour before Yahuah (God) runs toward the one who humbles himself, and the greater he is, the lower he should go. Yahusha (Jesus) thanks the Father for the same thing working: these things hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. The wise and prudent are the ones who did not humble themselves, who came to the Father with their standing in hand, and the revelation went past them to the ones with nothing to defend. Sirach names the principle; the prayer in Matthew 11 shows it happening.
4485.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:18 — *The greater you are, the more humble thyself.* Revealed unto babes, hidden from the wise and prudent (Matthew 11:25).
4485.old_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:18 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the greatness-through-humility architecture: the greater-one humbles himself; favour comes through the humbling. The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream Tanakh-anchor of Matt 11:25's revelation-economy logic: the Father reveals to the babes because the babes hold the disposition the wisdom-stream had named — humility before Yahuah (God). The system's wise-and-prudent operate the inverse — credential-elevation rather than self-humbling — and the revelation-channel does not reach them. The wisdom-stream named the principle; the King at Matt 11:25 names the operative-fact.

4486.new_note: *Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed to the meek.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:19). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Sirach says it as plainly as it can be said: many are in high place and of renown, but mysteries are revealed to the meek. Yahusha (Jesus) prays the same pairing to the Father, hidden from the wise and prudent, revealed unto babes. The meek in Sirach and the babes in Matthew are the same people, the ones with nothing to defend when the Father speaks, and the high and renowned are the same people as the wise and prudent, the ones whose standing fills the space where the hearing would be. The two verses line up in their shape, high against low, hidden against revealed, and they name one rule of how Yahuah (God) gives understanding.
4486.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:19 — *mysteries are revealed to the meek.* Hid from the wise and prudent, revealed unto babes (Matthew 11:25).
4486.old_note: *Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed to the meek.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:19 names THE direct verbal-anchor for Matt 11:25 at the extras-tier: *mysteries are revealed to the meek* — the precise inverse-pair the King names at Matt 11:25 (*hid from the wise and prudent, revealed unto babes*). The wisdom-stream had named the architecture at one of its strongest direct verbal-formulations; the King at Matt 11:25 prays the same architecture into his disciples' hearing. The *meek* of Sirach 3:19 and the *babes* (*nēpioi*) of Matt 11:25 are the same body: the *poor in spirit* of Matt 5:3, the *anawim*-disposition that has nothing to defend against the Father's-call. The wisdom-stream and the King name one diagnostic at one register.

4487.new_note: *Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:7). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Solomon prayed, and understanding was given him; he called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came. The King thanks the Father that these things were hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. The two agree on where understanding comes from: it is given. Solomon asked and it was given him; the babes had nothing in hand and it was revealed to them; the wise and prudent, sure they already had it, were passed over.
4487.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 — *I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* Understanding is given to the one who prays; the Father reveals to babes what the wise cannot reach (Matthew 11:25).
4487.old_note: *Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the prayer-as-the-channel-of-the-Spirit-of-wisdom: understanding is given to the one-who-prays; the spirit-of-wisdom comes to the one-who-calls-upon-Yahuah (God). Matt 11:25-27's Father-Son revelation-economy walks the same architecture: the Son addresses the Father (*I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth*) and the Father's sovereign-revelation flows. The wisdom-stream had named the prayer-channel for the Spirit-of-wisdom; the King at Matt 11:25-27 names the prayer-channel for the Father-Son revelation-economy substance itself.

4488.new_note: *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:23). *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28). Sirach ends his book with an invitation: draw near, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning. Yahusha (Jesus) issues the same one, come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden. Sirach was pointing people toward Wisdom; the one who speaks in Matthew is the Wisdom who stood beside the Maker before the world was (Ecclesiasticus 24:9; Proverbs 8:22–30), now speaking in his own voice. The load his hearers carried was the burden the scribes bound on them, *heavy burdens and grievous to be borne* (Matthew 23:4), not the Torah itself. The rest he offers is in the house of learning, not outside it.
4488.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 51:23 — *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* Sirach's closing invitation is the one Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 11:28; come near, and find the rest in the house of learning.
4488.old_note: *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51:23 names the wisdom-stream's direct *come-unto-me* invitation-substance: draw-near, you-unlearned, dwell-in-the-house-of-learning. Matt 11:28's *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden* walks the same invitation-substance at the kingdom-King's register. The wisdom-stream wisdom-figure's invitation to the unlearned is the typological-anchor of the King's invitation to the labour-and-heavy-laden — the same body (those-bearing-the-Pharisaic-oral-tradition-burden of Matt 23:4's *they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne*) the King now invites to come.

4489.new_note: *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:26). *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.* (Matthew 11:29). Sirach's yoke is instruction, and he tells the soul to receive it, so the rest he found was not rest from the yoke but rest under it. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same thing in the same order: take my yoke, learn of me, and you will find rest for your souls. He is quoting Jeremiah, *ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls* (Jeremiah 6:16). His yoke is not the absence of a yoke; it is the old path, his Father's commandments as he teaches and walks them, set in place of the heavy burdens the scribes had bound on men's shoulders (Matthew 23:4). Sirach put his neck under it and called it rest.
4489.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 51:26 — *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction.* The yoke is the instruction and the rest is found under it, not away from it; Matthew 11:29 says take my yoke, learn of me.
4489.old_note: *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51:26 names THE strongest extras-tier verbal-anchor in the entire Hebrew library for Matt 11:29's *take my yoke upon you, and learn of me.* The wisdom-stream's wisdom-figure issues the same yoke-invitation Yahusha (Jesus) issues at Matt 11:29: put-your-neck-under-the-yoke, let-your-soul-receive-instruction. The framework's reading of Matt 11:29 as exchange-the-Pharisaic-burden-yoke-for-the-King's-rest-yoke (NOT yoke-vs-no-yoke) is anchored at the wisdom-stream-register here. The wisdom-figure of Sirach 51 had named the come-unto-me / put-your-neck-under-the-yoke / receive-instruction architecture; the King at Matt 11:29 walks the same architecture as the Word-made-flesh issuing the invitation in person.

4490.new_note: *Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:27). *For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.* (Matthew 11:30). Sirach is not theorizing; he points to his own life and says look, little labour, much rest, and his neck is still under the yoke when he says it. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same of his yoke: easy, and the burden light. Neither man is describing a life without commandments. Moses said the commandment *is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off* (Deuteronomy 30:11), and John says *his commandments are not grievous* (1 John 5:3). The heavy thing was never the Torah; it was what men added to it, and the one who gave it carries it lightly.
4490.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 51:27 — *I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* Sirach's little labour and much rest under the yoke is Matthew 11:30, my yoke is easy and my burden is light.
4490.old_note: *Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51:27 names THE direct verbal-anchor for Matt 11:30's *for my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.* The wisdom-stream's wisdom-figure names the operative-fact: little-labour, much-rest under the yoke-of-wisdom. Matt 11:30's easy-yoke / light-burden walks the identical wisdom-stream architecture. The framework reads the verse-pair (Sirach 51:26-27 + Matt 11:29-30) as one architecture across the two registers: the wisdom-stream wisdom-yoke and the King's heart-Torah-yoke are the same yoke-substance, and the rest-promised under both is the rest-of-walking-in-the-good-way the prophet at Jeremiah 6:16 had named.

4491.new_note: *For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:28). *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.* (Matthew 11:29). Sirach's sixth chapter is about putting the neck under wisdom's yoke; her fetters look like bondage at first, and at the last you find her rest, and the rest is turned to joy. Yahusha (Jesus) offers his yoke in the same words: take it, learn of me, and ye shall find rest unto your souls. The yoke is not the opposite of the rest; it is the road to it, in Sirach and in the Messiah alike. The pulpit offers a rest with no yoke in it, and the other side of the aisle calls the yoke a burden; both have lost what Sirach and the Messiah say in the same breath, that the rest is found at the end of wearing it.
4491.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 6:28 — *at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* The rest found under the yoke at Matthew 11:29.
4491.old_note: *For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 6:28 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-yoke-leading-to-rest-and-joy architecture in the second Sirach yoke-passage (Sirach 6:24-31): the yoke-of-wisdom looks like fetters and chains initially (vv.24-25), but at-the-last yields rest-turned-to-joy. The framework reads the verse against Matt 11:29's *ye shall find rest unto your souls* — the rest-substance the King promises is the rest-substance the wisdom-stream had named at Sirach 6:28, and the journey from yoke-acceptance to rest-found walks the same shape: acceptance, instruction, the substance at-the-last yielding rest-turned-to-joy. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture twice (Sirach 6:24-31 + 51:23-27); the King at Matt 11:29 walks both witnesses simultaneously.

4492.new_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28). Wisdom has been calling this way all through Ecclesiasticus, and here she says it outright: come to me, all of you who want me, and be filled. When Yahusha (Jesus) stood in Galilee and said *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*, it was not a new voice. It was the same one, the Wisdom who sat beside the Maker in Ecclesiasticus 24, now speaking in flesh, and the ones he calls are the ones Sirach's Wisdom had already called, the weary who want her and have not yet been fed.
4492.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* The same call Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 11:28, *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*; Wisdom speaking before she came in flesh.
4492.old_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:19 names the wisdom-stream's third major *come-unto-me* invitation-passage (after Sirach 6 and 51): the wisdom-figure issues the universal-invitation *come to me, all you that be desirous of me.* Matt 11:28's *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden* walks the same universal-invitation-architecture at the King's register, with the labour-and-heavy-laden specifying the audience-shape the wisdom-stream's *all you that be desirous* shares. The wisdom-stream wisdom-figure issued the come-unto-me invitation three times in Sirach (chapters 6, 24, 51); the King in Matt 11:28 issues the same invitation as the Word-made-flesh.

4495.new_note: *At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brothers that were murdered in the secret places.* (1 Maccabees 2:41). *How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.* (Matthew 12:12). After a thousand of their brothers were slaughtered in the caves rather than lift a hand on the sabbath, Mattathias and his men decreed that they would fight whoever came against them on that day. They were not setting the sabbath aside; they were refusing to let the heathen use the sabbath to root the people who kept it out of the earth. Yahusha (Jesus) makes the same judgment when he asks whether a man is worth more than a sheep pulled from a pit on the sabbath and answers that it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. The sabbath was given for life; to preserve life on it is to keep it, not to break it.
4495.member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:41 — *Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him.* Preserving life on the sabbath is doing well on it (Matthew 12:12).
4495.old_note: *Then said they every one to his neighbour: If we all do as our brethren have done, and fight not for our lives and laws against the heathen, they will now quickly root us out of the earth. At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whosoever shall come to make battle with us on the Shabbat day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brethren that were murdered in the secret places.* 1 Maccabees 2:41 names the Maccabean Shabbat-defense decision — the wisdom-stream's direct documentation that life-saving-overrides-Shabbat-restriction was the operative-principle in the Second-Temple period. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:11-12: the King's *kal vachomer* argument (sheep-rescue-on-Shabbat is permitted in the Pharisaic tradition; how much more a man?) walks the same architecture the Hasmonean decision had locked under threat of extinction. The wisdom-stream had named the principle; the King at Matt 12:12 names the operative-substance: the Shabbat is FOR life and rest and doing-well, not for the fence-architecture that obstructs the same.

4496.new_note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:1). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Sirach says keeping the law is bringing offerings enough, and heeding the commandment is itself a peace offering. Yahusha (Jesus) quotes Hosea, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, against men who condemned the guiltless for picking grain on the Sabbath. Nothing in either verse loosens the Sabbath or the altar. What both say is that the man who holds the form of the commandment while condemning the hungry has not kept the commandment at all, and his sacrifice counts for nothing, while the one who shows mercy has brought the offering.
4496.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:1 — *he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.* Heeding the commandment is the offering; mercy over sacrifice at Matthew 12:7.
4496.old_note: *He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the mercy-substance-IS-the-true-sacrifice architecture: the keeping-of-the-law brings offerings enough; the heeding-of-the-commandment offers the peace offering. The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream restatement of Hosea 6:6's *I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings* — the same architecture Yahusha (Jesus) cites at Matt 12:7 (the second Hosea 6:6 citation in Matthew, after Matt 9:13). The Pharisaic-counterfeit-righteousness fails at the same diagnostic the wisdom-stream had named: external-credential-architecture without internal-mercy-substance is not the offering Yahuah (God) desires.

4497.new_note: *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:18). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Sirach says the offering of a thing wrongfully gotten is laughable before Yahuah (God), and the gifts of unjust men are not received. Yahusha (Jesus) told the Pharisees that if they had understood I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, they would not have condemned his hungry disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath. Both lines say the same thing about the altar: it does not wash the hands that bring to it. A sacrifice offered while mercy is withheld from the guiltless is the unjust man's gift, and Yahuah (God) does not take it.
4497.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 34:18 — *the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.* Sacrifice while condemning the guiltless (Matthew 12:7) is the gift Yahuah (God) does not take.
4497.old_note: *If a man offereth a sacrifice of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous, and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 34:18 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the heart-substance-required-for-the-sacrifice-to-be-accepted architecture: a sacrifice without the heart-substance is rejected. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:7's *if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless* — the Pharisees who condemned the disciples for the Shabbat-plucking operated the credential-without-substance pattern Sirach 34:18 had diagnosed: the credentialing-form (Shabbat-fence-adherence) without the mercy-substance is the rejected-offering at the wisdom-stream register.

4498.new_note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* (Tobit 4:10). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Tobit gives mercy its full weight: alms deliver from death and keep a man from the darkness. Mercy is not the soft side of the Torah, something to be set aside when the rules get strict. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same to the Pharisees on the Sabbath: if you had known what Hosea meant by mercy and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless. The system that condemned hungry disciples had lost the thing Tobit's household had kept, and the King names the loss in Hosea's own words.
4498.member_note: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Mercy carries eternal weight; the Sabbath condemnation showed a system that had lost it (Matthew 12:7).
4498.old_note: *For alms doth deliver from death, and shall not suffer thee to come into darkness.* Tobit 4:10 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the mercy-as-substance-with-eternal-weight architecture: alms (the operative-form of the mercy-substance) deliver from death. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:7's deployment of Hosea 6:6 in the Shabbat-controversy: the mercy-substance is not a soft-side of the Torah; it is the operative-substance with eternal-weight the wisdom-stream had named explicitly. The King at Matt 12:7 names the same operative-substance the wisdom-stream had named — and the Pharisaic-condemnation of the disciples reveals the system's loss of the substance the wisdom-stream had preserved.

4499.new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). The council that went out to plan his destruction was the system rendering its verdict on the righteous man. It had started by faulting his disciples, moved to calling him a drunkard and a friend of sinners, and now it was planning his death. Wisdom had already written the end of that story: the one the system condemned stands in great boldness before the faces of those who condemned him. The third day was the first installment of that standing, and the day of judgment is the rest of it, when the verdict rendered in this age is reversed in front of the men who rendered it.
4499.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The council to destroy him (Matthew 12:14) is the verdict this age renders; the day of judgment reverses it in front of them.
4499.old_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the eschatological-reversal-of-the-righteous-condemned architecture: the righteous-one whom the system condemned stands at the day-of-judgment in great-boldness before those-who-afflicted-him. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:14's Pharisaic-council-to-destroy-the-King: the system's trajectory from challenging the disciples (Matt 9:11) to slandering the King (Matt 11:18-19) to plotting destruction (Matt 12:14) is the operative-form of the architecture Wisdom 5:1 had named at the eschatological-end-point register. The day-of-judgment reverses the verdict the system rendered in the present age. The King at Matt 12:14 walks toward the cross under the same architecture Wisdom 5 had named at the wisdom-stream register; the resurrection is the operative-vindication.

4500.new_note: *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour:* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:4). *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). The men who held a council to destroy him accounted his life madness; before long they will say he casts out devils by Beelzebub. Wisdom puts their own confession in their mouths at the judgment: we fools, we accounted his life madness and his end without honour. The council of Matthew 12:14 is the first step of that story, and the verse that follows in Wisdom is its last, when they see him numbered among the children of Yahuah (God). The same reversal waits for everyone the system counts a fool for walking in his commandments now.
4500.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:4 — *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour.* The council to destroy him (Matthew 12:14) is the judgment of fools that the day of judgment turns into their own confession.
4500.old_note: *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of Elohim (God), and his lot is among the saints!* Wisdom of Solomon 5:4-5 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the system's-belated-recognition-of-the-righteous-one architecture: the same system that accounted his life madness and his end without honour recognizes at the day-of-judgment that he is numbered among the children-of-Elohim (God). The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:14's council-to-destroy: the Pharisees who plot the King's destruction will at the day-of-judgment recognize the substance Wisdom 5:4-5 had named — the same architecture operates against the heart-Torah-walking kingdom-citizens of the present age, with the same eschatological-reversal awaiting.

4505.new_note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:1). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach tells his son not to defraud the poor and not to make the needy eyes wait long; the next line adds not to make a hungry soul sorrowful or provoke a man in his distress. That is a description of handling the bruised reed without breaking it and the smoking flax without quenching it, which is what Isaiah said of the Messiah and what Matthew says Yahusha (Jesus) fulfilled. The disposition Sirach asks of a son is the disposition the Son carried. A system that sorts the bruised and the smoldering into categories and dismisses them has lost both the counsel and the Messiah who kept it.
4505.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 4:1 — *defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.* The bruised reed not broken at Matthew 12:20, asked of the son first.
4505.old_note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long. Make not an hungry soul sorrowful; neither provoke a man in his distress.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 4:1-2 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the bruised-reed-not-broken-and-smoking-flax-not-quenched mercy-substance: the wisdom-stream commands against making-the-needy-wait, against the hungry-soul-sorrowful, against provoking-the-man-in-distress. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:20: *a bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench.* The mercy-substance the prophet names of the King is the same substance the wisdom-stream named as the disposition required of the kingdom-citizens. The Pharisaic-system's pattern of categorical-classification-and-dismissal of the bruised and the smoking inverts both the wisdom-stream-disposition and the King's-disposition; the King restores; the system breaks-and-snuffs.

4506.new_note: *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:4). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach is describing a face that stays turned toward the one in need, and Matthew 12:20 describes the Messiah's: a bruised reed he will not break, smoking flax he will not quench. The supplication of the afflicted is the bruised reed, and the poor man at the door is the smoking flax, easy to snap and easy to snuff. What Sirach asked of every son of Yashar'el (Israel), Yahusha (Jesus) did. A religious system that turns its face from the afflicted has abandoned the counsel and parted ways with the Messiah in the same motion.
4506.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 4:4 — *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.* The face the Messiah keeps toward the bruised reed at Matthew 12:20.
4506.old_note: *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away thy face from a poor man. Turn not away thine eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse thee.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 4:4-5 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the kingdom-citizens' compassion-disposition: do not reject-the-supplication, do not turn-the-face-away, do not turn-the-eye-from-the-needy. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:20's bruised-reed-mercy substance: the disposition of the King walks the wisdom-stream-disposition the Pharisaic-system had abandoned through the categorical-classification-and-dismissal pattern. The wisdom-stream and the gospel name one disposition at two registers.

4507.new_note: *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint. Do not the tears run down the widow’s cheeks? and is not her cry against him that causeth them to fall?* (Ecclesiasticus 35:14–15). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach says Yahuah (God) does not despise the fatherless when they plead or the widow when she pours out her complaint. Matthew is quoting Isaiah about the servant who will not break a bruised reed or put out a smoking wick, and he says it of Yahusha (Jesus) in the same chapter where the Pharisees are plotting to destroy him. The ones who cause the tears and the one who hears them stand side by side. The widow's cry Sirach speaks of is heard by the same one who would not break a reed already bent.
4507.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:14 — *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow.* The bruised reed not broken (Matthew 12:20) is the same mercy toward the ones who cry.

4507.old_note: *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint. Do not the tears run down the widow's cheek? and is not her cry against him that causeth them to fall?* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:13-14 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the cry-of-the-bruised-heard-by-Yahuah (God) architecture: he-will-not-despise the supplication of the fatherless and the widow; the cry against the one who causes the tears reaches Yahuah (God). The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:20's bruised-reed-mercy substance: the wisdom-stream knew Yahuah (God) does not despise the bruised; the King at Matt 12:20 names the operative-disposition in his own ministry. The Pharisaic-system's plot at v.14 is precisely the act-causing-the-tears the wisdom-stream had named; the King's mercy-substance at v.20 is the operative-opposite-disposition.

4513.new_note: *But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* (Wisdom of Solomon 12:10). *And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.* (Matthew 12:32). Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on the Canaanites little by little and gave them place of repentance, knowing all the while that their malice was bred in them and their cogitation would never be changed; the next verse calls them a cursed seed from the beginning. The King speaks of a sin that will not be forgiven in this world or the one to come, the word spoken against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by men who had just watched the Spirit cast out devils and called it Beelzebub. Both passages describe a disposition that does not change: room to repent is given, and the heart that was never going to turn uses the room to harden. He said of such hearers that they believe not because they are not of his sheep (John 10:26).
4513.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 — *their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* The cogitation that would never be changed is the heart behind the word against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) that is not forgiven (Matthew 12:32).
4513.old_note: *But executing thy judgments upon them by little and little, thou gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the architecture-of-the-hardened-disposition that-will-never-be-changed: Yahuah (God) gives place of repentance, not being ignorant of the bred-in malice and the cogitation that will never change. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:31-32's blasphemy-against-the-Ruach: the wisdom-stream knew the hardened-disposition that will never change as a possibility-of-the-heart; the King at Matt 12:31-32 names the architecture's consequence — the blasphemy of those whose cogitation has hardened against the credentialing they have seen will not be forgiven, because the disposition itself is the hardening-against-repentance the wisdom-stream had named.

4514.new_note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:6). *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.* (Matthew 12:34). Sirach puts the two halves side by side: the fruit shows how the tree was kept, and what a man says shows the conceit of his heart. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same two things in one breath to the Pharisees, that a tree is known by its fruit and that the mouth speaks out of the abundance of the heart. Words are fruit. Bad fruit means a bad tree, and bad speech means a bad heart, and no amount of religious credential changes what the mouth gives away.
4514.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* Words as the fruit of the heart; *out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh* (Matthew 12:34).
4514.old_note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:6 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for Matt 12:33-35's tree-known-by-its-fruit / out-of-the-abundance-of-the-heart-the-mouth-speaketh architecture: the fruit-declares-the-tree's-dressing; the utterance-declares-the-heart's-conceit. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture in precisely the substance the King walks at Matt 12:33-35. *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh* (Matt 12:34) names the same diagnostic Sirach 27:6 had named: words-are-fruit-of-the-heart; bad-fruit-reveals-bad-heart-substance.

4515.new_note: *Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:7). *But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.* (Matthew 12:36). Sirach says a man is tried when he speaks, so hear him before you praise him. Yahusha (Jesus) carries the same trial all the way to the end: every idle word men speak will be given account of in the day of judgment. What Sirach says a wise listener does now, the Judge will do then. The words are the evidence of the heart, and the heart is what the judgment weighs.
4515.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 27:7 — *Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.* Speech as the trial of a man; at Matthew 12:36 that trial reaches the day of judgment, where *every idle word* is given account of.
4515.old_note: *Praise no man before thou hearest him speak; for this is the trial of men.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:7 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of speech-as-the-trial-of-men architecture: hear-the-man-speak-first-because-this-is-the-trial. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:36's *every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment* — the day-of-judgment is the cosmic-version of the wisdom-stream's speech-as-trial architecture: the words-spoken are the evidence-of-the-heart-substance the judgment will weigh.

4516.new_note: *Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:11). *But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.* (Matthew 12:36). Wisdom of Solomon says no word is so secret that it goes for nothing, and that a lying mouth kills the soul that owns it. Yahusha (Jesus) says every idle word will be accounted for in the day of judgment, and the next verse says what the accounting looks like: *by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned* (Matthew 12:37). Murmuring and backbiting feel like small, private sins. Both books say there is nothing private about them; the ear of jealousy hears everything, and the words are kept for the day.
4516.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought.* No word goes for nothing; Matthew 12:36 says every idle word is accounted for in the day of judgment.
4516.old_note: *Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the no-word-goes-for-nought-and-the-mouth-that-belieth-slays-the-soul architecture: words have eternal-weight at the wisdom-stream register; the lying mouth slays the soul. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:36's *every idle word ... give account thereof in the day of judgment*: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture the King names at the day-of-judgment register. *By thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned* (Matt 12:37) walks the same architecture: words-as-evidence-of-the-heart-substance the day-of-judgment will weigh.

4517.new_note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). *For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40). The Father holds both doors: he leads down to the gates of hell and he brings up again. Yahusha (Jesus) gave that generation one sign, the sign of Jonah — three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, and then up. The resurrection was not a new idea arriving in Galilee; the library already knew that the one who has power of life and death brings up from the grave, and the King walked that road in his own body so the sign would stand in front of everyone.
4517.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The sign of Jonah walks that road: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, then up (Matthew 12:40).
4517.old_note: *For thou hast power of life and death: thou leadest to the gates of Sheol, and bringest up again.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the gates-of-Sheol-and-bring-up-again architecture: Yahuah (God) has the power of life and death; he leads to the gates of Sheol AND brings up again. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:40's *so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth* — the sign-of-Yonah's three-days-three-nights-in-the-heart-of-the-earth is the operative-application of the architecture Wisdom 16:13 had named: descent-to-Sheol-and-bring-up-again. The wisdom-stream knew Yahuah (God) brings up from Sheol; the King's resurrection is the credentialing-event the typology pre-announces.

4520.new_note: *O you Adam, what have you done? for though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.* (2 Esdras 7:48). *Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.* (Matthew 12:45). Ezra cries out to Adam that his fall did not stay with him; everyone who comes of him fell with him, carrying the grain of evil seed sown in Adam's heart from the beginning (2 Esdras 4:30). Yahusha (Jesus) describes a house swept clean of its unclean spirit but left empty, so that the spirit returns with seven worse and the last state is worse than the first. A son of Adam cleaned out but not given a new heart is that empty house; the inherited pattern comes back to fill what was only swept. The remedy is not a cleaner house but a different heart in it (Ezekiel 36:26).
4520.member_note: 2 Esdras 7:48 — *though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.* The swept but empty house of Matthew 12:45 is a son of Adam without a new heart.
4520.old_note: *O Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee. For what doth this also profit, that we should now be promised an immortal time, whereas we have done the works that bring death?* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7:48 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Adam-introduced-the-evil-heart-and-the-children-inherit-it architecture: Adam's sin is not Adam's alone; the children-of-Adam inherit the operative-pattern. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:43-45's empty-house parable: the cleansed-house empty-of-the-new-heart is precisely the architecture 2 Esdras 7:48 had named — the children-of-Adam without the new-heart-cleansing carry the inherited-pattern that produces the empty-house-vulnerability. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture of the inherited-evil-heart; the King's empty-house parable names the architecture's operative-form at the deliverance-without-internal-replacement register.

4522.new_note: *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). The righteous one in Wisdom of Solomon calls himself the child of Yahuah (God), and two verses later the ungodly say why they believe him enough to hate him: his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion. Yahusha (Jesus) names the family of the Father the same way, whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother, sister, mother. The child of Yahuah (God) is known by a life that does the Father's will; that is how the Father's children are recognised. The ungodly recognised it too, and it was the recognising that made them lie in wait.
4522.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The child of Yahuah (God) is known by a life of another fashion; Matthew 12:50 says the same, whoever does the will of my Father.
4522.old_note: *He professeth to have the knowledge of Elohim (God): and he calleth himself the child of Yahuah (the Lord). He was made to reprove our thoughts. He is grievous unto us even to behold: for his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:13-15 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the child-of-Elohim-by-the-righteous-disposition architecture: the righteous-one calls-himself-the-child-of-Yahuah (the Lord) by his life-of-another-fashion (the heart-Torah-walking life). The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:50's *whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother* — the kingdom-family-recognition-criterion is the same doing-the-Father's-will substance the wisdom-stream had named as the operative-form of the child-of-Yahuah (the Lord) identity. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture; the King at Matt 12:50 names the kingdom-family substance.

4523.new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). The ungodly have a test for who is the son of Yahuah (God): will the Father step in and deliver him? Yahusha (Jesus) gives the Father's own test for who belongs to his family: whoever does the will of my Father in heaven. One measures sonship by rescue, the other by obedience. Wisdom shows the just man already living by the second standard before the first is ever applied to him, and that is exactly why his life was grievous to them.
4523.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* The ungodly test sonship by rescue; Yahusha (Jesus) marks his family by doing the Father's will (Matthew 12:50).
4523.old_note: *For if the just man be the son of Elohim (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the son-of-Elohim-tested-by-deliverance architecture: the just-man's son-of-Elohim-identity is to be tested by whether Yahuah (God) helps him. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:50's kingdom-family-recognition-criterion: the doing-the-Father's-will substance is the operative-identity-marker — the system's test (Wisdom 2:18) is whether Yahuah (God) delivers; the King's test (Matt 12:50) is whether the heart walks the will of the Father. The same architecture from both sides: the heart-Torah-walking-life IS the son-of-Elohim-identity-marker at both registers.

4524.new_note: *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:10). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). Sirach says the man who fathers the fatherless and stands in for the widow's husband shall be as the son of the Most High, loved by him more than a mother loves. Yahusha (Jesus) says whoever does the will of his Father is his brother, sister, and mother. In both, the family of Elohim (God) is known by the doing of the Father's will, which in Sirach's example is the Torah's own care for the orphan and widow. The doing does not manufacture the sonship; it shows it, the way a son is known by bearing his father's likeness, and that is why Yahusha (Jesus) names his kin by it.
4524.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 4:10 — *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother.* The doing of the Father's will by which the family is known at Matthew 12:50.
4524.reason: Theology adjustment: the old note read the doing as what 'makes' the doer a son of the Most High; rewritten so the doing reveals the family rather than creates it (hearing/doing reveals what was already true).
4524.old_note: *Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother: so shalt thou be as the son of the most High, and he shall love thee more than thy mother doth.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 4:10 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the doing-the-Father's-substance-makes-thee-a-son-of-the-Most-High architecture: the disposition-of-fathering-the-fatherless and being-a-husband-to-their-mother makes the doer the son-of-the-Most-High. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:50: the kingdom-family-recognition-criterion is the same doing-the-Father's-will substance the wisdom-stream had named as the operative-form of the son-of-the-Most-High identity. The wisdom-stream and the gospel name one architecture across two registers — the kingdom-family is identified by the heart-Torah-walking-disposition the wisdom-stream had named, the kingdom-entry-criterion at Matt 7:21 had named, and the 1 John 2:3-4 master-filter restates.

4527.new_note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber, And shall be sought of many, and yet not be found: then shall unrighteousness and incontinency be multiplied upon earth.* (2 Esdras 5:9–10). *He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.* (Matthew 13:11). Esdras is shown a day when understanding withdraws into its secret chamber and is sought by many and not found. The King tells his disciples why he speaks in parables: to you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom, to them it is not given. Understanding does not vanish from the earth; it withdraws from those who would not have it and is given to those who hear. The many who seek and do not find in Esdras are the ones who, in Matthew, hear and do not understand, because what is withdrawn from one is a gift to the other, and the hearing reveals which is which.
4527.member_note: 2 Esdras 5:9 — *then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber.* To some it is given to know the mysteries; to others it is not (Matthew 13:11).
4527.old_note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber, And shall be sought of many, and yet not be found: then shall unrighteousness and incontinency be multiplied upon earth.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 5:9-10 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-and-understanding-withdrawing-into-the-secret-chamber architecture: in the latter-days the understanding withdraws-itself and shall-be-sought-of-many-and-not-be-found. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:11-17's cause-and-effect-of-hearing diagnostic: the understanding the multitudes seek-from-the-parables withdraws from the system-rejecting-disposition; the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-withdrawal-from-the-disposition-that-rejects. The disciples-receive the mysteries-of-the-kingdom because the disposition-to-receive operates; the system-rejecting-disposition encounters the withdrawn-understanding.

4528.new_note: *For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject to sin.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:4). *Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.* (Matthew 13:13). Wisdom will not move into a soul that is set against her. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks in parables for the same reason he gives in the next lines, quoting Isaiah: *this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed* (Matthew 13:15). The parable did not shut them out; the closed eyes were their own doing, and wisdom does not force the door. In the same breath he tells the disciples their eyes are blessed because they see (Matthew 13:16). The teaching was one teaching; what differed was the soul it met.
4528.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 — *into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter.* Wisdom does not enter a soul set against her; at Matthew 13:13 the parables meet eyes that have closed themselves.
4528.old_note: *For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject unto sin.* Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the wisdom-shall-not-enter-into-a-malicious-soul architecture: wisdom does-not-enter the malicious-soul; the disposition determines the entry. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:13-15's Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 6:9-10 citation: the people's-heart has waxed-gross because they-have-closed-their-own-eyes; the wisdom does not enter the disposition-that-closes. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture-of-the-soul-that-refuses-wisdom; Matt 13:13-15 names the operative-form at the Pharisaic-system-rejecting-the-King register. The Father does not actively-prevent the hearing; the disposition closes itself; the wisdom encounters-the-closure.

4529.new_note: *When the great Yahuah (God) will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks to Yahuah (God) in his prayer.* (Ecclesiasticus 39:6). *But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.* (Matthew 13:16). Sirach says the scribe is filled with the spirit of understanding when the great Yahuah (God) wills it; the man does not work it up out of his own study, he is filled. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples their eyes and ears are blessed, and the verse before explains why: *it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom* (Matthew 13:11). The seeing and the hearing are given the same way the scribe's understanding is given. The hand that fills the scribe is the hand that opens the disciple's eyes, and both of them answer with thanks.
4529.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 39:6 — *he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences.* Understanding is given when Yahuah (God) wills; the blessed eyes and ears of Matthew 13:16 are given the same way.
4529.old_note: *When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks unto the Lord in his prayer.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 39:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the spirit-of-understanding-poured-out-on-the-elect-scribe architecture: when-the-great-Yahuah-wills, the scribe shall-be-filled-with-the-spirit-of-understanding. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:16-17's *blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.* The disciples' blessing-of-seeing-and-hearing operates in the same architecture the wisdom-stream had named — the spirit-of-understanding poured-out by Yahuah (the Lord) on the elect-disciples. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture; Matt 13:16-17 names the operative-blessing at the apostolic-circle.

4532.new_note: *For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?* (2 Esdras 4:30). *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24). Uriel says a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, that it has brought up ungodliness ever since, and that it will go on bearing until the time of threshing. Yahusha (Jesus) opens his parable with a man sowing good seed in his field, and the verses that follow tell of the enemy's seed and the harvest when the two are separated. Esdras and the King both speak of seed, of two kinds of seed in one ground, and of a threshing that ends the matter. The evil seed is not the last word in either book; the threshing is.
4532.member_note: 2 Esdras 4:30 — *the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning.* The parable of the good seed sown in the field (Matthew 13:24) runs to the same threshing.
4532.old_note: *For the grain of evil seed hath been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness hath it brought up unto this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing shall come?* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:30 names THE direct wisdom-stream parallel to the wheat-and-tares architecture at the heart-of-Adam register: the grain-of-evil-seed has been-sown-in-the-heart-of-Adam-from-the-beginning, AND the ungodliness it has produced continues-to-grow-until-the-time-of-threshing. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:24-30's *the kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-evil-seed-sown-from-the-beginning AND the time-of-threshing-when-the-sorting-occurs; the King at Matt 13:24-30 names the operative-parable-form. The framework reads the architecture in continuity: the watchers' incursion at Bereshit (Genesis) 6:1-4 + the dragon's corruption-of-the-line at Bereshit 3 + the seed-of-evil-sown-from-the-beginning at 4 Ezra 4:30 + the King's tares-sown-by-the-enemy at Matt 13:24-30 = one architecture across the canon and the wisdom-stream.

4533.new_note: *For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.* (2 Esdras 3:21). *But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.* (Matthew 13:25). Esdras says the first Adam bore a wicked heart, transgressed, and was overcome, and so are all who are born of him. The parable says that while men slept an enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat. These are two different facts about one field. The sons of Adam carry the wicked heart, and the law was given to bring fruit out of them in spite of it; the tares are another seed, planted by an enemy, not born of Adam at all. The wheat is wounded, the tares are not wheat, and the harvest will tell them apart.
4533.member_note: 2 Esdras 3:21 — *the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome.* The field of Adam's sons is where the enemy sowed tares while men slept (Matthew 13:25).
4533.reason: Kept the old note's line between the wicked heart inherited by Adam's sons (the wheat) and the tares the enemy sowed (a different seed); wrote it plainly so the two are not collapsed.
4533.old_note: *For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him. Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law also in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 3:21-22 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wicked-heart-inherited-from-Adam architecture: the first-Adam bore the wicked-heart; all-who-are-born-of-him inherit the operative-pattern. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:25's *while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares.* The wisdom-stream had named the inherited-wicked-heart as the architecture-the-tares-grow-in; the King's parable names the operative-form of the enemy-sowing-while-the-watchful-guard-fails. The framework reads the architecture WITHOUT collapsing into the Augustinian-original-sin doctrine in its Christian-developed form: the framework preserves the actor's-disposition (the watchful-guard-fails; *while men slept*) without erasing the actor's-responsibility; the wisdom-stream knew the inherited-heart-architecture without the Christian-doctrinal-overlay.

4534.new_note: *O Yahuah (God), if you suffer not your servant, that we may pray before you, and you give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it; how shall each man live that is corrupt, who bears the place of a man?* (2 Esdras 8:6). *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24). Ezra prays for seed to the heart and culture to the understanding, so that fruit may come, because a corrupt man cannot live any other way. The kingdom parable answers that prayer with a sower: a man goes out and sows good seed in his field. The seed to the heart Ezra begs for is what the sower is sowing; the fruit Ezra hopes for is what the good ground brings forth (Matthew 13:23). The prayer and the parable meet in the same field.
4534.member_note: 2 Esdras 8:6 — *give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it.* The sower of Matthew 13:24 is the answer to this prayer.
4534.old_note: *O Yahuah (Lord) that bearest rule, of every spirit that liveth, give us seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it; whereby every one shall live that is corrupt, who beareth the place of a man.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 8:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the prayer-for-seed-unto-the-heart architecture: Yahuah (Lord) is asked-for-seed-unto-the-heart and culture-to-the-understanding so-that-fruit-may-come. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:24's *the kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field.* The wisdom-stream knew the architecture of seed-given-by-Yahuah (Lord) to the heart that fruit-may-come; the King at Matt 13:24 names the operative-parable-form of the Sower-of-the-good-seed. The framework reads the architecture in continuity: the prayer of 4 Ezra 8:6 (give-us-seed-unto-our-heart) is the disposition the good-ground-soil at Matt 13:23 carries; the Sower's sowing IS the answer to the wisdom-stream's prayer.

4543.new_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.* (Matthew 13:43). Wisdom puts the shining of the righteous at a set time — the time of their visitation — and sets it in a harvest scene: sparks running among the stubble. Yahusha (Jesus) puts it at the same moment in the parable of the tares: when the field is reaped and the tares are bundled for the fire, then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun. The stubble burning and the sparks flying are the same picture as the tares burning and the wheat shining. The shining is not yet; it waits on the harvest.
4543.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 — *in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* The harvest scene of Matthew 13:43 — tares to the fire, *then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun.*
4543.old_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the righteous-shall-shine-at-the-time-of-their-visitation architecture: the souls-of-the-righteous shall-shine and run-like-sparks-among-the-stubble at the time-of-their-visitation. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:43: the visitation-of-the-righteous at the wisdom-stream register is the same eschatological-vindication the King names at the wheat-and-tares-interpretation register. The sparks-among-the-stubble carries the harvest-and-burning imagery directly — the same harvest the King's parable names, with the righteous-shining-as-sparks-among-the-burning-tares.

4546.new_note: *As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:22). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.* (Matthew 13:35). Solomon promises to tell what wisdom is and how she came up, to hide no mysteries, to trace her from the beginning of her nativity and bring the knowledge of her into light. The King opens his mouth in parables to utter things kept secret from the foundation of the world. Both are teachers who refuse to pass over the truth; both are bringing into the light what had been hidden, and the parables, which the crowd heard as stories, were that light being given to the disciples who asked what they meant.
4546.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 — *I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you.* Things kept secret from the foundation of the world uttered in parables (Matthew 13:35) is the same refusal to hide mysteries.
4546.old_note: *As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you; but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth.* Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the I-will-not-hide-mysteries-from-you architecture: the wisdom-stream's teacher commits to bring-the-knowledge-into-light and not-pass-over-the-truth. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:35's *I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world*: the wisdom-stream's commitment-to-reveal-the-mysteries operates in the same register the King's parables-method enacts. The mysteries-kept-secret-from-the-foundation revealed-now to the disciples is the operative-form of the architecture the wisdom-stream had named at its teacher-register.

4547.new_note: *And the men that are received shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth: and the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning.* (2 Esdras 6:26). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.* (Matthew 13:35). Among the tokens of the end Ezra is told that the heart of the inhabitants will be changed and turned into another meaning, and that men who have not tasted death will see it. When Yahusha (Jesus) teaches in parables he is uttering what had been kept secret from the foundation of the world, and a parable only opens to a heart that has been turned toward its meaning; to everyone else it stays a story about seed and soil. Ezra goes on to hear that the truth so long without fruit shall be declared (2 Esdras 6:28). The parables are that declaring begun, and the changed heart is the one that hears them.
4547.member_note: 2 Esdras 6:26 — *the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning.* The parables of Matthew 13:35 open what was kept secret to a heart turned toward their meaning.
