4547.reason: The old note quoted 2 Esdras 6:26–28 and leaned on v.28 ('the truth, which hath been so long without fruit, shall be declared'), which is not in this packet. I rebuilt on the live 6:26 (the changed heart) and mentioned v.28 in prose. The author may prefer this card to sit at 6:28.
4547.old_note: *And the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning. For evil shall be put out, and deceit shall be quenched. As for the faith, it shall flourish; corruption shall be overcome, and the truth, which hath been so long without fruit, shall be declared.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 6:26-28 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the truth-which-hath-been-so-long-without-fruit-shall-be-declared architecture: the latter-days will see the long-hidden-truth declared-at-last. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:35: the wisdom-stream knew the architecture-of-the-truth-revealed-after-long-hiddenness; the King's parables-method names the operative-form of the architecture the wisdom-stream had named. The truth-without-fruit-for-a-long-time = the substance-kept-secret-from-the-foundation-of-the-world; the declared-at-last = the King's-revealing-through-the-parables.

4548.new_note: *Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?* (Ecclesiasticus 20:30). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.* (Matthew 13:44). Sirach asks what good hidden wisdom or hoarded treasure does anyone — none, until it is found and brought out. Yahusha (Jesus) tells of treasure hidden in a field, and of the man who finds it and sells everything he has to buy the field, because treasure found is worth all of it. The man who buys the field is the one who paid the whole price: the Father, through the Son, finding his own scattered through the field of the world and giving everything to obtain them. The point Sirach made holds either way — hidden treasure profits no one until someone finds it, and finding it is worth everything.
4548.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 20:30 — *Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both.* The treasure hid in the field is found and bought with everything (Matthew 13:44).
4548.reason: Kept the old note's reading of the man who buys the field as the Father through the Son paying the whole price for the scattered seed hidden in the field of the world; stated plainly, not as settled. Author may want to check it.
4548.old_note: *Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 20:30 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-that-is-hid-and-treasure-that-is-hoarded-up architecture: the hidden-treasure has no profit-to-those-who-do-not-find-and-obtain-it. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:44's *the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field*: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the hidden-treasure-and-the-finding-and-obtaining; the King names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register. The framework's reading per the Father-Son-buyer-finds-the-treasure substance (per Red Line #11): the Father / the Son is the One-who-finds-the-hidden-treasure (the elect scattered through the field-of-the-world) and pays-the-full-price-to-obtain. The Tanakh-substance and the wisdom-stream-substance and the King's-parable-substance all carry the architecture.

4549.new_note: *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:14). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:* (Matthew 13:45). Sirach says a faithful friend is a treasure, and the next verse says nothing countervails him; there is no price you could set against him. Yahusha (Jesus) says the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking goodly pearls who finds one worth everything he owns and sells all to have it. The merchant is Yahuah (God), and the pearl is the seed of promise — always the few, scattered like gold through the dust of the earth, and worth to him everything he has. Sirach knew that kind of worth in a friend; the Father knows it in his own, and when he finds them he does not haggle.
4549.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 6:14 — *he that has found such an one has found a treasure.* The one pearl worth all the merchant had, Matthew 13:45.
4549.reason: Left out the old note's identification of the merchant as the Father/Son buying the elect; that reading is not in the voice skill spine I was given, so the card keeps only the incomparable-worth connection. Author may want it restored. Yoshi (Oct 23): the treasure/pearl is the seed of promise, the buyer is Yahuah — aligned with 4548.
4549.old_note: *A faithful friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure. Nothing doth countervail a faithful friend, and his excellency is invaluable.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 6:14-15 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the finding-a-faithful-friend-is-finding-a-treasure-nothing-countervails architecture: the supreme-worth substance of the faithful-friend is incomparable; nothing equals it. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:45-46's *the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.* The wisdom-stream knew the architecture-of-the-finding-of-the-incomparable-worth; the King names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register. The pearl-of-great-price = the elect (per the framework's preferred Father-Son-buyer reading) AS the supreme-worth substance the buyer pays-all-to-obtain.

4550.new_note: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:8). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:* (Matthew 13:45). A king with a sceptre and a throne in hand says he preferred wisdom before both of them and counted riches nothing beside her. The merchant in the parable does the same arithmetic over one pearl: he sells all he has to get it. That merchant is Yahuah (God), and the pearl of great price is the seed of promise, the few he has always called his treasure, found scattered in the nations like gold in the dust of the earth. Solomon weighed sceptres against wisdom and they came up light; the Father weighs everything against his own and pays it all.
4550.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:8 — *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.* The merchant who sells all for one pearl (Matthew 13:45) is doing Solomon's arithmetic: sceptres and riches are nothing beside wisdom.
4550.reason: Old note identified the buyer of the pearl as the Father or Son who pays all to obtain, citing an internal file (short.md). I could not verify that reading in the skill, so the rebuilt note keeps the plain comparison (king prefers wisdom / merchant sells all) and does not name who the buyer is. Author may want the buyer identification restored if it is settled teaching. Yoshi (Oct 23): the treasure/pearl is the seed of promise, the buyer is Yahuah — aligned with 4548.
4550.old_note: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her. Neither compared I unto her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.* Wisdom of Solomon 7:8-9 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-preferred-above-sceptres-and-thrones architecture: wisdom is preferred-above-rule and esteemed-above-riches-and-precious-stones; the precious-stones are little-sand and silver-is-clay before the supreme-worth of wisdom. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:45-46's pearl-of-great-price: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-supreme-worth-preferred-above-all-else at the wisdom-register; the King names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register. The buyer (per the framework's preferred reading at short.md) is the One-who-prefers-the-pearl-above-all-else and pays-the-full-price-to-obtain.

4551.new_note: *For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God), being commended for the gifts that come from learning.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:14). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.* (Matthew 13:44). Wisdom is a treasure to men that never fails, and those who use her become the friends of Yahuah (God). The King says the kingdom of heaven is like treasure hid in a field, found by a man who hides it again, sells all he has for joy, and buys the field. The man who buys the field is Yahuah (God), and the treasure hid in it is the seed of promise, the few scattered through the field of the world like gold in the dust of the earth; he gives everything to have the field so that he has them. The one who learns wisdom becomes his friend; the one he buys the field for was his treasure before anyone dug.
4551.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 — *she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God).* The treasure hid in a field worth selling all for (Matthew 13:44) is the treasure that never fails and makes friends of Yahuah (God).
4551.reason: Old note's buyer reading (Father or Son as the one who finds and pays all) rested on an internal reference I could not confirm in the skill; the rebuilt note leaves the buyer unnamed and keeps the treasure comparison. Yoshi (Oct 23): the treasure/pearl is the seed of promise, the buyer is Yahuah — aligned with 4548.
4551.old_note: *For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of Elohim (God), being commended for the gifts that come from learning.* Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-is-a-treasure-unto-men-that-never-faileth architecture: wisdom is the never-failing-treasure that makes-the-users-friends-of-Elohim (God). The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:44's treasure-hid-in-the-field: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-never-failing-treasure-of-wisdom; the King names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register. The treasure-hid-in-the-field is the substance-the-Father-Son-buyer-finds-and-pays-all-to-obtain (per the framework's preferred reading); the supreme-worth-of-the-treasure operates at the wisdom-stream-and-the-gospel registers together.

4553.new_note: *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:3). *So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,* (Matthew 13:49). Ezra is told that many are created but few saved, after the likeness of much clay and little gold (2 Esdras 8:2). Yahusha (Jesus) puts the sorting at the end of the world, when the angels sever the wicked from among the just as a net full of every kind is sorted on the shore. The net gathers all; the shore keeps few. The few saved are what remains when that severing is done.
4553.member_note: 2 Esdras 8:3 — *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* The angels sever the wicked from among the just at Matthew 13:49; the few are what remains.
4553.old_note: *Many be created, but few shall be saved.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 8:3 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the few-shall-be-saved architecture: many-be-created-but-few-shall-be-saved. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:49's severing-the-wicked-from-among-the-just at the dragnet-recapitulation register: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-few-saved-at-the-day-of-separation; the King names the operative-form at the dragnet-of-the-net-cast-into-the-sea-gathering-of-every-kind register. The framework reads the verse in continuity with the Matt 7:13-14 narrow-gate / few-find-it architecture: the wisdom-stream knew the substance the King names; the substance is the post-harvest-sifting per Red Line #11 operative at the eschatological-end-point.

4555.new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,* (Matthew 13:49). Wisdom says the righteous will judge the nations and have dominion over the people. Yahusha (Jesus) says what has to happen first: at the end of the age the angels come and sever the wicked from among the just. The sorting comes before the ruling. Once the wicked are taken out from among them, the just who are left are the ones Wisdom sees judging the nations — a kingdom of priests to the peoples left alive after that day, under an Elohim (God) who reigns for ever.
4555.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* After the angels sever the wicked from among the just (Matthew 13:49), the just are the ones who judge.
4555.old_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and Yahuah (their Lord) shall reign for ever.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the righteous-shall-judge-the-nations and have-dominion-over-the-people architecture at the eschatological-end-point. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:49's severing-the-wicked-from-among-the-just: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-righteous-judging-the-nations at the eschatological-judgment-and-millennial-reign register; the King's dragnet-parable lands the architecture at the present-chapter's recapitulation register. The framework reads the kingdom-of-priests destination-of-the-gathered-remnant per Red Line #7 in continuity: the righteous judge-and-rule the nations-left-after-the-judgment at the millennial-reign; the wisdom-stream and the gospel walk one architecture.

4556.new_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). *The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.* (Matthew 13:39). Wisdom names where death came from — the envy of the devil — and who finds it: they that hold of his side. Yahusha (Jesus) names the same enemy as the one who sowed the tares in the field, and in the verse before he calls the tares the children of the wicked one. The serpent in the garden, the watchers who corrupted the earth, the sower of tares in the field — it is one enemy doing one work across the whole story. Those who are of his side come to his end, because the seed shows at the harvest.
4556.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 — *through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side.* The enemy who sowed the tares (Matthew 13:39) is the one whose envy let death in.
4556.old_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the through-envy-of-the-devil-came-death-into-the-world architecture: the devil's envy is the source-of-death entering-the-world; they-that-hold-of-his-side find-death. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:39's *the enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-devil-as-source-of-death-in-the-world; the King names the operative-form at the wheat-and-tares-interpretation register. The framework reads the architecture in continuity: the devil's envy at Bereshit (Genesis) 3 (the serpent) + the devil's seduction at the watchers (1 Enoch 6-11) + the devil's sowing-of-tares at Matt 13:39 = one architecture of the source-of-death-and-corruption across the canon and the wisdom-stream. The they-that-hold-of-his-side find-death substance is the same architecture the children-of-the-wicked-one carry: paternal-source-determines-destination.

4559.new_note: *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:1). *For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.* (Matthew 14:3). Elijah's fire burned hottest at the king's court. He told Ahab to his face that the house of Ahab had forsaken the commandments of Yahuah (God), and Jezebel sought his life for it. John carried the same fire to Herod's court and said *it is not lawful for thee to have her* (Matthew 14:4), the Torah spoken against the king's own bed (Leviticus 18:16). Herod answered the prophet the way Ahab's house had answered Elijah: the king turned on him and a queen wanted him dead; this time the prophet was caught and bound. The word that burns like a lamp is not dimmed for royalty, and royalty does not forgive it.
4559.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:1 — *his word burned like a lamp.* Elijah's fire at Ahab's court is John's word to Herod at Matthew 14:3–4; the king answers the prophet by binding him.
4559.old_note: *Then stood up Eliyahu (Elias) the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-fiery-zeal-at-the-royal-court architecture: the prophet stood-up-as-fire and his word burned-like-a-lamp. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:3-4's *Herod had laid hold on Yochanan (John), and bound him ... For Yochanan (John) said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.* Yochanan (John)'s confrontation of Herod-Antipas at the Torah-violation operates in the same Eliyahu-pattern the wisdom-stream had named at the Achav (Ahab)-confrontation register. The Matt 11:14 identification of Yochanan (John) as *Eliyahu, which was for to come* is corroborated at the prophet's-zeal-and-Torah-confrontation pattern Sirach 48 walks. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture; Matt 14 names the operative-form at the gospel-level.

4560.new_note: *He brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:2). *For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.* (Matthew 14:3). Elijah's zeal against Ahab's idolatry shut up heaven; *there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word* (1 Kings 17:1), and the famine thinned the land. John's zeal against Herod's unlawful marriage brought no famine; it brought a prison cell and, before long, his head on a platter. The zeal is the same zeal, a prophet unwilling to let a king break the Torah in peace. Sirach records what it cost Ahab's people; Matthew records what it cost the prophet. Neither man softened the word to spare himself the consequences.
4560.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:2 — *by his zeal he diminished their number.* Elijah's zeal against Ahab's court brought famine; John's zeal against Herod's court brought his imprisonment at Matthew 14:3.
4560.old_note: *Who brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:2 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-zeal-bringing-judgment-on-the-Torah-violators substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:3-5's Yochanan (John)'s confrontation of Herod-Antipas's Torah-violation: the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-zeal at the Achav-Yezevel Torah-violation produced the famine-judgment (1 Melakhim (Kings) 17:1); Yochanan (John)'s-zeal at the Herod-Herodias Torah-violation produces the imprisonment-and-eventual-martyrdom. The Tanakh-pattern of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-confrontation-of-the-unrighteous-ruler the wisdom-stream had named the architecture for; Matt 14 names the operative-form at the second-coming-of-Eliyahu (the first-coming, preparing for the King's-first-arrival).

4561.new_note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:10). *And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.* (Matthew 14:5). Herod would have killed John and did not, because the people counted him a prophet. They were right, and more right than they knew. Sirach describes the prophet they were looking at: ordained for reproofs in his time, to hold back the wrath of judgment before it broke out, to turn the heart of the father to the son, to restore the tribes of Jacob. John reproved a king, called a nation to turn, and prepared the way for the one who gathers Jacob. Herod feared the crowd and not the Torah, and the crowd, for once, had the better instinct.
4561.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God).* The multitude at Matthew 14:5 counted John a prophet; Sirach describes which prophet, the Elijah ordained for reproofs and the restoring of Jacob.
4561.old_note: *Who wast ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of Yahuah (the Lord's) judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Ya'aqov (Jacob).* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:10 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the Malakhi (Malachi) 4:5-6 Eliyahu-promised-return substance: Eliyahu shall-be-ordained-for-reproofs and turn-the-heart-of-the-father-unto-the-son and restore-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob). The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:5's *they counted him as a prophet* — the Galilee-multitudes recognized Yochanan (John) as the Eliyahu-pattern-prophet the wisdom-stream had named the architecture for. The Matt 11:14 identification (*if ye will receive it, this is Eliyahu, which was for to come*) operates in the same architecture Sirach 48:10 had named. The framework reads the architecture in two-fold structure per voice-skill's eschatological-architecture: Yochanan (John) was the first-Eliyahu-coming preparing-the-way for the first-coming-of-the-King; the eschatological-second-Eliyahu (one of the two-witnesses of Revelation 11) will prepare for the second-coming. The restoration-of-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob) substance of Sirach 48:10 is the framework's scattered-seed-gathering-architecture the wisdom-stream knew.

4562.new_note: *Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:11). *And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Yahusha (Jesus).* (Matthew 14:12). Sirach blesses the ones who saw Elijah and then fell asleep in love, and gives the reason in one line: for we shall surely live. Death is a sleep for the righteous, and the sleeper will wake. John's disciples saw the Elijah of their day, and when Herod took his head they took up his body and buried him, and then they went and told Yahusha (Jesus). They carried the news of the prophet's death to the one who holds the life Sirach was sure of. They had seen Elijah, they buried him in love, and they walked straight to the resurrection.
4562.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:11 — *Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* John's disciples at Matthew 14:12 bury the Elijah of their day and go to Yahusha (Jesus), the one in whom we shall surely live.
4562.old_note: *Blessed are they that saw thee, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-disciples-blessed-in-the-prophet's-departure substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:12's *and his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Yahusha (Jesus).* The Eliyahu-pattern-prophet's-disciples honor the departing-prophet (Sirach 48:11 in the chariot-translation register; Yochanan (John)'s disciples at the burial-after-the-beheading) and walk-forward into the One the prophet prepared-the-way-for. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture of the prophet's-disciples-blessed-and-living-onward; Matt 14:12 names the operative-form at the gospel-pivot-from-Yochanan (John)-to-Yahusha (Jesus). The disciples' going-to-tell-Yahusha (Jesus) is the seed-war-pattern operating in the gathering-direction — Yochanan (John)'s-faithful-disciples drawn-into-the-King's-orbit.

4563.new_note: *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels’ bread.* (2 Esdras 1:19). *When Yahusha (Jesus) heard of it, he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard thereof, they followed him on foot out of the cities.* (Matthew 14:13). In 2 Esdras Yahuah (God) reminds the people that when they murmured in the wilderness he pitied them and fed them with manna, angels' bread. In Matthew the King goes by ship into a desert place and the people follow on foot out of the cities, and the verses that follow say he was moved with compassion and fed them there. The same pity, the same wilderness, the same bread given to a multitude that had nothing. The one who fed the fathers by the hand of Moses fed the children with his own hands by the sea of Galilee.
4563.member_note: 2 Esdras 1:19 — *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat.* The same pity fed the multitude in the desert place of Matthew 14:13.
4563.old_note: *I gave you angels' food to eat in your hunger; and when ye thirsted, I clave the rock, and waters flowed out to your fill.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 1:19 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father's-wilderness-feeding-of-the-multitude architecture: angels'-food in the hunger; water-from-the-rock in the thirst. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:13-14's King-withdrawing-into-the-desert-place and the multitudes-following-on-foot. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the Father's-wilderness-feeding through the Mosheh (Moses)-mediated-manna; the King at Matt 14:13-21 enacts the same architecture in person at the Galilee-desert-place. The Father's-wilderness-feeding-of-the-multitude operates across the canon and the wisdom-stream as one architecture; the King recapitulates the substance without mediation in the chapter's feeding-pericope.

4564.new_note: *Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20). *And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.* (Matthew 14:19). Bread from heaven, prepared without their labour, was how the Father fed his own people in the wilderness. On the grass in a desert place Yahusha (Jesus) looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks, and the loaves go out through the disciples' hands to a multitude that brought nothing but its hunger. The same hand that sent the manna is feeding Yashar'el (Israel) again, and John's account of this same meal ends with him saying who the bread is: *I am the bread of life* (John 6:35).
4564.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour.* Bread without labour again, blessed and broken in a desert place and handed out by the disciples (Matthew 14:19).
4564.old_note: *Instead whereof thou feddest thine own people with angels' food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the wilderness-manna substance: the Father fed-his-own-people with angels'-food sent-them-from-heaven bread-prepared-without-their-labour. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:19's King-taking-the-loaves-and-fishes and looking-up-to-heaven and blessing-and-breaking-and-distributing. The Father's-bread-from-heaven of Wisdom 16:20 is the substance the King enacts at the Galilee-desert-place — bread-prepared-without-their-labour multiplied for the multitudes, with the disciples-as-the-distribution-channel. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture; the King names the operative-form at the gospel-register; the John 6 *I am the bread of life* discourse following the Yochanan (John)-account of this same feeding-pericope (John 6:1-15 + 6:35) locks the substance: the King IS the bread-from-heaven the wisdom-stream had named the Father-feeding-his-people-with.

4565.new_note: *That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:26). *And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.* (Matthew 14:19). The manna was a lesson, and Wisdom of Solomon says what the lesson was: it is not the harvest that keeps a man alive but the word of Yahuah (God). When the King blesses five loaves and feeds a multitude, the loaves are the smaller thing; the disciples who hand them out have been receiving his word all along, and in John's telling of this same meal he says outright that his words are spirit and life (John 6:63). The bread points past itself to the word that preserves those who trust him.
4565.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word.* The loaves blessed and broken point past themselves to the word that nourishes (Matthew 14:19).
4565.old_note: *That thy children, O Yahuah (Lord), whom thou lovest, might know that it is not the growing of fruits that nourisheth man: but that it is thy word, which preserveth them that put their trust in thee.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the bread-of-life-is-the-Word-of-Yahuah substance: not-the-growing-of-fruits-nourisheth-man but-thy-Word-preserveth-them-that-trust. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:19's feeding-of-the-five-thousand and the Word-of-the-King the disciples have been receiving across the gospel. The wisdom-stream had named the substance the King anchors in the Yochanan (John) 6 account directly: *it is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life* (John 6:63). The feeding-substance points beyond-the-loaves to the Word-of-the-King the disciples are being trained to receive as the bread-from-heaven the wisdom-stream had named.

4566.new_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full.* (Matthew 14:20). Wisdom says come and fill yourselves with my fruits, and in the desert place Yahusha (Jesus) did exactly that: the multitude came to him, they ate, and they were filled. He is the Wisdom of Ecclesiasticus 24 feeding her children with her own hand, and the invitation of Matthew 11:28, *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*, is the same mouth speaking. Twelve baskets were left over, one for every tribe of Yashar'el (Israel), and the leftover says the feeding was never meant for that hillside alone. The scattered children of Wisdom will be gathered and fed the same way.
4566.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* In the desert place *they did all eat, and were filled* (Matthew 14:20); Wisdom feeding her children, with twelve baskets left for the twelve tribes.
4566.old_note: *Come unto me, all ye that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:19 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-feeding-her-children-with-her-fruits architecture: come-unto-me and fill-yourselves-with-my-fruits. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:20's *and they did all eat, and were filled.* The wisdom-stream knew the architecture of the wisdom-feeding-and-filling at the come-unto-me register; the King at Matt 14:20 enacts the operative-form at the Galilee-desert-place: the multitudes come; they eat; they are filled. The framework reads the Sirach 24:19 anchor in continuity with Matt 11:28's *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest* — the King's come-unto-me invitation across his ministry is the operative-form of the wisdom-stream's wisdom-inviting substance. The twelve-baskets-leftover of v.20 signal the twelve-tribes-restoration-architecture the wisdom-of-the-most-High had named as the destination-substance: the wisdom's-children gathered-and-fed in the wilderness.

4567.new_note: *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.* (Ecclesiasticus 43:23). *And in the fourth watch of the night Yahusha (Jesus) went unto them, walking on the sea.* (Matthew 14:25). Sirach praises the Maker who stills the deep by his counsel and sets islands in it, and Job says of the same one that he *alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea* (Job 9:8). In the fourth watch of the night the disciples watch a man do what Job said belongs to Elohim (God) alone. The one whose counsel appeases the deep is walking across it. The one who spoke the sea into its bounds came in flesh and treads on his own work.
4567.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 43:23 — *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.* The one who stills the deep by his counsel walks on it at Matthew 14:25; Job 9:8 said he alone treads upon the waves of the sea.
4567.old_note: *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands therein.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:23 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Creator's-appeasing-the-deep architecture: by-his-counsel he-appeaseth-the-deep. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:25's King-walking-on-the-sea in the fourth-watch. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-Creator's-mastery-of-the-deep at the counsel-and-appeasing register; the King enacts the operative-form by walking on the very-substance the Creator-masters. The Tanakh-direct-substance of Iyov (Job) 9:8 (*which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea*) names the action; the wisdom-stream's Sirach 43:23 names the authority-behind-the-action; the King at Matt 14:25 enacts both at once. The Formed-cloud-rider acts in the substance the Formless-Father's-counsel established.

4568.new_note: *For in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* (Ecclesiasticus 43:25). *And in the fourth watch of the night Yahusha (Jesus) went unto them, walking on the sea.* (Matthew 14:25). Sirach looks at the sea as a storehouse of the Creator's wonders, every beast and whale in it created, and in the next line he says *by his word all things consist* (Ecclesiasticus 43:26). The disciples saw a figure on the water and took it for a spirit. What they saw was the Creator of the sea walking on his own creation, and when he spoke he gave them his name, *it is I; be not afraid* (Matthew 14:27). The word that holds the sea together was the word speaking to them from on top of it.
4568.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 43:25 — *in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* The sea is the Creator's storehouse of wonders; at Matthew 14:25 the Creator walks on it and tells them, it is I.
4568.old_note: *For in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:25 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wonders-of-the-sea architecture: the sea-contains the strange-and-wondrous-works of the Creator. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:25-27's walking-on-the-sea in the fourth-watch with the *it is I* self-identification. The wisdom-stream had named the substance of the sea-as-the-Creator's-domain; the King at Matt 14:25 walks the sea AS the Creator-of-the-sea, with the *egō eimi* of v.27 naming the speaker as the One whose-counsel-appeases-the-deep at Sirach 43:23. The substance the wisdom-stream had named at the Creator-register operates in the King's-walking-and-naming at the gospel-register.

4569.new_note: *But your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves;* (Wisdom of Solomon 14:3). *And in the fourth watch of the night Yahusha (Jesus) went unto them, walking on the sea.* (Matthew 14:25). The Father has made a way in the sea and a safe path in the waves; the psalmist says the same, that his way is in the sea and his path in the great waters (Psalm 77:19). In the fourth watch the King walks that way, on the water, toward a boat full of men being tossed by it. The Formed one walks the path the Father's providence made, and when Peter steps out and sinks, the hand that catches him (Matthew 14:31) is the safe path in the waves Solomon prayed about. The way in the sea was never a figure of speech; a man walked it.
4569.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* The King walking on the sea in the fourth watch (Matthew 14:25) is walking the way the Father made in the sea.
4569.old_note: *But thy providence, O Father, governeth it: for thou hast made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father's-providence-governing-the-sea architecture: the Father's-providence governs-the-sea and makes-a-way-in-the-sea-and-a-safe-path-in-the-waves. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:25's King-walking-on-the-sea making-a-way-on-the-waves toward-the-disciples-in-the-tossed-ship. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the Father's-way-in-the-sea (echoing Tehillim (Psalm) 77:19 — *thy way is in the sea, and thy path in the great waters*); the King at Matt 14:25 enacts the operative-form of the same architecture. The Formed-Son walks the way the Formless-Father's-providence-makes-in-the-sea — and the King's catch-of-Kefa (Peter) at v.31 is the safe-path-in-the-waves the wisdom-stream had named the Father-providing-for-the-traveler.

4570.new_note: *Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction,* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:15). *But straightway Yahusha (Jesus) spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.* (Matthew 14:27). The almighty word leaped down from the throne into Egypt's night as a man of war. In the fourth watch of another night the disciples see a figure on the sea and are terrified, and the Word speaks: it is I; be not afraid. The one who came down from the Father's throne on Passover night is the same one walking the dark water, the Word who was with Elohim (God) and was made flesh (John 1:1, 14). Wisdom of Solomon shows the Word as one who comes down and acts; Matthew shows him in flesh naming himself.
4570.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 18:15 — *Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne.* The Word who came down on Passover night speaks across the dark water, *it is I; be not afraid* (Matthew 14:27).
4570.old_note: *Thine almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction.* Wisdom of Solomon 18:15 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the all-powerful-Word-leaping-down-from-heaven substance: thine-almighty-Word leaped-down-from-heaven out-of-thy-royal-throne. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:27's *be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid* — the King's *egō eimi* self-identification at the walking-on-the-sea moment. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the all-powerful-Word from-the-Father's-throne-coming-down-from-heaven; the Yochanan (John) 1:14 *the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us* names the substance-in-person; the King's *it is I* across the dark water at the fourth-watch is the operative-form of the Word-from-heaven the wisdom-stream had named. The Formed-Word that proceeded from the Formless-Father in the Wisdom 18:15 architecture is the speaker walking-on-the-water and naming-himself with the Ehyeh-substance of Shemot (Exodus) 3:14.

4571.new_note: *I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:3). *But straightway Yahusha (Jesus) spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.* (Matthew 14:27). Wisdom says she came out of the mouth of the Most High and covered the earth as a cloud. The one who came out of the Father's mouth is the Word the Father spoke — the Formed one beside the formless Maker — and the prophets knew him as the one who rides the clouds. On the water Yahusha (Jesus) says to the frightened men, it is I, the same words he uses when he says that before Abraham was, I am. The Wisdom that came out of the mouth of the Most High is the one walking on the sea, and he tells them not to be afraid.
4571.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:3 — *I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.* The Word from the Father's mouth is the one on the water saying *it is I* (Matthew 14:27).
4571.reason: Kept the old note's reading of Matthew 14:27's *it is I* as the Formed Wisdom of Ecclesiasticus 24 naming himself, with John 8:58 alongside. Live text reads *Most High* where the old note had *most High*.
4571.old_note: *I came out of the mouth of the most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:3 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Wisdom-proceeding-from-the-mouth-of-the-most-High architecture: came-out-of-the-mouth-of-the-most-High and covered-the-earth-as-a-cloud. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:27's *it is I* (*egō eimi*) — the King's self-naming with the Ehyeh-substance. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the Formed-substance proceeding from-the-mouth-of-the-Formless-most-High; the King at Matt 14:27 names-himself in the same substance the wisdom-stream had identified as the Wisdom-from-the-mouth-of-the-most-High. The framework reads this in continuity with the Yochanan (John) 8:58 *before Avraham (Abraham) was, I am* — the King's direct Ehyeh-substance self-identification operates in the architecture the wisdom-stream knew at the Wisdom-proceeding-from-the-Father register. The Formed-Word the Father spoke is the speaker on the water; the cloud-covering-the-earth substance is the cloud-rider Tanakh-substance the Tanakh-prophets had named.

4572.new_note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). *But straightway Yahusha (Jesus) spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.* (Matthew 14:27). Solomon prays to the Elohim (God) of his fathers who made all things with his word. John says the same of the Word: all things were made by him, and without him was not any thing made that was made (John 1:3). In the fourth watch the disciples see a figure walking on the sea and cry out, and he answers with the name the Formed one spoke from the bush: it is I, be not afraid. The one walking on the water is the Word the sea was made with, come in flesh and standing on his own handiwork. The Father made all things with his word; here the word is walking toward the boat.
4572.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *who have made all things with your word.* The Word all things were made with walks on the sea and says it is I (Matthew 14:27).
4572.old_note: *O Elohim (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (Lord) of mercy, who hast made all things with thy word.* Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father-made-all-things-with-his-Word architecture: the Father has-made-all-things-with-his-Word. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:27's *it is I* and the walking-on-the-sea moment of v.25. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the Word-as-the-Father's-agent-of-creation; the King at Matt 14:25-27 walks-on-the-sea (the creation-substance) AS the Word-through-whom-all-things-were-made (per Yochanan (John) 1:3 — *all things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made*). The framework reads the substance in continuity: the Father's-Word who made-all-things at Wisdom 9:1 + the Word-was-made-flesh at John 1:14 + the King-walking-on-the-sea-and-naming-himself-Ehyeh at Matt 14:25-27 = one architecture of the Formed-Word the Formless-Father expressed-from-the-beginning, now-walking-in-the-flesh on the sea his-own-Word-created.

4573.new_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.* (Matthew 14:3). John upbraided Herod with his offending the law, *it is not lawful for thee to have her* (Matthew 14:4), and Herod laid hold on him and bound him. That is Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 acted out at a king's court: the righteous one is clean contrary to what the king is doing, his word reproves the king's bed, and so the king and the woman lie in wait for him. The same reflex shows up wherever a righteous man reproves a system that has left the Torah, in the Pharisees who take counsel to destroy Yahusha (Jesus) (Matthew 12:14) and in the chief priests who do the same (Matthew 26:3–4). Herod is one more instance of a very old disposition.
4573.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* John upbraids Herod with the law at Matthew 14:3–4 and is bound for it, the ungodly lying in wait for the righteous.
4573.old_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the ungodly-determining-to-lie-in-wait-for-the-righteous architecture: the ungodly determine to-lie-in-wait-for-the-righteous because-he-is-clean-contrary-to-our-doings and upbraideth-us-with-our-offending-the-Torah. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:3-4's Herod-laying-hold-on-Yochanan (John) and binding-him for Herodias's-sake because Yochanan (John) said *it is not lawful for thee to have her.* Yochanan (John) upbraided Herod with the Torah-violation; Herod-Herodias determined to-lie-in-wait-for-the-righteous and to-bind-him. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-ungodly-disposition-toward-the-Torah-upbraiding-prophet centuries before; Matt 14:3-12 names the operative-form at the Herod-Antipas / Herodias / Salome arrangement. The disposition the wisdom-stream named operates at every recurrence of the architecture — the Pharisees against the King at Matt 12:14, Herod-Antipas against Yochanan (John) at Matt 14:3-12, the Sanhedrin against the King at Matt 26:3-4.

4574.new_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). *And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.* (Matthew 14:5). Wisdom shows the heart of the ungodly toward the righteous: torment him and see how long his meekness holds. Herod carried that heart toward John; he would have put him to death already, and only his fear of the crowd held his hand. The restraint was politics, not mercy, and a birthday oath later removed it. Isaiah's sheep dumb before her shearers, John in Herod's prison, Yahusha (Jesus) before Pilate — the ungodly keep running the same test on the righteous, and the righteous keep answering it the same way.
4574.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 — *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness.* Herod's heart toward John, held back only by fear of the multitude (Matthew 14:5).
4574.old_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the ungodly-determining-to-examine-the-righteous-with-despitefulness-and-torture architecture: examine-him-with-despitefulness-and-torture that-we-may-know-his-meekness. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:5's Herod's-restraint-from-killing-Yochanan-because-of-the-multitude — the disposition is to-test-and-eventually-kill, restrained-only-by-political-calculation. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture; Matt 14:5 names the operative-restraint-mechanism (the multitude's-fear) the disposition operates-within until the birthday-banquet arrangement removes the restraint. The framework reads the architecture in continuity with the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 53:7 *as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth* substance — the meekness-and-patience the ungodly-determine-to-examine-and-prove operates in the same architecture across Yochanan (John)'s-imprisonment, the King's-trial, and the apostolic-band's persecutions in Acts.

4575.new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.* (Matthew 14:10). A shameful death is not the honored end of a long life; it is a death arranged by men who want the righteous man gone. John's beheading in Herod's prison, on the strength of a rash birthday oath, is exactly the death Wisdom describes. The ungodly did not wait for the Father's verdict on his words; they gave their own. The prophets who upbraided the nation with the Torah died this way before him, and the King tells that whole history over in Matthew 23.
4575.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* John beheaded in the prison on a birthday oath (Matthew 14:10) is the death Wisdom describes.
4575.old_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the ungodly-determining-to-condemn-the-righteous-with-a-shameful-death architecture: condemn-him-with-a-shameful-death. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:10's *and he sent, and beheaded Yochanan (John) in the prison.* The shameful-death of the wisdom-stream's articulation is the beheading-in-the-prison the operative-form: the death is not the honorable-end of the natural-life-span; it is the execution-at-the-arrangement-of-the-corrupted-court at the birthday-banquet-oath. The framework reads the architecture in continuity with the broader Tanakh-prophet-killing pattern (2 Chronicles 24:20-22; Matt 23:34-37) — the shameful-deaths the ungodly-arrange for the Torah-upbraiding-prophets walk one architecture across the canon, the wisdom-stream, and the gospel-of-the-King's-ministry.

4576.new_note: *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:1). *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* (Matthew 15:4). Sirach begins his teaching on parents by speaking as a father: hear me, children, and do what I say, so that you may be safe. The whole chapter rests on the fifth commandment, the one Yahusha (Jesus) quotes back to the Pharisees in Matthew 15:4, honour thy father and mother, with the death penalty for cursing them attached. The tradition he is exposing in the verses that follow let a man vow to the altar what his aged parents needed and call himself free of them. Sirach had tied the children's safety to hearing and doing their father's word; the tradition untied it, and the Messiah names what Elohim (God) commanded to tie it back.
4576.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:1 — *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* The fifth commandment Yahusha (Jesus) quotes against the tradition at Matthew 15:4.
4576.old_note: *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the fifth-commandment substance — the parental-honor architecture the Torah commands at Shemot (Exodus) 20:12. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:4's *honour thy father and mother* citation. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the parental-honor-substance as the foundation-of-the-children's-safety; the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition the King exposes at vv.3-6 voids the architecture at the support-of-the-aged-parent level. The wisdom-stream's articulation reinforces the Torah-substance the King defends against the Pharisaic-tradition; the same architecture, the same load-bearing covenant-substance, the same diagnostic of the Pharisaic-system that voids the parental-honor commandment through the Corban-vow-mechanism.

4577.new_note: *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:8). *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* (Matthew 15:4). Honour your parents both in word and deed, Sirach says, and the two words are the whole argument. The corban tradition Yahusha (Jesus) exposes in Matthew 15 kept the word and dropped the deed: a man could speak a vow that sounded devout while the support his father and mother needed was cut off by it. The Messiah answers with what Elohim (God) commanded, honour thy father and mother, with no room left for honour that is spoken and not done. Sirach had closed that gap generations before by naming both halves, and a tradition that keeps one half has kept neither.
4577.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:8 — *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed.* The word without the deed the corban tradition allowed, against Matthew 15:4.
4577.old_note: *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:8 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the holistic-parental-honor substance — both in word and deed. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:4-6's King's-charge that the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition voids the parental-honor commandment. The Corban-tradition allowed the son to claim parental-honor-in-word (the formal-religious-vow appeared honorable) while voiding it in deed (the actual support-of-the-aged-parent was blocked by the vow's legal-mechanism). The wisdom-stream had named the architecture: honor must be BOTH word AND deed. The Pharisaic-Corban-tradition split them and called the word-without-the-deed righteous. The King names the split and dismantles it.

4578.new_note: *Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:27). *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* (Matthew 15:4). Sirach says honour your father with your whole heart, and he adds the mother's sorrows so the son remembers what he cost her. Matthew 15:4 is the commandment behind it, honour thy father and mother, quoted by Yahusha (Jesus) against a tradition that let a son divide his heart, a vow to the altar in one half and nothing left for his parents in the other. Whole heart is Sirach's word against that division. Later in the same chapter the Messiah says what defiles comes out of the heart (vv.18–20), and the corban device is the proof: an honour split by a vow was defiled before the vow was spoken.
4578.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 7:27 — *Honour your father with your whole heart.* The whole heart the corban tradition divided, against Matthew 15:4.
4578.old_note: *Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:27 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the whole-heart-parental-honor substance with the specific-remembering-of-the-mother's-sorrows. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:4's parental-honor commandment and the Pharisaic-Corban-evasion of vv.5-6. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture at the heart-level — honor your father with your WHOLE HEART; the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition violated the architecture by establishing a divided-heart-allowed-by-the-vow-mechanism. The King's-restoration of the heart-substance at vv.18-20 will close the loop on the heart-level the wisdom-stream had named.

4579.new_note: *He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed: of Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:16). *And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of Elohim (God) of none effect by your tradition.* (Matthew 15:6). Sirach does not treat neglect of parents as a small fault. To forsake a father is as blasphemy; to anger a mother is to be cursed of Yahuah (God). That is the weight behind Matthew 15:6, where a tradition lets a son honour not his father or his mother and call himself free, and the Messiah says the commandment of Elohim (God) has been made of none effect. What the tradition filed under devotion, Sirach had filed under blasphemy and curse. Yahusha (Jesus) is not inventing a harsher reading; he is reading the commandment the way the fathers already read it.
4579.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:16 — *He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer.* The weight behind the voided commandment at Matthew 15:6.
4579.old_note: *He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed: of Yahuah (God).* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:16 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the forsaking-the-father-as-blasphemy substance — the framework's reading of the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition at the worst-end of its diagnostic. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:6's *thus have ye made the commandment of Elohim (God) of none effect by your tradition.* The Pharisaic-Corban-tradition that allows the son to forsake the support-of-the-aged-parent is — at the wisdom-stream's articulation — the disposition of blasphemy and curse. The King's-charge at v.6 lands at the same load-bearing diagnostic the wisdom-stream had named: the disposition that voids the parental-honor commandment is at the architecture of blasphemy-against-the-Torah-the-Father-spoke-from-Sinai. The Pharisaic-system's-righteousness-credentialing was at the architecture the wisdom-stream had named cursed.

4580.new_note: *And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.* (Tobit 4:3). *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* (Matthew 15:4). A dying father in exile tells his son: honour your mother all the days of her life, please her, grieve her not. That is the fifth commandment lived out to the end of a parent's days, in a household far from the land. Yahusha (Jesus) quotes the same commandment against a tradition that let a man say *It is a gift* and so be freed from supporting his parents (15:5–6). Tobit shows what the commandment looks like when it is kept; the tradition shows what it looks like when a religious system finds a way around it, and it is the system that is being answered, not the people who were taught it.
4580.member_note: Tobit 4:3 — *despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life.* The commandment to honour father and mother, kept to the end of her days, which the gift tradition voided (Matthew 15:4).
4580.old_note: *And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.* Tobit 4:3 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the deathbed-instruction-of-the-Tobit-father to-his-son on the parental-honor architecture extending-to-the-mother-all-the-days-of-her-life. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:4's parental-honor commandment. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture across the second-Temple-Yashar'el (Israel) household-life: the parental-honor extends to the holistic-care of the mother (and by implication the father) across the entire-duration of the parent's-life. The Pharisaic-Corban-tradition the King exposes at vv.5-6 voids exactly this architecture; the wisdom-stream had named the substance the tradition was voiding centuries before.

4581.new_note: *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.* (Ecclesiasticus 15:11). *Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.* (Matthew 15:11). Sirach forbids a man to say he fell away through Yahuah (God); the things he hates are not his doing. Yahusha (Jesus) says defilement does not come in through the mouth but out of it — the source is the man's own heart. The two verses fence off the same lie from opposite sides: the Father does not cause the falling, and bread eaten with unwashed hands does not cause the defilement. What a man does and says comes from inside him, and that is where the Torah has always located it.
4581.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 15:11 — *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away.* The fall is not from Yahuah (God), and the defilement is not from the food (Matthew 15:11); both come from the man.
4581.old_note: *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father-NOT-being-the-source-of-the-man's-falling-away substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:11's *not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.* The King is restoring the substance-of-defilement to the heart-and-mouth (intentions, words, deeds proceeding from-the-heart) — the substance the wisdom-stream had named centuries before. The Father is NOT the source of the man's-defilement (Sirach 15:11's articulation); the man's-own-heart IS the source (Matt 15:18-19's articulation). The two articulations cohere at the heart-and-mouth-substance-as-the-locus-of-defilement architecture; the rabbinic-fence-tradition that had located-defilement at the un-washed-hands-and-the-food-categorically-touched-by-them inverted the architecture the wisdom-stream and the Torah had named.

4582.new_note: *He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.* (Ecclesiasticus 15:20). *But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.* (Matthew 15:18). Sirach says plainly that Yahuah (God) has commanded no man to do wickedly and given no man licence to sin. Yahusha (Jesus) says what defiles a man comes out of his own heart. Put the two together and the source of sin is found — not the Father, not the bread, not the unwashed hands the Pharisees fussed over, but the heart. Any teaching that gives licence to sin is giving what Yahuah (God) never gave.
4582.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 15:20 — *He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.* No licence to sin from Yahuah (God); the sin comes out of the heart at Matthew 15:18.
4582.old_note: *He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15:20 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father-NOT-commanding-wickedness and the Father-NOT-giving-licence-to-sin substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:18-19's *those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture: the Father has not commanded-wickedness and has not given-licence-to-sin; therefore the source-of-the-wickedness-and-the-sin is NOT-the-Father; therefore the source IS the man's-own-heart-out-of-which-the-evil-thoughts-and-the-second-table-Decalogue-violations-proceed. The King's-articulation at Matt 15:18-19 lands the substance the wisdom-stream had named at the gospel-level's precision.

4583.new_note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:6). *But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.* (Matthew 15:18). The fruit shows the tree, Sirach says, and a man's speech shows what his heart has conceived. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same when the Pharisees fuss over unwashed hands: what defiles a man comes out of his mouth, and it comes from the heart. The heart is the source. Bread eaten with unwashed hands does not defile the man; what defiles him is what his own heart conceives and his mouth lets out, and the good tree bringing forth good fruit in Matthew 7:17 is the same picture. Watch what comes out, and you have seen what is inside.
4583.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* The heart's conceit comes out in the mouth; *those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart* (Matthew 15:18).
4583.old_note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the tree-and-fruit-and-utterance architecture — the heart's-conceit manifests in the utterance-of-the-mouth. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:18's *those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture in the tree-and-fruit-metaphor centuries before; the King's Matt 7:17-20 *every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit* operates in the same architecture; the King's Matt 15:18 articulation locks the operative-form: the heart's-substance manifests in the mouth's-utterance and the deeds-that-follow. The cause-and-effect-of-hearing diagnostic per Red Line #11 carries through the same architecture — the heart's-substance determines what the mouth-and-deeds reveal.

4584.new_note: *Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:11). *For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:* (Matthew 15:19). Wisdom of Solomon warns about the mouth: murmuring, backbiting, the lying mouth that kills the soul. Yahusha (Jesus) traces the mouth back to its source, *those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart* (Matthew 15:18), and then lists what comes out of it, false witness and blasphemies among them. The two lists overlap because they are describing one thing from two ends: the heart is where the evil starts, and the tongue is where it shows. That is why the promise of the new covenant is a heart with the Torah written on it (Jeremiah 31:33), because a clean mouth needs a clean spring.
4584.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* The lying mouth of Wisdom 1:11 and the false witness of Matthew 15:19 come from the same place, the heart.
4584.old_note: *Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the mouth-and-tongue substance — the murmuring, the backbiting, the lying-mouth all operate at the soul-slaying register. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:19's catalogue: *evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies.* The Wisdom of Solomon catalogue (murmuring, backbiting, the lying-mouth) and the King's catalogue (false witness, blasphemies) overlap at the mouth-substance level. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture; the King names the operative-form. The framework reads this in continuity with the broader-Tanakh-substance: the tongue-and-the-mouth are the manifest-substance of the heart-Torah of Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31:33 / Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27 that the King is restoring.

4585.new_note: *Have mercy upon us, O Yahuah (God) of all, and behold us:* (Ecclesiasticus 36:1). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). Sirach opens his great prayer with a cry for mercy to the Elohim (God) of all, and the prayer goes on to ask that all the tribes of Jacob be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says he was not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel). The one being asked for mercy in Sirach's prayer is the one who answered it in person, sent to the very scattered house the prayer was about. Behold us, Sirach prays; the Shepherd came looking for the sheep.
4585.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:1 — *Have mercy upon us, O Yahuah (God) of all, and behold us.* The prayer for mercy that the mission to the lost sheep (Matthew 15:24) answers.
4585.old_note: *Have mercy upon us, O Yahuah (God) of all, and behold us.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the gathering-of-the-scattered-tribes prayer — the petition-for-mercy on the scattered-people-of-the-covenant. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:24's *I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* The wisdom-stream's prayer-for-the-gathering operates as the petition the King's-mission answers at the gospel-level: the lost-sheep-of-the-house-of-Yashar'el (Israel) are the recipients-of-the-mercy the Sirach 36 prayer petitioned-for. The framework reads the lost-sheep-mission-scope at v.24 as the King's-answer to the wisdom-stream's-articulated-petition for the gathering of the scattered-tribes.

4586.new_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). Sirach prays for the gathering of all the tribes of Jacob, back into the inheritance as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says he was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel). The prayer and the mission have the same object: not Yahudah (Judah) alone, who had a temple and a land, but the whole house that had been scattered and lost among the nations. The prophets promised it, Sirach prayed it, and the King came for it.
4586.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *inherit you them, as from the beginning.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in Matthew 15:24 are the tribes Sirach prayed home.
4586.old_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:11 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the gathering-of-all-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob) substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:24's lost-sheep-mission-scope. The wisdom-stream's prayer is for the gathering-of-ALL-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob) — the explicit articulation of the twelve-tribes-restoration-substance the prophets had named (Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37:21; Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31:8-10; Hosea 1:10-11; Zekharyah (Zechariah) 10:6-10). The King's-mission-scope at v.24 IS the operative-form of the wisdom-stream's-prayer at Sirach 36:11; the lost-sheep-of-the-house-of-Yashar'el (Israel) the King is sent-to IS the all-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob) the wisdom-stream had prayed for the gathering of. The framework reads this as FRAMEWORK-MAJOR for the lost-sheep-mission-scope's wisdom-stream confirmation.

4587.new_note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). When the woman of Canaan pressed him, Yahusha (Jesus) named the scope of his sending: the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) — and she, who heard the Shepherd and would not be turned away, was one of them. Ezra had already been shown who that house is, the ten tribes Shalmaneser led away captive over the waters into another land, who never returned. The lost sheep were not a figure of speech; they were a people with a date, a captor, and a direction of travel, the same carrying away the book of Kings records (2 Kings 17:6). The King was sent to them, and the prophets who promised their gathering (Jeremiah 31; Ezekiel 37) were speaking of the same people.
4587.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:40 — *whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) the King says he was sent to (Matthew 15:24).
4587.old_note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:40 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the ten-tribes-carried-away-by-the-Assyrian-exile substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:24's lost-sheep-mission-scope. The lost-sheep-of-the-house-of-Yashar'el (Israel) the King's-mission addresses at v.24 are precisely the ten-tribes 2 Esdras 13:40 names — the scattered-northern-house-of-Yashar'el (Israel) the Assyrian-deportation carried-into-the-territories-of-the-dispersion. The framework reads this in continuity with the broader-Tanakh-substance of the Assyrian-exile (2 Melakhim (Kings) 17:6, 17:23; 1 Divrei HaYamim (Chronicles) 5:26) and the prophetic-gathering-architecture (Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37 + 47; Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31).

4588.new_note: *But those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders.* (2 Esdras 13:48). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). The vision does not forget the ones who never left. After the ten tribes come home, Ezra is told that those left behind of his people are the ones found within the borders of the land, the remnant of Yahudah (Judah) that stayed. When Yahusha (Jesus) says he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), his sending reaches both of these: the multitudes of Galilee and Yahudah (Judah) he walked among inside the borders, and the scattered house beyond the waters his apostles would be sent after. The house of Yashar'el (Israel) is both of them, the ones who stayed and the ones who were carried, and the King's mission is to the whole house.
4588.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:48 — *those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders.* The remnant that stayed; the King's mission reaches them and the scattered alike (Matthew 15:24).
4588.old_note: *But those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:48 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the remnant-found-within-the-borders substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:24's lost-sheep-mission-scope. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the remnant-and-the-scattered-tribes-coming-home; the King's-mission addresses both registers — the remnant-within-the-borders (the Galilee-and-Yahudah multitudes) AND the scattered-tribes-in-the-territories-of-the-dispersion (the broader-mission the apostolic-extension will reach). The framework reads the lost-sheep-mission-scope at v.24 as encompassing both registers the wisdom-stream had named.

4589.new_note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* (Tobit 13:5). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). Tobit names who gets gathered and from where: the people Yahuah (God) scourged and scattered, brought back out of all the nations. Ezekiel had said the same, *I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side* (Ezekiel 37:21). When Yahusha (Jesus) says he is not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), he is stating the scope of that gathering, not narrowing his mercy. He said it to the woman of Canaan, and she was not turned away; the sheep hear the Shepherd's voice wherever the scattering has carried them, and the hearing shows who they are. The mission to the lost sheep is the mercy Tobit said would follow the scourge.
4589.member_note: Tobit 13:5 — *will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) Yahusha (Jesus) was sent to are the scattered Tobit said would be gathered (Matthew 15:24).
4589.reason: The Ezekiel 37:21 quotation is carried over from the old note; its live text was not in the packet, so please check it against the canon. Added one sentence on the woman of Canaan (the verse's setting) as seed revealed by hearing, per the skill.
4589.old_note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* Tobit 13:5 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the scourge-then-mercy-then-gathering-out-of-all-nations substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:24's lost-sheep-mission-scope.
