The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the gathering-out-of-all-nations-among-whom-the-Father-had-scattered-the-people — the exact-architecture the prophets had named (Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37:21's *I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side*) and the King's-mission enacts at v.24. The framework reads the Tobit 13:5 substance in continuity with the broader-Tanakh-substance and the King's-mission-scope at Matt 15:24.

4601.new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Messiah (Christ), the Son of the living Elohim (God).* (Matthew 16:16). The same words come from two mouths. The ungodly in Wisdom say it in mockery — if the just man is the son of Yahuah (God), let him be delivered. Peter says it in confession — thou art the Messiah (Christ), the Son of the living Elohim (God). What the wicked used as a taunt against the righteous man is the title the Father reveals to Peter at the turning point of the gospel. The just man of Wisdom is the Son Peter confessed, and the plot to test him never changed who he was.
4601.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* Said in mockery here; confessed by Peter at Matthew 16:16 as *the Son of the living Elohim (God).*
4601.reason: Old note reached into the nature-of-God question (Formed and Formless against Trinity and its denial); the card does not need it, so the rebuilt note keeps to the taunt-and-confession connection and asserts no doctrine either way.
4601.old_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the just-man-as-the-son-of-Yahuah substance — the wicked's-mocking-challenge against the righteous-one in the prefiguring-passage Wisdom of Solomon 2:12-20 carries. The framework reads the verse against Matt 16:16's *thou art the Messiah, the Son of the living Elohim (God).* Kefa's (Peter's)-confession articulates at the gospel-pivot the title the wisdom-stream had named in the prefiguring-of-the-righteous-one architecture: the just-man-is-the-son-of-Yahuah; the framework reads the substance against the inherited-Christian-Trinity-doctrine's collapse and against the Trinity-denial's collapse — the Son-of-Yahuah substance is the Formed-Voice's relation-to-the-Formless-Source per the framework's nature-of-God reading; the wisdom-stream had named the architecture in the prefiguring-passage; Kefa's (Peter's)-confession lands the operative-substance.

4606.new_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). The ungodly in Wisdom of Solomon 2 begin by lying in wait and end by resolving, *let us condemn him with a shameful death* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples the same ending in advance, suffering at the hands of the elders, chief priests and scribes, and death in Jerusalem. The religious leadership of the day fills the role Wisdom wrote for the ungodly, a system that could not bear a righteous man whose life reproved it. But he adds a line Wisdom's plotters never saw coming, raised again the third day, and Wisdom itself knew it: the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Elohim (God) (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1).
4606.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous.* The plot of Wisdom 2 ends in a shameful death; at Matthew 16:21 Yahusha (Jesus) names the same end and adds the third day.
4606.old_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the wicked's-plot-against-the-righteous-one substance — the prefiguring-passage Wisdom of Solomon 2:12-20 carries the architecture of the righteous-one persecuted-by-the-wicked-who-cannot-bear-his-reproof. The framework reads the verse against Matt 16:21's *he must go unto Yerushalayim (Jerusalem), and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the persecution-of-the-righteous-one centuries before; the King's-first-passion-prediction names the operative-form: the elders-and-chief-priests-and-scribes (the Pharisaic-and-Sadducean-second-Temple-aristocracy) are the wicked-Wisdom-of-Solomon-2-names-in-the-prefiguring-architecture; the King is the righteous-one Wisdom-of-Solomon-2-names; the suffering-and-killing the King names is the operative-fulfillment of the architecture.

4607.new_note: *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). The men who esteemed themselves righteous felt judged by a man who would not walk their way and who called Yahuah (God) his father. Wisdom puts the grievance in their own mouths; Matthew names who held it in Yahusha's (Jesus') day — the elders, the chief priests and the scribes, the men who held the seats of religion in Jerusalem. He told his disciples plainly that he must suffer at their hands and be killed, because a life that counts their ways as filthiness is an indictment they could not leave standing. It was the seat of the system that rose against him, not the people sitting under it.

4608.new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). Wisdom says the ungodly will condemn the righteous man to a shameful death. Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples he must suffer and be killed, and later he names how: delivered to be mocked, scourged and crucified (Matthew 20:19). The cross was the shameful death — the Torah itself says *he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim (God)* (Deuteronomy 21:23), so the men who hung him there meant it as the Father's own rejection of him. Isaiah's servant, Wisdom's just man and the passion the King announced all meet at that tree. And he named the third day in the same breath, which is the answer to the whole plot.

4609.new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples both halves in one sentence — he must be killed, and be raised again the third day. The being killed is the shameful death; the being raised is the hand of the Father. Wisdom had already laid the two chapters side by side, and the gospel shows the one man who walked through both.

4610.new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). Here the King lays out both halves at once: he will suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, be killed, and be raised the third day. Solomon saw the second half from far off, the righteous man standing in boldness before the very men who afflicted him and made no account of his labours. The third day is where that standing begins, and the King finishes the thought a few verses later, when the Son of Adam comes in the glory of his Father to reward every man according to his works (Matthew 16:27). The vindication does not make him righteous; it shows in public what was true all along.

4611.new_note: *For Yahuah (God) made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:13). *And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.* (Matthew 16:18). Wisdom of Solomon says it flatly: Yahuah (God) did not make death. It came in through the envy of the devil (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24) and through the sin in the garden; it is an intruder in his creation, not his design. That is why Yahusha (Jesus) can say the gates of hell, the gates of the grave, will not prevail against the assembly he builds. A thing the Father did not make has no permanent claim on what he did make. The grave's gates held every son of Adam until the one who said this walked out through them on the third day, and because he did, the gates will not hold his people either.
4611.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:13 — *Yahuah (God) made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.* Death is not of Yahuah's (God's) making, so the gates of the grave at Matthew 16:18 have no lasting claim on the assembly he builds.
4611.old_note: *For Yahuah (God) made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.* Wisdom of Solomon 1:13 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the death-is-not-from-Yahuah substance — the Father is not-the-source of the death-and-the-grave; the death-and-the-grave entered through the seed-war and the curse the Bereshit (Genesis) 3 narrative names. The framework reads the verse against Matt 16:18's *the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.* The gates-of-Sheol/Hades carry the power-of-death-and-the-grave that entered through the curse; the gates do not originate-with-the-Father; therefore the gates do not have permanence-against the assembly the King builds; therefore the resurrection-substance the King will demonstrate at the sign-of-Yonah breaks the gates' hold. 4612.new_note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). *And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.* (Matthew 16:18). The gates of hell have no final say, because the one who leads down to those gates is the same one who brings up again. That is what stands behind the promise to Peter: the assembly is built on the King who would be raised the third day (he says so plainly at verse 21), and the gates that closed on him could not hold him, so they will not prevail against what he builds. The same chapter opens with the sign of Jonah (verse 4); the whole chapter is carrying this one truth, that the grave is a door the Father opens.

4614.new_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.* (Matthew 16:18). The righteous dead are in chambers, Esdras is told, asking when the floor of their reward will come. They are not in torment and they are not in heaven; they are resting and waiting, and later in the book the chambers deliver up the souls committed to them at the resurrection (2 Esdras 7:32). That is what the King means when he says the gates of hell shall not prevail against his assembly. Sheol is a holding place with gates, and the gates do not hold his people past the day he calls them out. The chambers keep the righteous; they do not keep them forever.
4614.member_note: 2 Esdras 4:35 — *the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers.* The chambers hold the righteous until the resurrection; the gates of hell shall not prevail (Matthew 16:18).

4615.new_note: *As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he judges a man according to his works* (Ecclesiasticus 16:12). *For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* (Matthew 16:27). Sirach holds mercy and correction in the same hand and says the measure of both is a man's works. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same about his own coming in his Father's glory: every man rewarded according to his works. Grace is the door home, not the cancelling of the reckoning. The judgment weighs the fruit, and the fruit comes from a heart that either received the new heart Ezekiel promised or did not.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 16:27's *the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the judgment-according-to-works; the King's-second-coming-substance operates the same architecture at the eschatological-consummation. 4616.new_note: *Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.* (Ecclesiasticus 16:14). *For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* (Matthew 16:27). Yahusha (Jesus) says the finding happens when the Son of Adam comes in his Father's glory. Mercy done now is what is found then. The door home is opened by grace; what is weighed at the judgment is what the one who came home did after he walked in.

4617.new_note: *Till he have rendered to every man according to his deeds, and to the works of men according to their devices; till he have judged the cause of his people, and made them to rejoice in his mercy.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:19). *For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* (Matthew 16:27). Sirach says Yahuah (God) will not rest until he has rendered to every man according to his deeds and judged the cause of his people and made them rejoice in his mercy. Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam will come in the glory of his Father and reward every man according to his works. The two halves Sirach holds together are the two halves the King names: a reckoning by works for every man, and vindication and joy for his own people. Reward comes at his coming and it comes by deeds, and those who are his rejoice in mercy on that day rather than in a reckoning they skipped.

4618.new_note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). *For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* (Matthew 16:27). Ezra is shown the order: first the earth gives back those asleep in her and the secret places deliver the souls committed to them, then the Most High appears on the seat of judgment, and the work follows and the reward is shown (2 Esdras 7:33–35). Yahusha (Jesus) gives the same order in one sentence: the Son of Adam comes in his Father's glory, and then he rewards every man according to his works. Resurrection first, then the reward by works. The righteous who sleep are not being rewarded somewhere now; they rest in the places committed to them until the earth restores them, and the reckoning comes after.

4619.new_note: *And the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.* (2 Esdras 7:35). *For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* (Matthew 16:27). Yahusha (Jesus) says it as plainly: when the Son of Adam comes in his Father's glory, he rewards every man according to his works. This is not a man earning his place; it is a man's deeds going with him into the day and being weighed there. The works that follow are the fruit of a heart that kept what it was given, and those with no such fruit are told to depart (Matthew 7:23).

4687.new_note: *Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.* (Ecclesiasticus 19:13). *Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.* (Matthew 18:15). Sirach's counsel is to go to the friend first, because he may not have done it at all, and if he has, so that he will do it no more. Yahusha (Jesus) makes that the first step when a brother trespasses: go to him alone, tell him his fault, and if he hears you the brother is gained. Both aim at restoration, not at shame or gossip — the private word comes before anything else, and the Torah had already told a man to rebuke his neighbour rather than carry a grudge against him in his heart.
4687.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 19:13 — *Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it.* The private first step of Matthew 18:15 — go to him alone, and he may be gained.

The framework reads the verse against *go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.* The wisdom-stream had named the direct-and-private admonition-of-the-friend substance at the wisdom-instruction-register; the King institutionalizes the same substance at the assembly's-procedural-register. The substance reads in continuity with Vayikra (Leviticus) 19:17's *thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour.*

4688.new_note: *Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the Most High.* (Ecclesiasticus 19:17). *Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.* (Matthew 18:15). Sirach sets the order and the temper together: admonish before you threaten, and do it without anger, letting the law of the Most High govern the matter rather than your own heat. That is the spirit of the first step Yahusha (Jesus) gives — go to the brother alone and tell him his fault, which is admonition, not threat. The goal is to gain the brother, and a man cannot gain his brother while he is angry at him. The rebuke works when the Torah, not the rebuker's temper, is what it stands on.
4688.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 19:17 — *Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him.* The order and the temper of the private word in Matthew 18:15 — admonish first, and not in anger.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 18:15. The wisdom-stream names BOTH (a) the order — admonish BEFORE threatening, the substance of restoration before the substance of consequence — AND (b) the disposition — *not being angry, give place to the law of the Most High,* the wisdom-stream's articulation that the Torah-substance, not the rebuker's-own-anger, is the substance the rebuke-is-operating-from. 4689.new_note: *Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.* (Ecclesiasticus 19:15). *But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.* (Matthew 18:16). Sirach warns that many a report is slander and that not every tale should be believed — so go and admonish the friend rather than take the story as settled. Yahusha (Jesus) builds the same safeguard into the second step: if the brother will not hear, bring one or two more, so that every word is established in the mouth of two or three witnesses. The witnesses protect the accused from a false charge and the accuser from his own inflated one. What Sirach counseled as wisdom, the King set as procedure, and both rest on the Torah's rule that one witness is never enough.
4689.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 19:15 — *for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.* The two or three witnesses of Matthew 18:16 guard against the slander Sirach warns of.

The framework reads the verse against *then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.* The wisdom-stream names the substance the witness-verification-procedure protects against — slander, the false-tale, the unverified-charge. The King applies the Tanakh-Devarim (Deuteronomy) 19:15 evidentiary-standard the wisdom-stream had named the necessity-of at the wisdom-instruction-register. The substance protects both the brother-accused (from false-charge) and the brother-accusing (from inflated-or-fabricated charge); the witnesses serve as the substance-restraint on the offended-party as much as on the accused.

4690.new_note: *It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly: and he that confesseth his fault shall be preserved from hurt.* (Ecclesiasticus 20:2). *And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.* (Matthew 18:17). Sirach says open reproof is far better than secret anger, and the man who confesses his fault when reproved is preserved from hurt. That is what the third step in Matthew is for: when the private word and the witnesses have both been refused, the matter is told to the assembly in the open, where it can still be confessed and the brother still preserved. Secret anger restores no one. Open reproof, met with confession, does — and only when even the assembly is refused does the brother put himself outside.
4690.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 20:2 — *It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly.* The open reproof before the assembly in Matthew 18:17 — the alternative to secret anger that restores no one.
4690.old_note: *It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly: and he that confesseth his fault shall be preserved from hurt.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 20:2 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the substance-of-the-open-reproof — the assembly-level-confrontation the King names at Matt 18:17's step-three (*tell it unto the assembly*) operates in the architecture-of-open-reproof the wisdom-stream had named the substance for. The framework reads the verse against the King's assembly-level-step. The wisdom-stream names the alternative-architecture: angry-secretly is the substance that does-not-restore; the open-reproof followed-by-the-brother's-confession is the substance that restores. The King's step-three is the assembly-level operationalization of the wisdom-stream's instruction; the assembly-as-a-whole carries the open-reproof-substance at the corporate-register the wisdom-stream had carried at the wisdom-instruction-register.

4691.new_note: *Malice and wrath, even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:30). *Then came Peter to him, and said, Adonai (Lord), how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?* (Matthew 18:21). Sirach calls malice and wrath abominations, the portion of the sinful man. Peter comes to Yahusha (Jesus) still counting, asking how many times he has to forgive his brother, seven? A man who is counting offences is still holding them, and what he is holding is the malice Sirach names. The King's answer pushes past the count altogether, because the heart he is forming in his disciples is the new heart of Ezekiel 36:26, the one the Spirit moves to walk in the statutes, and that heart does not keep a tally against a brother.
4691.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 27:30 — *even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.* Malice and wrath as the sinful man's portion; Peter's *till seven times?* (Matthew 18:21) is still counting, and the King's answer leaves the count behind.
4691.old_note: *Malice and wrath, even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:30 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the disposition-the-King-is-forming-against at Kefa (Peter)'s v.21 question. The framework reads the verse against Matt 18:21. The wisdom-stream had named malice and wrath as abominations-before-Yahuah at the wisdom-instruction-register; Kefa's *how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?* is the disciple-substance still-counting-the-offences, and the King's answer presses-past-the-counting into the disposition-of-no-malice. The framework reads this in continuity with the kingdom-citizens' fruits-of-the-Spirit substance (Galatians 5:22-23's love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness) the new-heart of Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27 forms-the-walker-into. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.

4692.new_note: *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:2). *Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.* (Matthew 18:22). Sirach says forgive your neighbour, and your own sins will be forgiven when you pray. Peter asks how many times, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers seventy times seven, then tells the parable of the servant who was forgiven a fortune and would not forgive a few pence, and closes it with the warning that the heavenly Father will do the same to anyone who does not forgive his brother from the heart. The Lord's Prayer had already made the same condition, forgive and be forgiven, forgive not and be not forgiven (Matthew 6:14–15). Sirach said it in one line; the King said it in a prayer, a number, and a story, and it is one teaching.
4692.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 28:2 — *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you.* The one line behind the King's *seventy times seven* (Matthew 18:22) and the parable that follows it: forgive, and be forgiven.
4692.old_note: *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 28:2 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the conditional-forgiveness-architecture the King names at Matt 18:21-22 and parable-extends at vv.23-35. The framework reads the verse against the King's *seventy times seven* answer + the unforgiving-servant parable + the chapter-closing *so likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not* (v.35). The wisdom-stream had named the substance directly: forgive-the-neighbour, and your-sins-shall-also-be-forgiven; the conditional-substance the King's parable extends into full narrative-form was already-articulated at the wisdom-stream-register. The framework reads this in continuity with Matt 6:14-15's Lord's-Prayer conditional-substance — *for if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.* The architecture-of-mercy-met-with-mercy runs the King's-teaching from the Sermon through the assembly-discourse; the wisdom-stream had named the substance the King operationalizes.

4693.new_note: *One man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from Yahuah (God)?* (Ecclesiasticus 28:3). *Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?* (Matthew 18:33). Sirach asks the plain question: a man holds hatred against another man, and he goes looking for pardon from Yahuah (God)? The parable in Matthew 18 puts that man in a story. He has just been forgiven everything he owed, and he takes his fellow servant by the throat over a trifle, and his lord asks him the very question Sirach asked, should you not have had compassion as I had pity on you? The pardon he had received was taken back. Mercy received has to become mercy given, or it does not stay.
4693.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 28:3 — *One man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from Yahuah (God)?.* Sirach's question is the lord's question at Matthew 18:33, *shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant*; the pardon that was not passed on was taken back.
4693.old_note: *One man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from Yahuah (God)?* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 28:3 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the unforgiving-servant's-grotesque-architecture the King names at Matt 18:33. The framework reads the verse against the lord's charge to the first-servant: *O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?* The wisdom-stream had named the grotesque-substance: one-man-bears-hatred-against-another and yet seeks-pardon-from-Yahuah for himself; the parable shows the same architecture in narrative-form — the first-servant has-been-forgiven and refuses-to-forgive. The lord's-wrath-and-revocation-of-the-forgiveness in the parable is the same architectural-substance Sirach had named the wisdom-instruction-substance-against. The kingdom-citizen's-substance must match the substance-received; the architecture is mercy-met-with-mercy at every register the wisdom-stream-and-the-King-and-the-apostles articulate.

4694.new_note: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:7). *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* (Matthew 18:35). Sirach says two things in one line and means them as one: remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour; remember the covenant of the Highest, and overlook ignorance. Yahusha (Jesus) ends the parable of the unforgiving servant on the same note, that the heavenly Father will deal the same way with anyone who does not forgive his brother from the heart. Remembering the Torah and forgiving the brother are not two different religions; the law written on the heart (Jeremiah 31:33) is what produces a heart without malice. And the parable is plain that the forgiveness a man received can be taken back if he will not extend it; the door home stays a door, and the man who bears malice against his brother has walked away from it.
4694.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 28:7 — *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour.* Torah remembered and malice laid down as one thing; at Matthew 18:35 the Father deals the same way with the one who will not forgive *from your hearts*.
4694.old_note: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 28:7 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the heart-Torah-substance the King's chapter-closing v.35 lands-on. The framework reads the verse against Matt 18:35's *so likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* The wisdom-stream had named the substance directly: remember-the-commandments AND bear-no-malice to your-neighbour; remember-the-covenant-of-the-Most-High AND wink-at-ignorance. The two-substances are NOT in tension; the two-substances are one-substance — the Torah-internalized produces the substance-of-no-malice; the substance-of-no-malice is the operation-of-the-Torah-internalized. The framework reads this in continuity with Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31:33's new-covenant law-in-the-inward-parts and Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27's new-heart-and-Spirit-causing-the-walking — the wisdom-stream had named the substance the new-covenant brings-to-completion. The grace-that-can-be-lost architecture per Red Line #10 operates here: the walker who-walks-the-substance walks-through-the-door-home; the walker-who-bears-malice-against-the-brother has-not-walked-the-substance-the-grace-was-given-to-form.

4696.new_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 18:3). The greater you are, the more humble yourself, Sirach says, and Yahusha (Jesus) makes it the condition of entry: except you be converted and become as little children, you do not enter the kingdom at all. The disciples had just asked who is greatest, and the answer turned their measure upside down, because in the kingdom greatness is measured by how low a man will go, not how high he is set. Sirach was teaching it at a father's table long before the disciples argued about it on the road. The one who humbles himself as a little child is the greatest in that kingdom, which is exactly the favour Sirach said the humble find.
4696.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:18 — *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* The humbling that is the kingdom's entry at Matthew 18:3.
4696.old_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:18 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the kingdom-inversion-of-greatness substance the King teaches at Matt 18:3-4. The framework reads the verse against *except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.* The wisdom-stream had named the substance directly: the-greater-you-are, the-more-humble-yourself; the substance the King teaches at the assembly-disposition register the wisdom-stream had taught at the wisdom-instruction register. The framework reads this in continuity with the Tanakh-*anawim* (humble-poor) substance pattern (Tehillim (Psalm) 131:1-2; Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 57:15; Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 66:2; Mishlei (Proverbs) 22:4); the apostolic-restatement at 1 Peter 5:5 (citing Mishlei (Proverbs) 3:34) and Yaaqov (James) 4:10. The kingdom-citizen's greatness is measured by the depth of the humility-substance, not by the height of the position-substance.

4697.new_note: *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:14). *Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 18:4). Sirach says Yahuah (God) has already done it: the proud cast off their thrones, the meek set in their place. Yahusha (Jesus) says the one who humbles himself as a little child is the greatest in the kingdom. It is the same hand moving in the same direction. The assembly is told to walk now by the measure the Father will judge by on that day.
4697.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 10:14 — *cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* The meek set up in the proud's stead is the child who is greatest at Matthew 18:4.
4697.old_note: *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 10:14 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the kingdom-inversion-of-thrones substance — the proud-cast-down and the meek-set-up at the same divine-action. The framework reads the verse against Matt 18:4's *whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.* The wisdom-stream names the same inversion the King names — the substance the assembly is to walk-in is the substance the Father acts-by at the eschatological-day. The framework reads this in continuity with Mary's Magnificat at Luke 1:51-52 (*he hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree*) and the post-resurrection apostolic-restatement at 1 Corinthians 1:26-29 (*Elohim (God) hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and Elohim (God) hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty*).

4698.new_note: *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:7). *At the same time came the disciples unto Yahusha (Jesus), saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?* (Matthew 18:1). Sirach names pride as hateful before Yahuah (God) and man both, the root from which iniquity grows on either side. The disciples came to Yahusha (Jesus) asking who would be greatest in the kingdom; Mark records that they had been disputing it on the road. The question itself was the disposition Sirach warned against, and the King answered it by setting a child in their midst. The kingdom does not rank the way the kingdoms of the earth do.
4698.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 10:7 — *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man.* The pride Sirach names is the disposition behind who is the greatest at Matthew 18:1.
4698.old_note: *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 10:7 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the disposition-the-King-is-confronting at the disciples' v.1 hierarchy-question. The framework reads the verse against Matt 18:1's *who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?* The disciples have-imbibed-substantially of the kingdom-substance over months of ministry; the disciples have-not-yet-shed the natural-kingdoms' hierarchy-substance the wisdom-stream had named the pride-substance for. The framework reads the verse in continuity with the Markan-parallel's preserved-detail at Mark 9:33-34 (the disciples-had-been-disputing-on-the-road *who should be the greatest*) — the pride-substance the wisdom-stream names is the substance operating-in the disciples' road-side-dispute. The King's-acted-parable of the child-in-the-midst is the substance-correction the wisdom-stream had instructed-toward.

4701.new_note: *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.* (Tobit 8:6). *Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore Elohim (God) hath joined together, let not man put asunder.* (Matthew 19:6). On his wedding night Tobias prays the creation back over his marriage: you made Adam and gave him Eve for a helper, and from them came mankind. When the Pharisees pressed Yahusha (Jesus) about divorce he went to the same place, to the beginning, and said that what Elohim (God) has joined no man may put asunder. The library and the gospel stand on the same ground: marriage is the Father's joining, not a human arrangement to be undone at preference. Malachi says he hates putting away (Malachi 2:16), and Tobias's prayer shows a young man who already knew it.
4701.member_note: Tobit 8:6 — *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay.* The creation prayed over a marriage bed; *What therefore Elohim (God) hath joined together, let not man put asunder* (Matthew 19:6).
4701.old_note: *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.* Tobit 8:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the creation-ordinance marriage-substance in Tobias's-prayer-at-the-marriage-bed — the same Bereshit (Genesis) 2:18 + 2:23-24 substance the King restates at Matt 19:6's *wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore Elohim (God) hath joined together, let not man put asunder.* The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream's direct anchor for the Father-joins-the-one-flesh-substance — Tobias prays the creation-ordinance substance over his marriage to Sarah, naming the same substance the King names at the divorce-controversy-pivot. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the Father-joins-the-one-flesh-substance architecture; what the Father has joined, no human authority undoes at preference. The substance is in continuity with Malachi 2:14-16's *Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)... hateth putting away* — the Father's-substance toward-putting-away has-always-been-hate-substance, the Mosaic-concession-permission notwithstanding.

4702.new_note: *And blessed is the eunuch, which with his hands has wrought no iniquity, nor imagined wicked things against Yahuah (God): for to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (God) more acceptable to his mind.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:14). *For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.* (Matthew 19:12). Wisdom blesses the eunuch who has kept his hands clean and promises him the special gift of faith and an inheritance in the house of Yahuah (God). Isaiah had said it first — *even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters* (Isaiah 56:5). Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of eunuchs who have made themselves so for the kingdom of heaven's sake, and adds: he that is able to receive it, let him receive it. All three treat it as a gift received, not a rule imposed, which is the word both the system that made celibacy a requirement for its clergy and the system that treats the unmarried as half a life managed to miss. The inheritance is for the one to whom it is given.
4702.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:14 — *to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (God).* The gift behind Matthew 19:12's *he that is able to receive it, let him receive it.*
4702.old_note: *And blessed is the eunuch, which with his hands has wrought no iniquity, nor imagined wicked things against Yahuah (God): for to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (the LORD) more acceptable to his mind.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:14 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the blessed-eunuch-with-an-inheritance substance — the Isaiah 56:3-5 substance the King's eunuchs-for-the-kingdom-of-heaven's-sake saying at Matt 19:12 carries forward at the gospel-register. The framework reads the verse against the King's *there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.* The Isaiah 56:3-5 promise — *a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters* in the Father's-house — and the Wisdom of Solomon 3:14 promise — *the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (the LORD)* — both name the wisdom-stream-substance the voluntary-celibate-for-the-kingdom-of-heaven walks. The substance is gift, not mandate; the substance is the kingdom-citizen-receiving-the-substance, not the system imposing it. The framework rules out BOTH the Roman-Catholic-mandatory-clerical-celibacy substance the institutional-tradition has imposed AND the Reformation-marriage-mandate-with-no-honored-celibate-substance over-correction. The substance the King-himself walked (1 Corinthians 7:7-8, 32-35's apostle Sha'ul (Paul) walking the same gift-substance) is the substance offered-to-those-to-whom-it-is-given, with the wisdom-stream's-promise-of-inheritance the Isaiah 56 substance carries.

4703.new_note: *Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:23). *Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them.* (Matthew 19:13). Sirach puts children on the list of a man's responsibilities: if you have them, instruct them and bend their necks from their youth. The parents in Matthew 19:13 are doing that when they bring their little ones to Yahusha (Jesus) for his hands and his prayer; it is the Torah's own charge to teach the children carried out in the plainest way, bringing them to the one who teaches. The disciples rebuked the parents, and the Messiah rebuked the disciples, because the bringing was right. Instruction begins with whom you bring your children to.
4703.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 7:23 — *Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.* The parents bringing their children to Yahusha (Jesus) at Matthew 19:13.
4703.old_note: *Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:23 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the parental-instruction-of-children substance — the substance the parents-bringing-the-little-children-to-the-King at Matt 19:13 enact at the practical-substance level. The framework reads the verse against Matt 19:13's *then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray.* The parents' act is in continuity with the Tanakh-and-wisdom-stream-substance of bringing-children-to-the-Father-for-instruction-and-blessing — the parental-substance of transmitting-the-covenant-to-the-next-generation (Devarim (Deuteronomy) 6:6-7's *and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house*; Tehillim (Psalm) 78:5-7's substance-of-teaching-the-children). The King-as-the-Father's-substance-in-the-flesh receives-the-children the parents have brought to him; the wisdom-stream had named the substance the parents are walking-in.

4704.new_note: *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:1). *But Yahusha (Jesus) said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 19:14). Sirach's picture of safety is children who hear their father and do what he says. Yahusha (Jesus) says the kingdom of heaven is of such, and he says it while his own disciples are forbidding the little ones to come. The kingdom belongs to children not because children are innocent but because a child hears his father's voice and comes when he is called; that is the disposition the kingdom is made of. Hearing is how the Father's children are shown to be his, and the one who hears and does thereafter is the one Sirach says will be safe.
4704.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:1 — *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter.* The children who come when called, of whom the kingdom is, at Matthew 19:14.
4704.old_note: *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct opening of the children-hearing-the-father substance — the kingdom-citizens' child-substance-disposition the King names at Matt 19:14's *suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.* The framework reads the verse against the four-fold-child-substance the King had unpacked at Matthew 18:1-5 — humility, receptiveness, dependence, honesty. The wisdom-stream-substance of children-hearing-the-father is the substance the kingdom-citizen-disposition walks-in: hearing the Father, doing thereafter. The framework reads in continuity with the cause-and-effect-of-hearing per Red Line #11 — *if you hear, you are sons of Avraham (Abraham); you are sons of Adam; you are the seed of promise.* Hearing reveals what was always true. The kingdom-citizens' child-substance is the substance-that-hears the Father's-substance when the Father's-substance speaks. The framework reads this NOT as original-innocence-by-default per the institutional-Christian-tradition (which the Tanakh-and-the-King do not name) BUT as the disposition-substance the four-fold-child-substance carries.

4705.new_note: *And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.* (Tobit 4:3). *And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.* (Matthew 19:15). Tobit calls his son to him before he dies and hands him the commandments — honour your mother, bury me, walk uprightly — which is a father's blessing in the old form. Parents brought their children to Yahusha (Jesus) and he laid his hands on them. The library shows a father passing covenant life to the next generation; the gospel shows the King receiving the children their parents bring to him. The two belong together at the household, where the covenant has always been handed down.
4705.member_note: Tobit 4:3 — *My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother.* A father handing covenant life to his son; the King laying hands on the children brought to him (Matthew 19:15).
4705.reason: Thin pairing. The old note was mostly padding (Genesis 48, Numbers 6) around a weak link between Tobit 4:3 and Matthew 19:15; I kept the only real thread, a father blessing his son with instruction and parents bringing children to the King for blessing. Consider whether this card should stand at all.
4705.old_note: *And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.* Tobit 4:3 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the paternal-instruction-substance the substance of children-honoring-parents the Decalogue-fifth-commandment (Shemot (Exodus) 20:12, Devarim (Deuteronomy) 5:16) names. The framework reads the verse against Matt 19:15's *and he laid his hands on them, and departed thence* — the King performs the substance the parents had brought their children for. The Tanakh-paternal-blessing-substance of Bereshit (Genesis) 48's Ya'aqov (Jacob)-laying-hands-on-the-sons-of-Yoseph (Joseph) and the priestly-blessing-substance of Numbers 6:24-26 is the substance the King-enacts at the laying-on-of-hands. 4706.new_note: *Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:11). *And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.* (Matthew 19:17). Being created does not make a man one of the few, and neither does being called. Hearing and keeping do, and those come from what he already was.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 20:16's *many be called, but few chosen.* The substance the wisdom-stream names is NOT the Reformed-eternal-security-without-the-walking, which would collapse the substance into the Father-unilaterally-saves-from-the-foundation-without-the-disposition-walked; NOR is it the Arminian-perfectability-by-effort, which would collapse the substance into the citizen-saves-himself-by-walking. The substance is the cause-and-effect-of-hearing per Red Line #11 — the *few* are the ones whose names-were-written-in-the-Book-of-Life-from-the-foundation-of-the-world AND who hear-because-they-are-sheep AND who walk-the-substance-of-the-fruit-bearing the post-harvest-sifting tests-for. Names get blotted-out at the post-harvest-sifting for lawlessness; the warning is to wheat, not to tares. The *few-saved* is the substance of the wheat-that-bears-fruit-and-is-not-blotted-out, not the tares-that-were-never-written.

4730.new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.* (Matthew 20:22). James and John asked for thrones and were handed a cup. Yahusha (Jesus) asked whether they could drink what he was about to drink, and they said they could, not knowing what they were agreeing to. James was put to the sword by Herod (Acts 12:2); John outlived them all and was on Patmos for the testimony. The cup was real suffering, and Wisdom tells where it ends: the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there no torment touches them. James drank the cup to the bottom and lies down in that hand, kept and asleep until the Father raises him; the sword reached his body and could not follow him there.

4731.new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* (Matthew 20:23). The sons of Zebedee asked for the seats; the King promised them the cup. They would drink what he drank and be baptized with what he was baptized with, and the seats would be the Father's to assign. Wisdom puts the order the same way: the righteous man's labours are made no account of first, and the standing in great boldness comes after. The cup is the afflicting; the boldness before the afflicters is what follows it, and who sits where on that day is in the Father's hand, not seized along the road.

4732.new_note: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). *And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* (Matthew 20:23). The righteous live for evermore and their reward is with Yahuah (God). It is kept in his hand, which is what the King tells the sons of Zebedee when they ask for the seats: to sit at his right hand and his left is not his to give, it is given to those for whom it is prepared of his Father. The reward is real and it is the Father's to give. It is not seized by flesh and it is not handed out regardless of the walk; it is held for the righteous by the one who sees their labours when no one else does.

4733.new_note: *But I, as my brothers, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers, beseeching Yahuah (God) that he would speedily be merciful to our nation; and that you by torments and plagues may confess, that he alone is Yahuah (God);* (2 Maccabees 7:37). *But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.* (Matthew 20:22). The youngest brother offers his body and life for the laws of his fathers and prays that in him and his brothers the wrath on the nation would cease (2 Maccabees 7:38). When James and John ask for the chief seats, Yahusha (Jesus) asks whether they can drink the cup he is about to drink, and they say they are able. The brothers under Antiochus had drunk a cup like that, giving their lives for the Torah and for mercy on their people. Only the King's cup carries the remission of sins; his death is the one no martyr could die. But the cost of following him is real, and the seven brothers show what the sons of Zebedee were agreeing to, James by the sword (Acts 12:2) and John in exile on Patmos (Revelation 1:9).

4738.new_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;* (Matthew 20:26). The kingdoms of the world run on domination; Yahusha (Jesus) has just said so of the princes of the Gentiles, and then he says it shall not be so among you. Whoever will be great among you, let him be your minister, the one who waits the table. Sirach had set the same direction centuries earlier: the greater you are, the more humble yourself, and favour before Yahuah (God) follows the humbling. In the kingdom greatness flows downward into service, the exact reverse of the kingdoms around it, and the Messiah is not introducing that reversal; he is restoring what the fathers had already taught and then living it out with a towel.

4744.new_note: *Therefore they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms to him that had given them good success in cleansing his place.* (2 Maccabees 10:7). *And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.* (Matthew 21:8). When the temple was cleansed, the people carried branches and fair boughs and palms and sang psalms to the one who had given them success in cleansing his place, keeping eight days with gladness like the feast of tabernacles (2 Maccabees 10:6). When Yahusha (Jesus) rode into Jerusalem, the multitude cut down branches and strewed them in the way and cried Hosanna from Psalm 118, and the next thing he did was walk into the temple and cleanse it. Branches, psalms, and a cleansed temple belong together in both books. The people at the gate were doing what their fathers had done after Judas's victory, whether they knew it or not, and the King they welcomed went straight to his Father's house as the Maccabees had gone to theirs.

4746.new_note: *Who cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place.* (1 Maccabees 4:43). *And Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God), and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,* (Matthew 21:12). The priests Judas chose carried the defiled stones out of the sanctuary to an unclean place. Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God) and carried out the sellers, the buyers, the tables, and the seats. What defiled the house in Judas's day was an idol the Greeks had set on the altar; what defiled it in the King's day was trade the priesthood had set in the court of prayer. Both were put out. Cleansing the sanctuary is what faithful men do when the house of Yahuah (God) has been made to serve something other than him.

4747.new_note: *And having cleansed the temple they made another altar, and striking stones they took fire out of them, and offered a sacrifice after two years, and set forth incense, and lights, and shewbread.* (2 Maccabees 10:3). *And Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God), and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,* (Matthew 21:12). Judas and his men cleansed what Antiochus had defiled: they pulled down the heathen altars, built a new altar, struck fresh fire from stones, and brought back the sacrifice, the incense, the lamps, and the shewbread after two years without them. Yahusha (Jesus) also walked into the temple and cleansed it, but the defilement he drove out had not come from a foreign king. It came from the house's own leadership, who had let the courts become a market, and he answered them with Jeremiah's words: *My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves* (Matthew 21:13; Jeremiah 7:11). The Maccabees cleansed the temple of a defilement pressed on it from outside; the King cleansed it of the one that grew up inside, in the very priesthood their victory had restored. Both cleansings say the same thing about whose house it is.
4747.member_note: 2 Maccabees 10:3 — *having cleansed the temple they made another altar.* The temple cleansed of a defilement from outside; the King cleansed it from inside (Matthew 21:12).

The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:12's temple-cleansing substance. The substance the King-walks-against is not the Antiochene-outer-defilement but the Pharisaic-Sadducean-inner-corruption — the substance Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 7:11 had-named at the First-Temple-pivot when the leadership-substance trusted-in-the-Temple while-walking-against the covenant. 4748.new_note: *Do not think to corrupt with gifts; for such he will not receive: and trust not to unrighteous sacrifices; for Yahuah (God) is judge, and with him is no respect of persons.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:12). *And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.* (Matthew 21:13). Sirach says do not think to corrupt Yahuah (God) with gifts, for he will not take them, and do not trust in unrighteous sacrifices, for he is judge and shows no favour to persons. Yahusha (Jesus) walked into the temple courts and found the house of prayer turned into a den of thieves; the gifts and the sacrifices had become a trade. The leaders who ran that trade trusted that the sacrifices would still cover them. Sirach had already told them the judge does not take bribes, and the King overturning the tables was the judge saying it in person.

4749.new_note: *And laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.* (1 Maccabees 4:46). *And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.* (Matthew 21:13). Judas's priests did not know what to do with the stones of the profaned altar, so they laid them up on the temple mount until a prophet should come to say. Yahusha (Jesus) came into that temple as the prophet the crowds had just named him, the prophet of Nazareth (Matthew 21:11), and the word he gave about the house was from the prophets already written: it is written, my house shall be called the house of prayer. The Maccabees waited for a prophet to tell them what the house required. When he came, he told them, and what it required was that it be a house of prayer and not a den of thieves.

4750.new_note: *For though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:4). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Wisdom describes the brood of the ungodly as branches that flourish for a while with nothing under them; the wind shakes them and finally roots them out. Yahusha (Jesus) came to a fig tree in full leaf, found no fruit, and it withered. Leaves without fruit is the same picture as branches without roots — a show of life with nothing feeding it. The tree stands for the religious leadership of that day, which had the look of the covenant and none of its fruit; it does not stand for the people of Yashar'el (Israel) as a whole. What flourishes without a root does not stand when the wind comes.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:19's *he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only.* The wisdom-stream-substance the Wisdom of Solomon 4 passage walks is the substance-of-the-ungodly-substance's-branches that-flourish-for-a-time but-have-no-standing-because-the-root-is-not-there. 4751.new_note: *The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yes, meet for nothing.* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:5). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Wisdom is describing branches that flourish for a season, bear nothing worth eating, and are broken off. The fig tree the King met on the road the morning after he cleansed the Temple was all leaves and no fruit, and he spoke its end on the spot. The tree was not the people of Yashar'el (Israel); it was the leadership standing in that Temple with every show of foliage and nothing to feed anyone, the same men he answers with seven woes in Matthew 23 before the week is out. The test he had already given his disciples was fruit, not leaves (Matthew 7:16), and Solomon had written the same verdict long before.

4752.new_note: *Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:25). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Sirach says of the adulterous woman that her children will not take root and her branches will bring forth no fruit — what grows from unfaithfulness has nothing underneath it, and nothing comes of it. Yahusha (Jesus) came to the fig tree, found leaves and no fruit, and spoke the same sentence over it: let no fruit grow on you from now on. The tree stands for the leadership that held the vineyard in trust and gave the Father leaves instead of fruit, as the parable of the husbandmen later in the same chapter says plainly. No root, no fruit, and then no fruit forever — the judgment reads the same in both books.

4754.new_note: *But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:24). *He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.* (Matthew 21:29). Sirach says Yahuah (God) grants return to them that repent and comforts those who failed in patience. The first son in the parable said I will not, then repented and went — and he is the one who did the father's will. The publicans and harlots Yahusha (Jesus) names a few lines later walked the same road: a no at first, and then a return. Return is granted to the one who turns, not to the one who said the right word and stayed where he was.

4755.new_note: *Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:28). *And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.* (Matthew 21:30). The second son in the parable says yes with his mouth and no with his feet. Sirach had already named that man: the one who comes to Yahuah (God) with a double heart, one heart for what he says and another for what he does. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the parable to the chief priests and elders, who had answered the Father's call through John with the words of obedience and none of the walking, and the double heart is what he is exposing. A yes that does not go is not a weaker obedience; it is the thing Sirach warns against, and the Father does not receive it.

4756.new_note: *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:29). *And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.* (Matthew 21:30). Sirach's warning is against being a hypocrite in the sight of men, and against careless speech, and the second son in the parable fails both at once. He speaks the right words, I go, sir, where men can hear them, and then does not go. Yahusha (Jesus) is telling the parable to the chief priests and elders, who had given the Father the public yes and withheld the obedience, which is hypocrisy as Sirach defines it: a performance for the watching crowd with nothing behind it. Take good heed what you speak, Sirach says, because the Father holds a man to what his mouth promised.

4757.new_note: *My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:1). *For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.* (Matthew 21:32). Sirach opens the chapter with the whole of repentance in one line: stop doing it, and ask pardon for what is past. That is what John came preaching in the wilderness, and Yahusha (Jesus) names who actually did it — the publicans and the harlots believed him and turned, while the chief priests and elders saw it and repented not. The ones with the least standing walked Sirach's counsel; the ones holding the office refused it. Sonship is shown by the turning, not by the title.

4758.new_note: *And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it;* (2 Esdras 9:11). *For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.* (Matthew 21:32). The Most High describes those who loathed his law while they still had liberty, while a place of repentance stood open to them, and despised it. The chief priests and elders are told the same about themselves: John came in the way of righteousness, which is the law's own way, and they did not believe him, and even after watching publicans and harlots repent they did not repent afterward. The open place of repentance was John at the Jordan; they walked past it. Ezra's lament and the King's rebuke describe the same men in the same posture.

4759.new_note: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* (2 Esdras 1:32). *And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.* (Matthew 21:35). Yahuah (God) says he sent his servants the prophets and the people took them, slew them, and tore their bodies in pieces, and he will require their blood. In the parable the husbandmen take the owner's servants and beat one, kill another, and stone another. The servants are the prophets, the husbandmen are the men set over the vineyard, and the owner who sent them is going to require the blood. The parable is not a new story; the King is telling the leadership of his day the history already written against their fathers, and daring them to finish it.

4760.new_note: *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* (2 Esdras 1:33). *And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.* (Matthew 21:39). The sentence in 2 Esdras follows directly on the slaying of the prophets: your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble. The parable follows the same order. After the servants are beaten and killed the son is sent, and the husbandmen cast him out of the vineyard and slay him, and the King asks his hearers what the owner will do to them. The desolate house is the answer. Killing the prophets brought the sentence near; killing the son brought it down, and within a generation not one stone of that house was left on another.

4762.new_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of Elohim (God) shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.* (Matthew 21:43). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the chief priests the kingdom will be taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth its fruits; a nation, one, not the nations. That one nation is the gathered tribes of Jacob bearing fruit, the very people Sirach prayed for. It is not the church put in the place of Yashar'el (Israel), and it is not whoever keeps Torah regardless of seed; it is Jacob's own tribes, gathered home and bearing the fruit their leaders in that day would not bring.
4762.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *inherit you them, as from the beginning.* The one nation bringing forth fruit (Matthew 21:43) is the gathered tribes of Jacob, not a replacement.
