The substance is-substantial — the wisdom-stream had-prayed-the-Father-for the substance the King-walks-out at v.43; the substance the apostolic-witness carries-forward at Matt 19:28's *twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el* + Acts 26:6-7's *twelve tribes, instantly serving Elohim (God) day and night, hope to come* + James 1:1's *to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad* + Revelation 7:4-8's twelve-tribes-sealed + Revelation 21:12-14's twelve-gates-of-the-twelve-tribes + Ephesians 2:20's apostolic-foundation + 1 Peter 2:9-10's holy-*ethnos* singular addressed to the *strangers scattered* — IS the substance the wisdom-stream had-named, the substance the framework reads at-the-Red-Line-#11-load-bearing-anchor.

4763.new_note: *Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God);* (2 Esdras 2:38). *Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.* (Matthew 22:9). Esdras is told to stand and look at the number of those sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God). In the parable the first guests would not come, so the king sends his servants into the highways to bid as many as they find to the marriage. The ones found on the highways are not strangers to the king; they are the scattered children whose number he already knows, sealed before the servants ever went out. The feast of Yahuah (God) in 2 Esdras and the marriage in Matthew are the same table, and the guests are gathered in from wherever they were scattered.
4763.member_note: 2 Esdras 2:38 — *behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God).* The servants sent into the highways gather them to the marriage (Matthew 22:9).
4763.old_note: *Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God).* 2 Esdras 2:38 names the direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the gathered-to-the-feast substance — the *number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God)*. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:9's *go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.* The highways-and-hedges-gathering the king-substance sends-the-servants-into is the wisdom-stream's sealed-in-the-feast-of-Yahuah substance — the gathering of the scattered-seed of the twelve-tribes per Red Line #11's ingathering architecture the prophet Hoshea (Hosea) at Hosea 1:9-10, the prophet Yeshayahu (Isaiah) at Isaiah 11:11-12, the prophet Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) at Ezekiel 37:21, and the prophet Zecharyah (Zechariah) at Zechariah 10:8-10 had named. The substance is NOT the categorically-unrelated-nations-grafted-into-the-tree-by-faith-confession substance the inherited-Christian-replacement-theology had collapsed-the-substance-into; the substance is the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the sealed-citizens-of-the-kingdom gathered-to-the-Father's-feast.

4764.new_note: *I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* (2 Esdras 2:42). *So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.* (Matthew 22:10). Esdras sees on mount Sion a great people he could not number, all praising Yahuah (God) with songs. The parable ends with the wedding furnished with guests, gathered from the highways, both bad and good. John saw the same crowd in Revelation 7, a great multitude no man could number, out of all nations. Esdras saw the gathered on the mountain, the parable shows the gathering on the roads, and the next verse in each shows the King coming among them to see who is wearing what.
4764.member_note: 2 Esdras 2:42 — *a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* The wedding furnished with guests (Matthew 22:10) is the same gathered crowd.
4764.old_note: *I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* 2 Esdras 2:42 names the wisdom-stream's vision of the great-people-upon-the-mount-Tsion (Sion) substance — the gathered-multitude at the Father's-feast. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:10's *and the wedding was furnished with guests.* The wedding-feast filled-with-guests at the king's-table is the wisdom-stream's great-people-upon-the-mount-Tsion-substance — the gathered-citizens of the kingdom the framework reads through the apostle Yochanan (John) at Revelation 7:9-17's *a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues* (the gathered-from-the-scattering substance per Red Line #11, NOT the gathered-from-categorically-unrelated-peoples substance). The wisdom-stream and the apostolic-vision cohere at the gathered-multitude-on-Sion architecture the King's wedding-feast-parable walks-out.

4765.new_note: *And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted; which I marvelled at greatly.* (2 Esdras 2:43). *And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:* (Matthew 22:11). In the midst of the gathered crowd on mount Sion a young man taller than all the rest sets a crown on every head, and the angel tells Esdras a few verses on that this is the Son of Elohim (God) whom they confessed in the world. In the parable the king comes in to see the guests and finds a man with no wedding garment. Both scenes have the King walking among the gathered, and in both what he does depends on what they are wearing; in 2 Esdras the verses before say the gathered have received glorious garments, and these receive crowns. The man without the garment at the marriage receives nothing and is put out. The garment is the righteousness of the saints, and the King himself inspects it.
4765.member_note: 2 Esdras 2:43 — *upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted.* The king came in to see the guests and found one without a wedding garment (Matthew 22:11).
4765.old_note: *And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted.* 2 Esdras 2:43 names the wisdom-stream's direct vision of the young-man-of-high-stature setting-crowns-upon-the-gathered substance — the Messianic-figure crowning the citizens at the Father's-feast. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:11's *when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment.* The king-substance walking-among-the-guests at the wedding-feast is the wisdom-stream's young-man-of-high-stature among-the-gathered. 2 Esdras 2:43 articulates the substance the gospel-wedding-feast walks at the historical-pivot — the Messianic-king walks-among the gathered-citizens and the substance-walked-with reveals the substance-walked-without (the man-without-the-garment receives no crown; the citizens-walking-in-the-righteousness-of-saints per Revelation 19:8 receive crowns).

4766.new_note: *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:16). *And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.* (Matthew 22:12). The guest came in without a wedding garment and had nothing to say. Wisdom shows what the garment was for: those who receive a glorious kingdom and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God) receive them clothed. The fine linen of the bride is the righteousness of saints (Revelation 19:8), granted to her and then worn, and the man at the feast had neither put it on nor walked in it. The crown is given from the Father's hand to those who came dressed for the feast; the one who came in his own clothes receives the silence and the door.
4766.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 — *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God).* The man without a wedding garment (Matthew 22:12) has no crown to receive; the kingdom and the crown go to those clothed for the feast.
4766.old_note: *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the glorious-kingdom-and-beautiful-crown the righteous-citizen receives from-the-hand-of-Yahuah. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:12's *friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.* The wedding-garment-substance the king-substance categorically-requires is the substance the citizen-walking-in-the-righteousness-of-saints (Revelation 19:8) walks-in; the beautiful-crown of Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 is the substance received-from-the-Father's-hand for the substance walked-out. The man-without-the-garment has-no-crown to receive because the substance-walked-into-the-feast was not the substance-the-feast-was-meant-to-be-walked-in; the speechless-substance at the king's-question pre-figures the system's-substance-silenced at v.46 (*no man was able to answer him a word*). The wisdom-stream had named the garment-and-crown architecture centuries before the wedding-feast-parable walks-it-out at the historical-pivot.

4767.new_note: *He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image,* (Ecclesiasticus 17:3). *And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?* (Matthew 22:20). Sirach says the Maker made men according to his image, with strength of their own, carrying Genesis 1 forward. Yahusha (Jesus) held up the coin and asked whose image and superscription it bore. The coin bears Caesar's image and goes back to Caesar; the man bears the Father's image and belongs to the Father. The question about the tribute was a question about ownership, and Sirach had already said who stamped the man.
4767.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 17:3 — *made them according to his image.* The image stamped on man is the image the King asks about at Matthew 22:20.
4767.old_note: *He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:3 names the direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the image-of-Elohim-stamped-on-man substance — Sirach 17 carries the Bereshit (Genesis) 1:26-27 creation-substance forward at the wisdom-stream-register, articulating the substance-of-the-citizen-of-the-covenant bearing-the-Father's-image the same way the coin bears Caesar's. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:20's *whose is this image and superscription?* The Greek *eikōn* the King uses is the same Septuagint-Greek the Genesis 1:26-27 creation-substance carries and the apostle Sha'ul (Paul) uses of the Son-substance at Colossians 1:15 (*the image of the invisible Elohim (God)*) and of the citizen at Romans 8:29 (*conformed to the image of his Son*). The image-architecture the King invokes at the tribute-coin is the substance Sirach 17:3 had named the wisdom-stream-substance for; what is stamped with the Father's-image belongs to the Father.

4768.new_note: *Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:11). *They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God’s).* (Matthew 22:21). Sirach says the law of life was given as an heritage — set on the people along with the image. Yahusha (Jesus) says to render to Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God's). What is Elohim's (God's) is what he put on the man: his image, and the law he gave for the man's inheritance. Rendering it back is not a burden laid on a free man; it is the heir keeping his inheritance.
4768.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 17:11 — *he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* The law of life given as heritage is among the things that are Elohim's (God's) at Matthew 22:21.
4768.old_note: *Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the law-of-life-for-an-heritage substance — the Torah given to the citizen-stamped-with-the-Father's-image as the inheritance, the substance Sirach 17:12 continues at *he made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments* and Sirach 24:23 names as *all these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Ya'aqov (Jacob).* The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:21's *render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God's).* The substance the citizen renders-back-to-the-Father is the substance the Father stamped-the-citizen-with — the image, and the law-of-life-for-an-heritage Sirach 17:11 names the wisdom-stream-substance for. Per Red Line #4: Torah is NOT the curse but the covenant-inheritance the Father stamped on the citizen; per the framework's reading of grace-as-return-to-the-way, the citizen-rendering-back-to-the-Father walks the heart-Torah of Jeremiah 31:31-34 and Ezekiel 36:26-27 from the inside.

4769.new_note: *For Yahuah (God) created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:23). *And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?* (Matthew 22:20). Yahusha (Jesus) asked whose image was on the coin, and the answer settled where the coin belonged. Wisdom tells us whose image is on the man: Yahuah (God) made him an image of his own eternity. Caesar's stamp is on the money, so the money goes back to Caesar; the Father's stamp is on the one holding it, so the one holding it goes back to the Father. The coin is perishable and so is its owner. The man was made for immortality, and the image he bears tells him whose he is.
4769.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:23 — *made him to be an image of his own eternity.* Caesar's image is on the coin (Matthew 22:20); the Father's image is on the man who holds it.
4769.old_note: *For Yahuah (God) created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:23 names the wisdom-stream's direct verbal-anchor for the image-of-Elohim-as-image-of-his-own-eternity substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:20's *whose is this image and superscription?* The image-architecture the King invokes at the tribute-coin operates at two-registers-at-once: the Caesar-coin bears Caesar's perishable-image; the citizen-of-the-kingdom bears the image-of-Elohim's-own-eternity. The Caesar-coin returns to Caesar; the citizen-stamped-with-the-image-of-his-own-eternity returns to the Father who-stamped-him with the substance Wisdom of Solomon 2:23 names the wisdom-stream-substance for. The framework reads this in continuity with John 1:18's *no man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him* — the citizen-stamped-with-the-image is being-conformed-to-the-image-of-the-Son the apostle Sha'ul (Paul) names at Romans 8:29, the substance walked-out from the Formless-Source through the Formed-Expression into the citizen-of-the-kingdom.

4770.new_note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). *They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God’s).* (Matthew 22:21). Caesar's face on the coin makes the coin Caesar's. Solomon's prayer tells you what makes everything else the Father's: he made all things with his word, and the next verse adds that he ordained man through his wisdom to rule over what was made. So when the King says render unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God's), the things in question are all things, man first, because man carries the Maker's image the way the denarius carries Caesar's. The Word the Father made all things with is the one standing in the court holding the coin and asking whose image is on it.
4770.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *who have made all things with your word.* Render unto Elohim (God) the things that are his (Matthew 22:21): all things, since he made them all with his word.
4770.old_note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word.* Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the made-all-things-with-thy-word substance — the same substance the apostle Yochanan (John) walks at John 1:1-3 (*in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God) ... all things were made by him*). The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:21's *unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God's).* The substance-the-Father-claims is the substance-the-Father-made-with-his-Word; the Word-through-whom-all-things-were-made is the Formed-Expression the framework's nature-of-God reading names (the Son who-spoke-at-creation, who-spoke-at-Sinai, who-spoke-from-the-bright-cloud at the transfiguration, who-walks-the-tribute-question at the Temple-court). The substance Caesar-stamped belongs to Caesar; the substance the Father-and-the-Son-made-together belongs to the Father — and the Father-and-the-Son are substantially-one in the Source-and-Expression substance the next thread's Psalm 110-architecture walks-out at the framework-major level.

4771.new_note: *And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.* (2 Maccabees 7:9). *Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 22:29). The second of the seven brothers, dying under Antiochus for refusing to break the Torah, said with his last breath that the King of the world would raise him up to everlasting life. He did not hold a philosophy about the afterlife; he held a hope in the resurrection, and he paid for it with his body. When the Sadducees, who said there is no resurrection (Acts 23:8), came to trap Yahusha (Jesus), he told them they erred because they knew neither the scriptures nor the power of Elohim (God). The brothers in 2 Maccabees 7 knew both. The resurrection the King defended in the temple was the resurrection a family had already confessed under torture, for his laws.
4771.member_note: 2 Maccabees 7:9 — *the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.* The resurrection confessed in blood; the Sadducees erred, not knowing the power of Elohim (God) (Matthew 22:29).
4771.old_note: *And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.* 2 Maccabees 7:9 names THE direct wisdom-and-martyrdom-stream verbal-anchor for the resurrection-of-the-righteous substance — the second son of the mother-and-seven-sons-substance under Antiochus Epiphanes confessing-the-King-of-the-world-shall-raise-us-up before-dying-for-his-laws. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:29's *ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of Elohim (God).* The Sadducean-substance categorically-denies the resurrection (Acts 23:8); the wisdom-and-martyrdom-substance of 2 Maccabees 7 articulates the resurrection-doctrine at the strongest external-witness-register the Second-Temple-period produced — seven sons and their mother dying-for-the-Torah confessing-the-King-of-the-world-shall-raise-us-up to-everlasting-life. The substance the King defends at vv.23-33 is the substance the wisdom-and-martyrdom-stream had already-confessed at the cost-of-blood centuries before the Sadducean-trap-question.

4772.new_note: *But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as you now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.* (2 Maccabees 7:23). *I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* (Matthew 22:32). The mother tells her sons where life comes from: she did not give them breath, the Creator did, and the one who formed man at the beginning can give breath and life again. That is her whole comfort as they die. Yahusha (Jesus) makes the same argument from the same ground: Elohim (God) names himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and he is not the Elohim (God) of the dead but of the living, so the fathers must rise. Neither the mother nor the King speaks of souls already in heaven; both look to the Creator giving breath again to those who sleep. The seven sons and their mother lie down in that hope, waiting with the fathers for the day their breath is given back.
4772.member_note: 2 Maccabees 7:23 — *will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again.* The Creator gives breath again; Elohim (God) of the living, not of the dead (Matthew 22:32).
4772.old_note: *But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as you now regard not your own selves for his laws' sake.* 2 Maccabees 7:23 names the wisdom-and-martyrdom-stream's direct articulation of the Creator-shall-give-breath-and-life-again substance — the mother of the seven sons confessing the resurrection-doctrine to her sons in their hearing as they die. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:32's *I am the Elohim (God) of Avraham (Abraham), and the Elohim (God) of Yitschaq (Isaac), and the Elohim (God) of Ya'aqov (Jacob); Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* The King's-citation of Exodus 3:6 walks the same substance the mother-of-the-seven-sons walks at 2 Maccabees 7:23 — the Creator who-formed-the-generation-of-man will-give-breath-and-life-again because the substance-of-the-Father-relating-to-the-patriarchs-and-the-citizens is the substance-of-the-living. The framework reads the asleep-awaiting-the-first-resurrection substance through this anchor — the patriarchs and the seven martyred-sons-and-their-mother are asleep, awaiting the Father's-substance to give-breath-and-life-again, NOT the inherited-Christian immediate-disembodied-soul-going-to-heaven-or-hell-at-death substance the modern-Christian-pulpit had collapsed-the-grief-substance-of-the-citizen-into.

4774.new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* (Matthew 22:32). Read this verse with the rest of its chapter and it is not souls flying off to heaven. The righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God) — kept, at rest, waiting; a few verses on, *in the time of their visitation they shall shine* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7), and that visitation has not come yet. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead but of the living. The fathers are asleep and held, and the Father counts them living because he is going to raise them. That is why Paul can tell the grieving not to sorrow as those who have no hope (1 Thessalonians 4:13), and it is the only reason.
4774.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* Kept and asleep, not in heaven now — the living Abraham, Isaac and Jacob of Matthew 22:32, held for the resurrection.
4774.old_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the souls-of-the-righteous-in-the-hand-of-Yahuah substance — read carefully through the framework, this is the asleep-in-the-Father's-keeping substance, the substance-of-the-Father-holding-the-citizens-He-will-raise, NOT the inherited-Christian immediate-conscious-disembodied-soul-going-to-heaven substance the Wisdom of Solomon 3 surrounding-context (vv.7-8 — *and in the time of their visitation they shall shine ... they shall judge the nations*) makes plain belongs to the resurrection-day-substance not to the immediate-after-death-substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:32's *Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* The Father-relating-to-the-asleep-as-the-living is the substance Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 names — the souls-of-the-righteous-are-in-the-hand-of-Yahuah because the Father holds-them-for-the-resurrection-day, the substance the citizen-of-the-kingdom can grieve-with-hope (*not as others which have no hope,* the apostle Sha'ul (Paul) at 1 Thessalonians 4:13) but should not grieve with the inherited-Christian collapsed-into-immediate-disembodied-substance.

4775.new_note: *Love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:30). *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God) with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.* (Matthew 22:37). Sirach is carrying the Shema forward: love him that made you with all your strength, the strength Deuteronomy 6:5 names and that Yahusha (Jesus) renders heart, soul, and mind when he gives the great commandment in Matthew 22:37. The Messiah is not replacing the commandments with love; he is quoting the commandment, the same one Sirach's readers recited twice a day. Sirach's next clause keeps love and Torah together, forsake not his ministers, and the verses around it give the priests their portion as it is commanded; loving Yahuah (God) with all your strength shows up as keeping what he commanded. That is the love written on the heart the prophets promised, not a feeling that excuses the walk.
4775.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 7:30 — *Love him that made you with all your strength.* The Shema the Messiah quotes at Matthew 22:37, carried forward by Sirach.
4775.old_note: *Love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:30 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the love-Yahuah-with-all-thy-strength substance — Sirach 7:30 carries the Shema-substance of Devarim (Deuteronomy) 6:5 forward at the wisdom-stream-register, articulating the love-him-that-made-you-with-all-your-strength substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:37's *thou shalt love Yahuah (the LORD) thy Elohim (God) with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.* The King's-citation of the Shema is the substance the wisdom-stream had already-articulated at Sirach 7:30 — the love-Yahuah-with-all-thy-strength substance the Father called-the-citizen-to walk-out twice-daily in the substance-of-the-Shema-recitation. The substance is NOT the post-Reformation collapse-of-the-commandments-into-replacement-of-the-Torah; the substance is the heart-Torah of Jeremiah 31:31-34 + Ezekiel 36:26-27 walked-out from-the-inside through the Spirit-internalized-substance.

4776.new_note: *And he said to them, Beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:14). *And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.* (Matthew 22:39). Sirach says the commandment concerning the neighbour was given to every man, in the same breath as the warning against all unrighteousness — this is Sinai, where their eyes saw his glory and their ears heard his voice. When Yahusha (Jesus) names the second great commandment he is quoting the Torah, the commandment Sirach is describing. The King added nothing. He put his finger on what was given at the beginning.
4776.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 17:14 — *he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.* The commandment concerning the neighbour is the second great commandment of Matthew 22:39.
4776.old_note: *And he said to them, Beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:14 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the commandment-concerning-the-neighbor substance — Sirach 17:14 carries the Vayikra (Leviticus) 19:18 love-thy-neighbor substance forward at the wisdom-stream-register, naming the architecture explicitly as the Father giving-every-man-commandment-concerning-his-neighbor. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:39's *and the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.* The King's-citation of Leviticus 19:18 is the substance the wisdom-stream had already-articulated at Sirach 17:14 — the every-man-commandment-concerning-his-neighbor substance the Father walked-into the substance-of-the-Torah from-the-beginning. The substance is NOT the modern-liberal categorically-universal-neighbor collapse the Lukan Good Samaritan parable is sometimes pressed-into; the substance is the substance-of-the-covenant-fellow-citizen plus-the-stranger-who-joins-the-covenant (Leviticus 19:34) plus-the-substance-of-mercy-walked-where-the-substance-of-need-is-encountered.

4777.new_note: *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:2). *And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.* (Matthew 22:39). Sirach says forgive your neighbour the hurt he did you, and your own sins will be forgiven. Yahusha (Jesus) names the second great commandment as love your neighbour as yourself, quoting Leviticus 19:18, and that verse in the Torah begins by forbidding vengeance and grudges before it ever says love. Forgiving the hurt is what loving the neighbour looks like when he has wronged you. Sirach is not adding to the commandment; he is reading it, and the King's answer to the lawyer stands on the same verse.

4778.new_note: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:7). *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* (Matthew 22:40). When Yahusha (Jesus) says all the law and the prophets hang on loving Yahuah (God) and loving your neighbour, he is doing the same thing, not the opposite: he is saying what the whole Torah is for, not cutting it down to two lines. A man cannot hang a coat on a peg and then throw the coat away. Remember the commandments, and the love of the neighbour is what keeping them looks like; the heart Jeremiah 31:33 and Ezekiel 36:26–27 promise is the heart that does both at once.

4779.new_note: *And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption;* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:18). *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* (Matthew 22:40). Love is the keeping of her laws. The King hangs all the law and the prophets on two commandments, love of Yahuah (God) and love of neighbour, and the pulpit has used that sentence for centuries to say love replaced the law. Solomon says the opposite: love is what keeping the law looks like, and heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption. John says it the same way, that this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments (1 John 5:3). 4785.new_note: *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:14). *And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.* (Matthew 23:12). Sirach says the throne itself changes hands: the proud prince loses it and the meek receive it. Yahusha (Jesus) states the rule behind the history — exalt yourself and you are abased, humble yourself and you are exalted — and he says it in the middle of his rebuke of the scribes and Pharisees who loved the chief seats. This is not piety literature sitting beside the gospel; it is the same voice. What the Father does to kingdoms he does to men.

4786.new_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.* (Matthew 23:11). Sirach's counsel runs opposite to how religious status works: the greater you are, the more humble yourself. In Matthew 23 Yahusha (Jesus) is describing a leadership that had reversed it, loving the chief seats and the greetings and the titles, and in the middle of the woes he states the kingdom's rule: he that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Any system that climbs as it grows holy has walked Sirach backward. The favour before Yahuah (God) that Sirach promises goes to the one who goes down, and the Messiah says the same of greatness.

4787.new_note: *Seek not of Yahuah (God) preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:4). *And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,* (Matthew 23:6). Matthew 23:6 describes a religious leadership that loved exactly those things, the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues. The counsel and the woe are the same measure applied twice, once as a warning and once as a diagnosis, and the seat of honour is the tell in both. 4792.new_note: *Because, being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of Yahuah (God);* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:4). *But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.* (Matthew 23:13). 4793.new_note: *Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:9). *Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!* (Matthew 23:16). Sirach's counsel is simple: do not get your mouth used to swearing or to naming the Holy One. The tradition Yahusha (Jesus) is answering had gone the other way — it had built grades of oath, where swearing by the temple meant nothing but swearing by the gold of the temple bound you. The Torah knows no such grades; every vow binds and every oath counts. Sirach stood with the Torah on this, and the blind guides are the office that built the ladder of evasions, not the people who were taught to climb it.

4794.new_note: *A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: if he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he makes a double offence: and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:11). *And he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of Elohim (God), and by him that sitteth thereon.* (Matthew 23:22). Sirach says the man who swears much is filled with iniquity and his house is full of calamities — he takes every oath seriously, because every one of them counts. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same against the tradition that had sorted oaths into binding and empty: to swear by heaven is to swear by the throne of Elohim (God) and by him who sits on it, so there is no empty oath. Sirach and Yahusha (Jesus) stand together on the Torah here; the grading of oaths was the invention of the system, not of Moses.

4795.new_note: *The talk of him that sweareth much makes the hair stand upright; and their brawls make one stop his ears.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:14). *And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty.* (Matthew 23:18). A double heart is a clean outside and a different inside. Sirach warns the one who comes to Yahuah (God) not to come that way; Yahusha (Jesus) names the religious leadership of his day as having done exactly that, the cup scrubbed where men can see and full of extortion and excess where only Elohim (God) sees. 4804.new_note: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* (2 Esdras 1:32). *Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:* (Matthew 23:34). 4805.new_note: *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* (2 Esdras 1:33). *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38). The words are nearly the same in both books. Yahuah (God) Almighty says through Esdras, your house is desolate; Yahusha (Jesus) says in the temple, behold, your house is left unto you desolate, and walks out of it. Jeremiah had said it of the first house before Babylon burned it, and Ezekiel watched the glory leave it. Now the one whose glory it was leaves the second house on his own feet, and the house was desolate from that hour whatever the priests kept doing in it. The leadership that killed the prophets lost the house; the children the hen would have gathered are still being gathered.

4815.new_note: *Nevertheless as concerning the tokens, behold, the days shall come, that they which dwell upon earth shall be taken in a great number, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith.* (2 Esdras 5:1). *And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.* (Matthew 24:10). The first sign Esdras is given of the end is not war or famine but this: the way of truth hidden and the land barren of faith. The King gives the same sign in the same order in Matthew 24, many offended, betraying one another, hating one another, and two verses on, because lawlessness abounds the love of many grows cold. Faith does not die by itself; it dies when the way of truth, which is the law of Yahuah (God), is hidden from the people, and lawlessness fills the place it left. Esdras saw the land barren; the King explains what made it so.

4816.new_note: *But if the Most High grant you to live, you shall see after the third trumpet that the sun shall suddenly shine again in the night, and the moon thrice in the day:* (2 Esdras 5:4). *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29). Esdras is told that those who live to see it will see the sun shine in the night and the moon by day, after the third trumpet. The King says that immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give her light, and the stars will fall. The prophets had said the same of the day of Yahuah (LORD): Isaiah, Joel, Amos, Zephaniah. In both books the disordered heavens come after the trouble, not before it, and in both they are seen by people still standing on the earth. A teaching that has his people carried away before those days has to set 2 Esdras 5 and Matthew 24 both aside to stand.

4817.new_note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber,* (2 Esdras 5:9). *And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.* (Matthew 24:10). Among the signs Esdras is given is that all friends shall destroy one another. The King names the same thing among his: many shall be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. The pressure of the last days does not only come from outside; it turns friend on friend and brother on brother inside the house, and Paul tasted it when Demas forsook him and no man stood with him at his first answer. Esdras and Matthew both put the betrayal of friends on the list of signs, so the reader will not mistake it for proof that the way was wrong.

4822.new_note: *As when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remains; so the filth of man in his talk.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:4). *And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 24:51). Shake a sieve and what stays behind is the refuse; so a man's talk shows what is left in him once everything else falls through. The servant in Matthew 24 was trusted with his lord's household, and his talk and his conduct while the lord delayed showed what he was, so that when the lord came he was cut asunder and given his portion with the hypocrites. That is a sifting of the household, not of strangers; the one being sifted had been given a stewardship. Ezekiel says the same about the righteous man who turns from his righteousness, that none of his righteousness will be remembered (Ezekiel 18:24), and John the Baptist saw the fan in the Messiah's hand purging his own floor (Matthew 3:12). The sieve finds the refuse among the servants.

4829.new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:* (Matthew 25:32). Before the righteous judge the nations there is a gathering and a sorting. Yahusha (Jesus) says all nations are gathered before him and he separates them as a shepherd divides sheep from goats — the seed brought out of every nation and sifted, the way Ezekiel saw it pass under the rod. Then the sifted remnant, his brethren of Matthew 25:40, does what Wisdom says: judges the nations and has dominion over the people. Daniel saw the same order — *judgment was given to the saints of the El Elyon (most High); and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom* (Daniel 7:22). The gathering comes first, the reign after.
4829.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* The reign that follows the gathering and sorting of Matthew 25:32 — sheep from goats first, then the saints possess the kingdom.
4829.old_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the gathered-remnant judging the nations + having dominion + the kingdom-of-Yahuah-reigning-for-ever substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:32's *and before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another.* The gathering of Matt 25:32 comes first — the seed brought out of all nations and sifted, the sheep from the goats; then the gathered remnant of the seed of promise (the King's brethren of Matt 25:40), once sifted, judges the nations in the reign, as Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 had named. The Tanakh-parallel at Daniel 7:22 (*judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom*) and Daniel 7:27 (*the kingdom and dominion ... shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High*) carries the same architecture. The framework reads this in continuity with Red Line #11's destination-of-the-gathered-remnant-as-priests-to-the-nations during the millennial-reign + per Revelation 5:10 (*and hast made us unto our Elohim (God) kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth*).

4830.new_note: *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:5). *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* (Matthew 25:34). At the judgment his afflicters discover that the man they despised is numbered among the children of Yahuah (God) and has his lot among the saints. The King says where that lot came from: a kingdom prepared for the blessed from the foundation of the world. It was not assigned on the day; it was prepared before there was a world, and the day only reveals whose it was. Names were written in the Lamb's book from the foundation of the world (Revelation 13:8), and on that day the sheep hear the Shepherd say come, because they were his before they ever heard him.
4830.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:5 — *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints.* The lot among the saints is the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world (Matthew 25:34), revealed on the day, not assigned on it.
4830.old_note: *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* Wisdom of Solomon 5:5 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the children-of-Yahuah substance + the lot-among-the-saints substance — the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) declares at Matt 25:34's *Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.* The wisdom-stream had named the post-judgment-recognition-of-the-righteous at the prefiguring-register; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) speaks the operative-form at the gospel-pivot. The framework reads this in continuity with Red Line #11's names-written-in-the-Lamb's-book-from-the-foundation-of-the-world architecture per Revelation 13:8, 17:8; the lot-among-the-saints Wisdom of Solomon names is the inheritance-prepared-from-the-foundation-of-the-world the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-out. Election precedes hearing; lineage precedes response; the day-of-vindication reveals what was-true-from-before-the-creation.

4831.new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:* (Matthew 25:41). Wisdom and the King are describing the same day from two sides. On that day the righteous stand in great boldness, and the next verse in Wisdom has their afflicters troubled with terrible fear and amazed at a salvation they never looked for, which is exactly the astonishment of those on the left hand asking when they ever saw him hungry or thirsty (Matthew 25:44). Notice what the King says about the fire: it was prepared for the devil and his angels, the fallen ones Jude and Peter say are kept in chains for judgment (Jude 6; 2 Peter 2:4), and John sees the devil himself cast into that lake of fire (Revelation 20:10). The goats are sent toward a place that was not made for them. They are the unfruitful among the gathered, sifted before the reign, not the nations being judged for entry.
4831.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The day the righteous stand in boldness is the day of Matthew 25:41; the fire was prepared for the devil and his angels, and the goats are the unfruitful among the gathered.
4831.old_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the reversal-architecture of the day-of-vindication-of-the-righteous. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:41's *Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.* The day Wisdom of Solomon prefigured at the wisdom-stream-register is the day Matt 25 enacts — the righteous stand in great boldness; the ungodly are terrified and confess at vv.42-44 the same way Wisdom of Solomon 5:2-6 had named (*they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation* + *therefore have we erred from the way of truth*). The wisdom-stream had named the reversal at the prefiguring-passage centuries before; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks the operative-substance at the sheep-and-goats-judgment. The framework reads the substance carefully — the everlasting-fire was-substantively-prepared FOR-the-devil-and-his-angels (the Watcher-rebellion the apostle-Yahudah (Jude) walked at Jude 6-7 + the apostle-Kefa (Peter) walked at 2 Peter 2:4 + the apostle-Yochanan (John) walks at Revelation 20:10 + 20:14-15); the goats sent toward it are the unfruitful among the gathered, sifted before the reign — not the nations judged for entry into it.

4832.new_note: *Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.* (Ecclesiasticus 11:21). *His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* (Matthew 25:21). Sirach tells the labourer not to marvel at how sinners get on, but to trust Yahuah (God) and stay at the work, because he can make a poor man rich in a moment. The faithful servant of the parable did exactly that — did not look sideways, did not stop, traded what he was given — and heard well done. The commendation is for the faithfulness, not the size of the return; the servant with two talents heard the same words as the one with five.
4832.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 11:21 — *trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour.* Abiding in the labour is what earns well done, thou good and faithful servant at Matthew 25:21.
4832.old_note: *Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11:21 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the trust-and-abide-in-your-labour substance — the substantial-substance the faithful-servants at Matt 25:16-23 walked-out the doubling of the talents-substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:21's *Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* The faithful-servants neither marvelled at the works of the sinners-around-them nor stopped-the-labour; they abided-in-the-labour the Father-substance had-given-them, trusting the Father-substance's-knowing per Romans 12:3-8 + 1 Corinthians 12:4-11. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the abide-in-your-labour substance — the substantial-faithfulness, NOT the substantial-comparative-quantity, is the criterion of the Father-substance's-substantial-commendation.

4833.new_note: *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.* (Ecclesiasticus 22:1). *His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed:* (Matthew 25:26). Sirach's picture is blunt: a slothful man is a filthy stone, and everyone hisses him out to his disgrace. The lord in the parable is just as blunt with the servant who buried his talent — wicked and slothful, he calls him, because the servant knew what his master expected and did nothing. The fault in both is the same: not wickedness done, but the work left undone. Sloth is treated as disgrace in the wisdom book and as judgment in the parable, and it is the same sin in both.
4833.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 22:1 — *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone.* The *wicked and slothful servant* of Matthew 25:26 — the work left undone is the disgrace.
4833.old_note: *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 22:1 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the slothful-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) names at the unprofitable-servant. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:26's *Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not.* The Greek *oknēre* — slothful, hesitating, shrinking — is the operative-form of the Tanakh-and-wisdom-stream slothful-substance the prophet-Shlomo (Solomon) had walked at Proverbs 6:6-11, 13:4, 19:15, 24:30-34. Sirach 22:1 names the same architecture at the wisdom-stream-register. The substantial-substance is the substantial-failure-of-the-action — the substantial-talent was-not-substantively-put-to-work, was-not-substantively-traded; the substantial-non-action is the substantial-substance the Father-substance walks-against. The wisdom-stream had named the diagnosis; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks the operative-form at the parable.

4834.new_note: *Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.* (Ecclesiasticus 33:28). *Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.* (Matthew 25:27). Sirach's counsel for a servant is to set him to work fit for him, and if he will not obey, to bind him tighter; idleness, the verse before says, teaches much evil. The master in the parable judges his servant by the same measure. The servant was not condemned for losing the money; he was condemned for doing nothing with it, when even handing it to the exchangers would have been work enough. The one who was given a charge and buried it is the one Sirach's heavier fetters were written for.
4834.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 33:28 — *Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters..* The servant of Matthew 25:27 was judged for doing nothing with his charge.
4834.old_note: *Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 33:28 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the set-him-to-work substance — the substantial-master-substance's-substance-of-the-substantial-work the substantial-servant-substance is to-walk-out, and the substantial-substance of the consequences-for-the-substantial-failure-of-the-substantial-work-substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:27's *thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.* The Father-substance walks the substantial-minimal-stewardship-substance — even the substantial-minimal-action (the substantial-putting-of-the-money-to-the-exchangers) is the substantial-substance the substantial-action the Father-substance walks-as-the-substantial-minimum. 4835.new_note: *Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:30). *His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* (Matthew 25:23). Sirach's last word is a word about timing: do your work early, and the reward comes in his time, not yours. The faithful servant in the parable did exactly that; he worked while the master was away and was paid when the master came back, rule over many things and entry into his lord's joy. The reward is not handed out along the way. Yahusha (Jesus) says *the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works* (Matthew 16:27), and the reigning with him that follows the first resurrection is that reward (Revelation 20:4–6). The work is now; the wages are at his coming.

4835.old_note: *Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51:30 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the work-your-work-betimes substance + the substantial-reward-in-his-time substance — the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the second-faithful-servant's-substantial-commendation. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:23's *Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* The substantial-reward the substantial-faithful-servant walks-into is the substantial-substance-of-the-millennial-reign-stewardship per Revelation 2:26-27, 3:21, 5:10, 20:4-6 + the twelve-thrones the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walked at Matt 19:28 + the marriage-of-the-Lamb at Revelation 19:7-9. The substantial-substance the wisdom-stream had named at the work-your-work-betimes architecture is the substantial-substance the substantial-faithful-servants walk-into at the substantial-second-coming-substance — the substantial-substance the substantial-Father-substance gives the substantial-reward in-his-time, not-in-the-substantial-self-determined-time of-the-substantial-servant. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the work-your-work-betimes substance.

4836.new_note: *And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.* (2 Esdras 8:1). *And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.* (Matthew 25:10). Ten virgins went out to meet the bridegroom, and all ten were called to the wedding; only those who were ready went in before the door was shut. That is Ezra's answer told as a story: this world is made for many, the world to come for few. The five who found the door shut were not strangers; they were virgins with lamps who had gone out to meet him. The few are those found ready when he comes, which is why readiness matters more than having once set out.
4836.member_note: 2 Esdras 8:1 — *this world for many, but the world to come for few.* The shut door of Matthew 25:10 divides the many who set out from the few found ready.
4836.old_note: *The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 8:1 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the world-to-come-for-few substance — the substantial-substance the substantial-post-harvest-sifting-substance per Red Line #11 walks. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:10's *and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.* The substantial-shut-door is the substantial-substance the substantial-post-harvest-sifting-substance walks-with — the substantial-many-virgins (the substantial-called-substance) divide into the substantial-wise-and-foolish; the substantial-wise-five-with-oil walk-into the marriage; the substantial-foolish-five-without-oil find the substantial-shut-door. 2 Esdras 8:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the same architecture — the substantial-world-to-come is for-the-substantial-few; the substantial-many-are-called-but-the-substantial-few-are-chosen per Matt 22:14. The framework reads this carefully per Red Line #11's post-harvest-sifting architecture — the substantial-wheat-after-the-gathering is-sifted-into-wheat-and-chaff; the substantial-foolish-virgins are wheat-that-did-not-bear-the-fruit-of-readiness, NOT tares (the tares were burned at the harvest of Matt 13's wheat-and-tares).

4837.new_note: *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:3). *But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.* (Matthew 25:12). Many created, few saved: Ezra receives it as the hard rule of the age. The foolish virgins knock at the shut door and hear I know you not, the same word spoken to those who say Lord, Lord and work iniquity (Matthew 7:23). They were among the called and they were not among the few. Ezra's few saved and the bridegroom's I know you not are the two ends of one sentence.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:12's *Verily I say unto you, I know you not.* The substantial *I know you not* of the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) at the shut-door is the substantial-direct-echo of Matt 7:23's *I never knew you* — the substantial-substance the substantial-form-of-the-substantial-Lord-Lord-confession-without-the-substantial-substance-of-the-substantial-doing walks-into. The substantial-many-created walks the substantial-many-called of Matt 22:14; the substantial-few-saved walks the substantial-few-chosen of the same verse + the substantial-foolish-five who-found-the-shut-door at Matt 25:10. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the few-saved-many-lost architecture per Red Line #11.

4838.new_note: *And the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.* (2 Esdras 7:35). *And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 25:30). Ezra is told that at the judgment the work follows and the reward is shown, that good deeds are of force and wicked ones bear no rule. The servant in the parable was given a talent and called a servant; he belonged to the house. What condemned him was not that he was never the master's, but that his work did not follow, and so he is cast into the outer darkness. The warning here is to those inside the household whose deeds bore no fruit, which is why it is so sharp.
4838.member_note: 2 Esdras 7:35 — *the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.* The unprofitable servant of Matthew 25:30 was of the house, and his work did not follow him.
4838.old_note: *And the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7:35 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the work-shall-follow + the reward-shall-be-shewed substance — the substantial-substance the substantial-post-harvest-sifting-substance walks-out for-the-substantial-substance the substantial-unprofitable-servant walks-into. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:30's *And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* The substantial-substance the wisdom-stream had named at the work-shall-follow architecture is the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-out at the substantial-unprofitable-servant — the substantial-failure-of-the-work walks the substantial-substance into-the-substantial-outer-darkness. 4840.new_note: *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.* (Tobit 4:16). *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:* (Matthew 25:35). Bread to the hungry, garments to the naked, alms according to abundance, no envious eye — Tobit gives his son two of the very things the King names at the judgment: *I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat ... naked, and ye clothed me.* Isaiah had said the same, to deal bread to the hungry and cover the naked. This is not a charity program for the world in general; the King says it is mercy done to his brethren, and it is the measure by which the sheep are told from the goats. The library had been teaching that measure in the exile household all along.
4840.member_note: Tobit 4:16 — *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked.* Two of the King's own measures at the judgment, *I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat* (Matthew 25:35).

The framework reads the verse against *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat ... naked, and ye clothed me.* Tobit 4:16 names the wisdom-stream's direct verbal-anchor for two of the six-fold-criterion-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the sheep-and-goats-judgment. The wisdom-stream had named the substance the substantial Tanakh-prophets walked at Isaiah 58:6-10 (*deal thy bread to the hungry* + *when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him*) + Job 31:16-22 (*If I have seen any perish for want of clothing*) + Proverbs 19:17 (*he that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (the LORD)*) + Deuteronomy 10:18-19 (*love ye therefore the stranger*). The substantial-substance is NOT the substantial-categorical-charity-program-substance the inherited-Christian-collapse walks; the measure is mercy toward the King's brethren, the seed of promise, and it is the measure by which the gathered are sifted, the sheep from the goats, before the reign.

4841.new_note: *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:32). *Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.* (Matthew 25:36). Sirach says the hand stretched to the poor is what perfects the blessing — the blessing is not finished until it has gone out the door to someone in need. Yahusha (Jesus) sets the same thing as the measure at his judgment seat: the naked clothed, the sick visited, the prisoner visited, and he counts it as done to himself. Sirach keeps going in the next verses — be with them that weep, be not slow to visit the sick — and the list reads like the King's own. This is the fruit of the new heart Ezekiel promised, a heart that keeps his judgments because it has been made able to; a confession that never stretches out its hand has not yet been perfected into a blessing.
4841.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 7:32 — *stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* The hand stretched to the poor is the measure the King uses at Matthew 25:36.
4841.old_note: *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:32 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the stretch-your-hand-to-the-poor substance — the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the substantial-criterion-of-mercy. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:36's *I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.* Sirach 7:32-35 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the same architecture — *stretch your hand to the poor* (v.32), *fail not to be with them that weep* (v.34), *be not slow to visit the sick: for that shall make you to be beloved* (v.35) — the same six-fold-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the sheep-and-goats-criterion. The substantial-substance is the substantial-substance-of-the-blessing-substance-being-perfected-through-the-substantial-mercy-toward-the-substantial-poor — the substantial-substance the inherited-Christian-collapse of-grace-without-fruit explicitly-rules-out; the substantial-substance the framework reads in-continuity-with the new-heart of Ezekiel 36:26-27 the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) gives-into-the-substantial-individual-substance.

4842.new_note: *Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:9). *And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.* (Matthew 25:40). Sirach says help the poor because the commandment says so, and do not turn him away because he is poor. At the judgment the King says that whatever was done to the least of his brethren was done to him. The mercy Sirach commands is not a charity program; it is the commandment kept, and the King counts it as done to himself because the least of these are his own kin, his brethren, the household of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered and poor. Help the poor for the commandment's sake and you have served the King without knowing his face.
4842.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 29:9 — *Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away.* Mercy as the commandment kept; at Matthew 25:40 what was done *unto one of the least of these my brethren* was done to the King.

4843.new_note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:1). *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:* (Matthew 25:35). Sirach's command not to defraud the poor and not to keep needy eyes waiting is what the sheep in Matthew 25 are found to have done: I was hungry and you gave me meat, thirsty and you gave me drink, a stranger and you took me in. The judgment does not ask whether a man knew the right words; it asks what he did when the needy eyes were on him, and Sirach's chapter goes on to name the failure the goats are judged for, turn not away your eye from the needy (verse 5). This is not earning anything; it is what covenant life with Yahuah (God) looks like from the outside. The King recognizes his own by it because it was always his way.

4844.new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.* (Matthew 25:40). Tobit promises that the face of Yahuah (God) stays turned toward the man who does not turn his face from the poor. Yahusha (Jesus) says it more sharply: what you did to the least of my brethren you did to me. The giver meets the King in the one he feeds, and the King's face toward him is the Father's face toward him. The same thing was said to Saul on the Damascus road, that to persecute the brethren was to persecute him (Acts 9:4–5). It is personal: mercy toward the King's brethren is mercy the King himself receives.

4855.new_note: *Wherefore they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.* (1 Maccabees 1:63). *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). Under Antiochus the faithful in Yashar'el (Israel) chose death over unclean meat because eating it would profane the holy covenant, and so they died. At the table Yahusha (Jesus) names his own blood the blood of the new covenant, shed for many. The covenant the Maccabean faithful died for and the covenant he died to seal are not two covenants with two laws; Jeremiah says the new covenant is the law written in the inward parts and on the heart, the same law those men would not break. They gave their lives rather than profane it; he gave his to write it where it could not be taken from them.

4856.new_note: *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* (1 Maccabees 2:50). *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). Mattathias, dying, charges his sons to be zealous for the law and to give their lives for the covenant of their fathers. The King does both. His zeal for his Father's house and his Father's commandments runs through the gospels, and at the table he gives his life, his blood of the new covenant shed for many. The covenant of the fathers and the new covenant are one covenant; what is new in Jeremiah 31 is where the law is written, on the heart, not whether it stands. So the zeal Mattathias asked of his sons is not a different thing from what Yahusha (Jesus) poured out; it is the same love of the same law, carried to the same end.

4857.new_note: *For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of Yahuah (God), shall receive just punishment for your pride.* (2 Maccabees 7:36). *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). The youngest brother says his brothers are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life. They died for his laws, and their deaths are held inside a covenant that promises them life again. At the last supper Yahusha (Jesus) names his blood as the blood of the new covenant, shed for many for the remission of sins. The covenant the martyrs died under and the covenant the King's blood seals are not two covenants; the brothers trusted a promise of everlasting life, and the King's death and third-day rising are where that promise was made good. Their short pain and his cup end in the same resurrection, and the Torah they died for is the Torah the new covenant writes on the heart (Jeremiah 31:33).

4864.new_note: *Instead of a friend become not an enemy; for thereby you shall inherit an ill name, shame, and reproach: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:1). *Then Judas, which betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said unto him, Thou hast said.* (Matthew 26:25). Sirach warns against two things in one verse, the friend who turns enemy and the sinner with a double tongue, and Judas is both at the table. He had already sold his Master for thirty pieces of silver, and he asks, Master, is it I?, with the bargain in his pocket; that is the double tongue, one voice at the supper and another with the priests. Yahusha (Jesus) answers, thou hast said, and lets the man's own mouth carry the verdict. The betrayal served the Father's purpose and was Judas's own choice at the same time; the devil put it in his heart, John says, and Judas walked it out, and Sirach's warning stands over him as the shame and reproach of a friend who became an enemy.

Then came they, and laid hands on Yahusha (Jesus), and took him.* (Matthew 26:50). Sirach asks whether it is not a grief unto death when a companion and friend turns enemy. 4867.new_note: *My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:1). *Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.* (Matthew 26:41). In Gethsemane Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples to watch and pray so they do not enter into temptation, and they fall asleep. Sirach had said what they needed to hear before they ever came to the garden: if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation. The flesh is weak, the Messiah says; what Sirach adds is that a servant can get his soul ready for that weakness instead of being surprised by it. The disciples were willing in spirit and unprepared in soul, and the night proved Sirach right.

4868.new_note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). *And Peter remembered the word of Yahusha (Jesus), which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.* (Matthew 26:75). Peter went into the furnace that night and came out weeping. He had denied his Master three times, the cock crowed, the word came back to him, and he went out and wept bitterly. Sirach says acceptable men are tried in the furnace of adversity the way gold is tried in the fire, and the bitter weeping is the fire working. Caiaphas had rent his garments a few verses earlier (v.65); Peter rent his heart, which is the tearing Yahuah (God) asks for, and it carried him to the restoration by the shore in John 21. A disciple can fail, and a failed disciple is neither finished nor safe; he repents, and the furnace is what shows whether he is gold.

4881.new_note: *After these years shall my son Messiah (Christ) die, and all men that have life. And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.* (2 Esdras 7:29–30). *Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.* (Matthew 27:45). Ezra is told that the Messiah will die, and that the world will then be turned back into the old silence, as in the former judgments, before the raising up that follows (2 Esdras 7:31–32). When Yahusha (Jesus) hung on the tree, darkness lay over all the land from the sixth hour to the ninth, as if creation had drawn back toward its first dark. The three hours were not the seven days; they were a small showing of them, the world going quiet at the death of the Messiah (Christ) before the graves gave up their dead (Matthew 27:52). Amos had said *I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day* (Amos 8:9); Ezra was told the Messiah's death brings the old silence; the cross carried both for three hours.
