4881.old_note: *And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7:30 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the world-turned-into-old-silence substance — the apocalyptic-stream had named the architecture of the cosmic-darkness-and-silence at the day-of-the-Messiah's-death + the post-death-silence-before-the-resurrection. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:45's *now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour* — the three-hours-of-darkness at the substance of the King's-walking-into-the-cross is the historical-pivot-foretaste of the broader-cosmic-darkness the apocalyptic-stream had named. 2 Esdras 7:28-29 names the architecture directly — *my son the Messiah shall be revealed... after these years shall my son Messiah (Christ) die, and all men that have life. And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days.* The wisdom-stream had named the Messianic-death-and-cosmic-darkness architecture; the cross walks-out the historical-pivot-fulfillment per Amos 8:9's *I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day.* FRAMEWORK-MAJOR for the wisdom-stream's direct prefiguring.

4882.new_note: *And the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away, and the long suffering shall have an end:* (2 Esdras 7:33). *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51). In Ezra's order, once the earth has given back her dead the Most High appears upon the seat of judgment, and misery and long suffering come to an end. At the moment Yahusha (Jesus) died the veil of the temple tore from top to bottom, the earth quaked, the rocks split, and the graves were opened (Matthew 27:52). The signs that belong to the day of the Most High's appearing broke through for a moment at the cross. It was not that day, but it carried the marks of it, the way a first shaking tells of the one still to come (Haggai 2:6–7).
4882.member_note: 2 Esdras 7:33 — *the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away.* The veil rent and the earth quaking at Matthew 27:51 carry the marks of that day.
4882.old_note: *And the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away, and the long suffering shall have an end.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7:33 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Most-High-appearing-upon-the-seat-of-judgment substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:51's veil-rent + the earthquake + the rocks-rent — the cosmic-signs at the cross are the historical-pivot-foretaste of the broader-day-of-the-Most-High the apocalyptic-stream had named. The framework reads this in continuity with Haggai 2:6-7's *I will shake the heavens, and the earth* + Hebrews 12:26-27's *yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the Most-High-appearing-and-misery-passing-away; the cross walks-out the in-flesh-substance of the day-of-the-Most-High's-acting at the historical-pivot. The eschatological-day-of-the-Most-High the apocalyptic-stream named at the wisdom-register is rehearsed-in-foretaste at the historical-cross-pivot.

4883.new_note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). Ezra is told that the earth will restore those asleep in her, that the dust will give back those that dwell in silence. At the cross the earth quaked and the graves were opened, and many bodies of the saints that slept arose. The earth was doing in small measure what Ezra was told she will do fully: giving back what was sleeping in her. The saints who came out of their graves that day are a first showing of the resurrection the fathers are still waiting for, the first resurrection in which the faithful who fell asleep are raised (Revelation 20:4–6; Hebrews 11:39–40).

The framework reads the verses together in continuity with Daniel 12:2's *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake* + Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37:1-14's valley-of-dry-bones + 1 Corinthians 15:20-23's *Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits; afterward they that are Messiah's (Christ's) at his coming.* Per Red Line #11's first-resurrection-foretaste reading: the forefathers-who-walked-the-covenant-faithfully Yahuah is able to graft-in-again at the first-resurrection (Romans 11:24 + Hebrews 11:39-40); the Matt 27:52-53 saints-arising substance is the historical-foretaste-of-the-fuller-first-resurrection-at-the-King's-coming.

4890.new_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). The angel at the tomb announced the first man to pass through Wisdom's time of visitation: He is not here, for he is risen. The righteous who are held in the Father's hand shine when he visits them, and the empty tomb is the firstfruits of that day — *Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits; afterward they that are Messiah's (Christ's) at his coming* (1 Corinthians 15:23). Daniel saw the rest of them still sleeping in the dust until they awake and shine (Daniel 12:2–3). One has risen; the others rest and wait for the same visitation.

4891.new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). Wisdom sees the righteous judging the nations and ruling the people under an Elohim (God) who reigns for ever — the reign John saw on the earth, where *they lived and reigned with Messiah (Christ) a thousand years* (Revelation 20:4). That reign needs risen saints, and the empty tomb is where the rising began: He is not here, for he is risen. The first to rise is the one who will seat the rest. This is not souls escaping to heaven while the earth burns; it is the dead raised to rule on the earth with their King, the way Daniel said the saints of the most High would take the kingdom.

4892.new_note: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). *And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* (Matthew 28:9). The righteous live for evermore. The women at the tomb found out what that looks like: they held him by the feet. He had a body they could grip, flesh and bones he would show the disciples that evening (Luke 24:39), and that risen body is the firstfruits of what Wisdom promises the righteous. The righteous dead are not disembodied souls already in heaven; they are asleep, their reward kept with Yahuah (God), waiting for the day the one who rose first raises them (1 Thessalonians 4:16). The care of them is with the Most High the whole time they wait.

4893.new_note: *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:16). *And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. 4903.new_note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). Set these two side by side and the Great Commission stops reading as a change of audience. Ezra was shown the ten tribes carried over the waters into another land, and that land is among the nations; the scattered house lives there, mixed in and unrecognizable, the people Hosea called not my people (Hosea 1:9). So the King who said he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) now sends his disciples to all nations, because that is where the sheep are. The scope widened to every nation because the flock is scattered through every nation, not because the flock was replaced. We do not know those sheep by sight, so the word goes out broadly, and the ones who hear are revealed to be his (John 10:27).
4903.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:40 — *he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* The scattered house lives among the nations, which is why the word goes to all nations (Matthew 28:19).

The proclamation goes-broadly because the sheep-are-scattered; those-who-hear-are-revealed-to-be-sheep-because-they-were-sheep-before-the-foundation-of-the-world per Red Line #11. 4904.new_note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* (2 Esdras 13:47). *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). Ezra sees the ten tribes come back through the stream the Most High stays for them; the peaceable multitude of his vision is the scattered house coming home, and it is the Highest who does the gathering. Yahusha (Jesus) sends his disciples to all nations, and these two verses explain each other: the disciples go out into the nations because that is where the tribes were carried, and the Father brings them back. Isaiah had already said he would set his hand the second time to recover the remnant of his people from the four corners of the earth (Isaiah 11:11–12); James wrote to the twelve tribes scattered abroad (James 1:1), and Peter to the strangers scattered through the provinces (1 Peter 1:1). The proclamation to all nations is that second recovery going out to find them.

7835.new_note: *For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honoured in it for ever.* (2 Esdras 9:31). *And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.* (Mark 4:20). The law is spoken of here as seed: I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you. The good ground in the parable is those who hear the word, receive it, and bring forth fruit, thirty, sixty, a hundredfold. The word sown in Mark is the law sown in Ezra, and the fruit is the same fruit, a people keeping what was put in them. Ezra goes on to say that the fathers who received it and kept it not perished (2 Esdras 9:32–33), which is the other soils of the parable.
7835.member_note: 2 Esdras 9:31 — *I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you.* The good ground of Mark 4:20 brings forth the fruit the sown law was given to bring.
7835.old_note: *For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honoured in it for ever. But our fathers, which received the law, kept it not... they that received it perished, because they kept not the thing that was sown in them.* (2 Esdras 9:31-33.) The law sown to bring fruit, and the fathers who perished because they kept not what was sown in them, is the same hearing-and-keeping diagnostic Mark 4:20 names: *such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.* The good ground is the heart that keeps the sown word; the Hebrew library names the law-sown-bringing-fruit the good-ground parable walks.

7837.new_note: *For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?* (2 Esdras 4:30). *And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.* (Mark 4:15). The evil seed in the heart of Adam has been bearing ungodliness since the beginning, Uriel says, and will until the threshing. In the parable of the sower the word is sown and Satan comes at once and takes it out of the heart before it can root. The heart is the ground in both; in one the evil seed is sown into it, in the other the good seed is stolen out of it. Mark's four soils are the field Esdras was shown, and the adversary works the same ground the same way until the harvest.
7837.member_note: 2 Esdras 4:30 — *how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time?.* The same heart is the ground where Satan takes away the word that was sown (Mark 4:15).

The sower's seed by the way-side that *Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away* (Mark 4:15) and the soils that bring forth no fruit are the same diagnostic: the evil seed contests the good seed in the heart until the time of threshing. The Hebrew library names the two-seeds-in-the-heart the parable enacts in the four-soils.

7849.new_note: *For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:9). *Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.* (Mark 7:13). Sirach says a father's blessing establishes the houses of children and a mother's curse roots out foundations, so honour toward parents is not a courtesy; it is what a house stands on. Yahusha (Jesus) says the tradition that voided the fifth commandment made the word of Elohim (God) of none effect, and Sirach tells you what that costs: the blessing forfeited and the foundation uprooted. A tradition that teaches sons to withhold from their parents is pulling the house down on them while calling it devotion. The Messiah names the voiding; Sirach had already named the price.
7849.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:9 — *the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children.* The foundation the tradition of Mark 7:13 roots out.
7849.reason: Regrade said NOT_FOUND only because the old note quoted the Mark verse first; the Sirach verse is 3:9 as labelled. Rebuilt in place, no move.
7849.old_note: *Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered.* The tradition does not merely fail to bless; it brings the curse the wisdom-stream warns of: *For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 3:9) The man-made tradition that voids the fifth commandment forfeits the blessing and invites the uprooting; the King names the voiding, and the Hebrew library had already named the cost.

7850.new_note: *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:8). *And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;* (Mark 7:12). Mark 7:12 is the deed being forbidden: once the vow was spoken, the tradition suffered a man no more to do anything for his father or his mother. Sirach had said honour is both in word and deed, and the corban ruling kept the word, a vow formula that profited the system, and outlawed the deed. Measured by Sirach's own standard, the tradition did not merely fall short of the commandment; it subtracted half of it and called the remainder righteousness. Yahusha (Jesus) is not bringing a new standard against the elders, only the old one they had cut in two.
7850.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:8 — *both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* The deed the tradition forbids at Mark 7:12.
7850.old_note: *And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother.* The tradition forbids the very service Sirach commands *in word and deed*: *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 3:8) The corban ruling is honour in word only — a vow-formula that profits the system — while the deed of provision is forbidden; the Hebrew library had already named honour as word AND deed, so the tradition's subtraction is exposed by the wisdom-stream's own standard.

7851.new_note: *He that fears Yahuah (God) will honour his father, and will do service to his parents, as to his masters.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:7). *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* (Mark 7:10). Sirach binds honouring one's father to the fear of Yahuah (God): the man who fears him will serve his parents the way a servant serves his masters. Yahusha (Jesus) quotes the commandment behind that, for Moses said, honour thy father and thy mother, and then shows how the corban tradition severed what Sirach had joined, letting a man withhold from his parents what he vowed to the altar and call it devotion. A fear of Yahuah (God) that excuses a man from his parents is not the fear Sirach knew. The tradition had split the two apart; the Messiah puts Moses back on the table.
7851.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:7 — *He that fears Yahuah (God) will honour his father.* The commandment the corban tradition severs from the fear of Yahuah (God) at Mark 7:10.
7851.reason: Regrade said NOT_FOUND only because the old note quoted the Mark verse first; the Sirach verse is 3:7 as labelled. Rebuilt in place, no move.
7851.old_note: *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother.* The commandment the corban tradition voids is the same the Hebrew library's wisdom-stream binds to the fear of Yahuah: *He that fears Yahuah (God) will honour his father, and will do service to his parents, as to his masters.* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 3:7) Sirach makes honour-of-parents the test of the fear of Yahuah; the corban device, which lets a man withhold from his parents what he vows to the altar, is the exact severing of the two the wisdom-stream had joined.

7859.new_note: *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). *And as touching the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush Elohim (God) spake unto him, saying, I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob?* (Mark 12:26). Wisdom admits the plain fact: the righteous are punished in the sight of men, and men watch them die. Then it names what the watchers cannot see — a hope full of immortality. Yahusha (Jesus) puts the same hope on the record of Moses: at the bush, generations after the patriarchs were buried, Elohim (God) still called himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Their death was in the sight of men; their life is in his sight. The resurrection is the shape that hope takes when it is kept.
7859.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:4 — *though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.* The hope the bush bears witness to at Mark 12:26 — the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, long after their burial.
7859.old_note: *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:4 names the hope-full-of-immortality the resurrection-argument of Mark 12:26 grounds itself in. The King reads the bush-revelation — *I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob* — as the Father's standing relation to the living, not to the perished. The wisdom-stream had already named the righteous as carrying a hope full of immortality though they die in the sight of men; the gospel names the resurrection that hope reaches toward.

7860.new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *He is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but the Elohim (God) of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.* (Mark 12:27). The Sadducees denied the resurrection, and Yahusha (Jesus) answered them from the bush: Elohim (God) named himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob long after they were buried, and he is not the Elohim (God) of the dead. Wisdom explains how the fathers can be counted living while they lie in the ground — their souls are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and no torment touches them there. They rest, held against the day he raises them. To deny that is to err greatly, as he told the Sadducees to their faces.
7860.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God).* Why the fathers are living to the Father — *He is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but the Elohim (God) of the living* (Mark 12:27).
7860.old_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 names the souls-of-the-righteous-in-the-Father's-hand architecture the King invokes at Mark 12:27 — *he is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but the Elohim (God) of the living.* The patriarchs Avraham (Abraham), Yitschaq (Isaac), and Ya'aqov (Jacob) are alive to the Father because the souls of the righteous are held in his hand against the resurrection; the Sadducees who deny the resurrection know neither the scriptures nor the power of Elohim. The Hebrew library had already named the righteous as living in the Father's hand; the gospel names the same in the bush-revelation.

7861.new_note: *And they which did gainsay your promises, and believed not your covenants, have trodden them down.* (2 Esdras 5:29). *What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.* (Mark 12:9). In Ezra's prayer the ones who trod the people down are the ones who gainsaid the promises and did not believe the covenants, the many nations the one people had been given over to (2 Esdras 5:28). In the parable the same unbelief shows up inside the hedge: the husbandmen entrusted with the vineyard beat the servants and kill the heir, acting as though the owner's word about returning were empty. Ezra asks why the Most High lets his people be trodden down; the parable answers with what the lord of the vineyard will do when he comes. Those who tread down what the covenants cover, whether from outside the hedge or from within it, meet the same owner.
7861.member_note: 2 Esdras 5:29 — *they which did gainsay your promises, and believed not your covenants, have trodden them down.* The husbandmen of Mark 12:9 carry the same unbelief inside the hedge, and meet the same owner.
7861.reason: The old note identified Ezra's 'they which did gainsay your promises' with the wicked husbandmen. In 2 Esdras 5:28–29 the ones treading the people down are the many nations the one people was given over to, not its own keepers. I kept the connection as the same unbelief seen from outside the hedge (Ezra) and from inside it (the parable), rather than making them the same men.
7861.old_note: *And they which did gainsay your promises, and believed not your covenants, have trodden them down.* 2 Esdras 5:29 names the covenant-trodden-down by those who gainsay the promises — the wisdom-stream's lament over the very failure the wicked husbandmen embody at Mark 12. The keepers who beat the servants, kill the heir, and seize the inheritance are those who gainsaid the promises and believed not the covenants; the lord's coming to destroy them and give the vineyard to others (Mark 12:9) answers the 2 Esdras lament with the master's own judgment.

7862.new_note: *And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.* (2 Esdras 5:27). *What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.* (Mark 12:9). Ezra names what the vineyard is before the parable ever has to explain it: one people gotten out of all the multitudes, loved, and given a law. The lord of the vineyard in the parable owns it because he chose it; the husbandmen only hold it. When they beat his servants and kill his heir, what he takes from them is the stewardship, and that is what he gives to others. The one people the Most High loved and gave his law to is still his vineyard; it was never the keepers' to lose.
7862.member_note: 2 Esdras 5:27 — *among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people.* The lord of the vineyard at Mark 12:9 takes back the keeping of a people that was always his.
7862.old_note: *And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.* 2 Esdras 5:27 names the one-chosen-people-given-the-law architecture the wicked-husbandmen parable presupposes — the vineyard is the one people loved and given the Torah. Mark 12:9's *what shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others* turns on the same election: the vineyard belongs to the lord who chose it, not to the keepers; the keepers who slay the heir forfeit the stewardship, but the one-only-vine remains the lord's own.

7863.new_note: *And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:* (2 Esdras 5:23). *And he began to speak unto them by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it, and digged a place for the winefat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.* (Mark 12:1). The vineyard of the parable is not a figure Yahusha (Jesus) invents on the spot; Ezra had already prayed it back to the Most High, who out of all the trees of the earth chose one only vine. In the parable that chosen vine is hedged, given a winefat and a tower, and let out to husbandmen while the owner goes into a far country. Everything the husbandmen later do, they do to a vineyard that was never theirs. The one vine remains the owner's choice; the keepers were only ever entrusted with it.
7863.member_note: 2 Esdras 5:23 — *you have chosen you one only vine.* The vineyard let out to husbandmen at Mark 12:1 was the owner's choice, never the keepers'.
7863.old_note: *O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine.* 2 Esdras 5:23 names the one-chosen-vine architecture — Yahuah's singular election of one vine out of all the trees of the earth, the wisdom-stream's own naming of the vineyard the King plants in the parable of Mark 12:1. The vineyard *let out to husbandmen* is the one-only-vine 2 Esdras names: the covenant body Yashar'el (Israel), chosen out of all the peoples, set with hedge and tower and winefat, then entrusted to the keepers who fail it.

7864.new_note: *It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:7). *It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God).* (Mark 10:25). Sirach says gold is a stumblingblock to those who sacrifice to it, and every fool is taken by it, taken as a bird is taken in a snare. Yahusha (Jesus) says the rich man passes into the kingdom about as easily as a camel through a needle's eye. The two sayings are one picture: a man held by what he sacrifices to cannot get through the narrow door, because the thing holding him will not fit. It is not the gold that stops at the needle's eye; it is the man who will not let go of it.
7864.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 31:7 — *every fool shall be taken with it.* The one taken by his gold cannot pass the needle's eye of Mark 10:25.
7864.old_note: *It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 31:7 names gold-as-stumblingblock-for-those-who-sacrifice-to-it — wealth as an object of worship that captures its devotees. Mark 10:25's *it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)* walks the same architecture: the one taken by the gold he sacrifices to cannot pass into the kingdom while the gold holds him.

7865.new_note: *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:6). *And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Yahusha (Jesus) answereth again, and saith unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)!* (Mark 10:24). Sirach does not say gold is evil; he says it has ruined many, and that their destruction was standing right beside them while they held it. Yahusha (Jesus) puts his finger on the same spot: not the riches, but the trusting in them. The hand that closes around gold is the hand that cannot take hold of the kingdom, and the disciples were astonished because the whole world around them measured blessing by that very gold.
7865.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 31:6 — *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present..* The ruin is in the trusting; *how hard is it for them that trust in riches* (Mark 10:24).
7865.old_note: *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 31:6 names the gold-as-ruin diagnostic. Mark 10:24's clarifying word — *how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)!* — lands the diagnostic exactly where the wisdom-stream lands it: not on the riches themselves but on the trust-in-riches that has been the ruin of many. The closed hand that trusts in gold is the heart the gospel warns cannot pass through the needle's eye.

7866.new_note: *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:5). *And Yahusha (Jesus) looked round about, and saith unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)!* (Mark 10:23). Sirach says the man who loves gold will not be justified. Yahusha (Jesus) looks round at his disciples after the rich young man walks away and says how hard it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of Elohim (God). It is the same man in both verses: the one Sirach says will not be justified is the one the King says hardly enters. Not because riches are a sin, but because gold tends to own the man who has it, and a man owned by gold does not come in.
7866.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 31:5 — *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption.* The one Sirach says will not be justified is the one who *hardly* enters the kingdom at Mark 10:23.
7866.old_note: *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 31:5 names the gold-love-disqualifies architecture directly. Mark 10:23's *how hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)!* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-entry level: the gold-lover the wisdom-stream says shall not be justified is the rich man the gospel says hardly enters the kingdom.

7867.new_note: *Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:8). *Then Yahusha (Jesus) beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.* (Mark 10:21). Sirach calls the rich man blessed who is found without blemish and has not gone after gold, and the next verse asks, who is he? as if such a man were rare enough to go looking for. Yahusha (Jesus) looked at a rich young man, loved him, and put Sirach's question to him in the flesh: sell what you have, give to the poor, and come. The man went away grieved, because his great possessions had him. The blessing Sirach names was offered to him on the road and he could not take it, because he had gone after gold and the gold had gone after him.
7867.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 31:8 — *Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold..* The rich young ruler of Mark 10:21 was offered that blessing and went away grieved.
7867.old_note: *Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 31:8 names the rare-blessing of the rich-who-has-not-gone-after-gold — the exact test the rich young ruler fails at Mark 10:21-22. The King's *one thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor* lays the wisdom-stream's diagnostic bare: the man's riches have his heart, and he goes away grieved *for he had great possessions.* The Hebrew library had already named the blessedness of the rich who is not held by his gold; the gospel names the man held.

7871.new_note: *For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of Yahuah (God), shall receive just punishment for your pride.* (2 Maccabees 7:36). *And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.* (Mark 14:24). Dying under Antiochus, the youngest brother names where his brothers now lie: dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life. They were faithful to the covenant unto death, and the covenant holds them. At the table Yahusha (Jesus) lifts the cup and calls it his blood of the new covenant, shed for many. The martyrs of 2 Maccabees 7 died trusting a covenant of everlasting life whose promise had not yet been made good; Mark 14:24 is the King's own blood put to that same covenant. The many it is shed for include the seven who went before it, and their everlasting life waits on the resurrection the King's own rising opened.
7871.member_note: 2 Maccabees 7:36 — *are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life.* Mark 14:24's blood of the new covenant seals the covenant of everlasting life the martyrs died under.
7871.old_note: *For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life.* 2 Maccabees 7:36 names the brothers dead *under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life* — the faithful-unto-death-for-the-covenant whose dying is held within the covenant of everlasting life. Mark 14:24's blood *shed for many* is the covenant-of-everlasting-life sealed in the King's blood; the Hebrew library named the everlasting-life covenant the martyrs died under, and the King names the blood that seals it.

7872.new_note: *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* (1 Maccabees 2:50). *And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.* (Mark 14:24). A dying father tells his sons to give their lives for the covenant of their fathers, and the sons do it, one after another, through the rest of the book. Mark records the King doing the same thing with his own blood, the blood of the new covenant, shed for many. The many he died for are the people whose fathers cut that covenant at Sinai and whose sons died for it under Antiochus. Mattathias asked his sons for what Yahusha (Jesus) gave, and the covenant both were given for is the same covenant, now written on the heart.
7872.member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:50 — *give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* Mark 14:24, the King's blood of the new covenant shed for many, is a life given for that covenant.
7872.old_note: *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* 1 Maccabees 2:50 names Mattathias' charge — give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. Mark 14:24's *my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many* is the King giving his own life for the covenant, the substance the Hebrew library named at the martyr-register. The covenant the Maccabean faithful died for is the covenant the King seals in his blood shed for many — the blood-of-the-covenant architecture the wisdom-stream had already carried.

7880.new_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.* (Mark 13:27). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and given back their inheritance as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam will send his angels and gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of the earth to the other. The four winds are where the tribes were scattered; the elect gathered out of them are the tribes Sirach prayed home. The prayer names who; the gospel names how and when.
7880.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together.* The elect gathered from the four winds (Mark 13:27) is this prayer answered.
7880.old_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:11 prays the gathering as the petition of the wisdom-stream — *gather all the tribes of Jacob together* — and names whom: not a believing remnant of any people, but *all the tribes of Jacob,* the twelve-tribe inheritance *as from the beginning.* Mark 13:27's gathering of the elect from the four winds is the answered form of this prayer: the Son of Adam sends his angels to gather the very tribes the Hebrew library had been praying home.

7881.new_note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 5:5). *And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.* (Mark 13:27). Baruch 4:37 brought the children from east to west; here they come from west to east. Between the two verses the gathering comes from every direction. Mark 13:27 says it the same way: the Son of Adam sends his angels to gather his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth. Jerusalem's children in Baruch and the elect in Mark are one people, the scattered seed, brought home by the word of the Holy One and the hand of the Son of Adam at the end of the age. Jerusalem is told to stand on high and watch, because the homecoming is something she will see.
7881.member_note: Baruch 5:5 — *behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One.* With 4:37 the gathering comes from every direction; the elect from the four winds (Mark 13:27).
7881.old_note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).* Baruch 5:5 names the gathering from the opposite quarter — *from the west to the east* — so that Baruch 4:37 and 5:5 together name the gathering from every direction, the four-winds substance Mark 13:27 carries. The children gathered are the scattered children of Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) brought home by the word of the Holy One; Mark's *from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth* is the same paternal-blood ingathering at the end of the age.

7883.new_note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* (2 Esdras 13:47). *And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.* (Mark 13:27). The ten tribes did not find their own way home in Ezra's vision. The Highest stayed the springs of the stream for them, as he had once held the waters when they went out, and the multitude came through in peace. Mark 13:27 is the same homecoming seen from the gospel side: when the Son of Adam comes, he sends his angels to gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of the earth to the other. The gathering is his act in both books. The scattered seed is brought back by the hand of the Most High, not by its own contriving, and the elect of Mark 13 are the people Ezra watched cross the stream.
7883.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:47 — *therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* The act of the Most High, not the scattered's own contriving; Mark 13:27's elect gathered from the four winds.
7883.old_note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:47 names the return-passage the Most High opens for the ten tribes at the latter time — the same Most High who held the flood for them at the going-out holds it again for the coming-home. Mark 13:27's gathering of the elect from the four winds is the gospel-form of this homecoming the wisdom-stream had already named: the scattered seed brought back by the act of the Most High, not by their own contriving.

7885.new_note: *And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him; Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:39–40). *And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.* (Mark 13:27). The man who comes up from the sea gathers a peaceable multitude to himself, and Ezra is told in the next breath who they are: the ten tribes Salmanasar of Assyria carried away captive over the waters into another land. When Yahusha (Jesus) says the angels will gather his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth, that is the multitude he means. The elect are not a people assembled out of whoever chose to join; they are the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) brought home from where they were carried. Ezra puts a name on the ones the four winds give back.
7885.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:39 — *he gathered another peaceable multitude to him.* The elect gathered from the four winds at Mark 13:27 are the ten tribes the next verse names.
7885.old_note: *And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:39 names the peaceable-multitude the Most High gathers to the man who ascends — and the verses that follow (13:40-47) identify them by name: the ten tribes of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) carried away captive. Mark 13:27's *he shall send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds* walks the same architecture the Hebrew library had already named: the gathering is the homecoming of the scattered paternal-blood remnant, not the assembling of a self-selected community. The wisdom-stream names whom the gathering gathers.

7888.new_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *He hath holpen his servant Yashar'el (Israel), in remembrance of his mercy;* (Luke 1:54). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Mary, carrying the child, sings that he has helped his servant Yashar'el (Israel) in remembrance of his mercy. The help she sings is the beginning of the answer to Sirach's prayer: mercy remembered toward the whole servant Yashar'el (Israel), all the tribes, not a figure of speech for some other people. The gathering was being set in motion in her womb.
7888.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *inherit you them, as from the beginning.* Mary's *he hath holpen his servant Yashar'el (Israel)* (Luke 1:54) is this prayer beginning to be answered.
7888.old_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:11 names the gathering-of-all-the-tribes-of-Jacob as the prayer of the Hebrew library — the same twelve-tribe ingathering the Magnificat sings when Miriam (Mary) names *he hath holpen his servant Yashar'el (Israel), in remembrance of his mercy* (Luke 1:54). The mercy Miriam names is the keeping of the gathering-prayer Sirach already prayed: gather the tribes, inherit them as from the beginning. This is the seed-of-promise gathering, not a metaphorical-Yashar'el.

7889.new_note: *O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:12). *He hath holpen his servant Yashar'el (Israel), in remembrance of his mercy;* (Luke 1:54). Sirach asks mercy for the people called by the name of Yahuah (God), for Yashar'el (Israel) his firstborn. Mary sings that he has helped his servant Yashar'el (Israel) in remembrance of his mercy. The mercy prayed for and the mercy remembered fall on the same people, the firstborn son, the servant, and both are tied to the gathering: Sirach's verse before asks for all the tribes of Jacob, and Mary's next lines name the oath sworn to Abraham. The firstborn is remembered, not replaced.
7889.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:12 — *have mercy upon the people that is called by your name.* Mercy remembered toward his servant Yashar'el (Israel) in Luke 1:54.
7889.old_note: *O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:12 names Yashar'el as the firstborn-called-by-the-Name and the object of the mercy. Luke 1:54's *in remembrance of his mercy* toward *his servant Yashar'el* walks the same architecture — the mercy is on the firstborn-people the prophets named, the seed the gathering brings home. The Hebrew library names the mercy on the firstborn; the Magnificat sings that mercy as the keeping of the oath.

7890.new_note: *O Jerusalem, look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 4:36). *As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.* (Luke 1:55). Jerusalem is told to turn east, the direction her children were carried, and watch the joy coming back to her from Yahuah (God); the next verse says what the joy is, her sons gathered from east to west. Mary ends her song on the ground that joy stands on: Yahuah (God) spoke to the fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. The gathering is how the oath to Abraham is kept. Baruch's song and Mary's are singing one thing, a seed promised to the fathers, scattered, and now being brought home because he remembers what he said.
7890.member_note: Baruch 4:36 — *look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).* The gathering that keeps the oath to Abraham and his seed for ever (Luke 1:55).
7890.old_note: *O Jerusalem, look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).* Baruch 4:36 turns the desolate-and-scattered toward the east to behold the gathering-joy coming from Yahuah. Luke 1:55's *as he spake to our fathers, to Avraham (Abraham), and to his seed for ever* names the same to-the-fathers-and-the-seed-for-ever promise the gathering keeps. The Hebrew library's gathering-song and the Magnificat's seed-promise are the same architecture: the scattered seed of the fathers brought home as the oath is kept.

7891.new_note: *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 4:37). *As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.* (Luke 1:55). Here is what Jerusalem sees when she looks east: her sons, the ones she sent away, coming gathered from east to west by the word of the Holy One. Mary's song ends with the seed those sons belong to; Yahuah (God) spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. The sons gathered in Baruch are Abraham's seed, scattered by exile and brought back because the oath was for ever. The Magnificat names the promise; Baruch names its fulfillment walking home.
7891.member_note: Baruch 4:37 — *your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west.* Abraham's seed for ever, gathered home (Luke 1:55).
7891.old_note: *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).* Baruch 4:37 names the sons-sent-away coming gathered from east to west by the word of the Holy One. Luke 1:55's closing of the Magnificat — *to Avraham (Abraham), and to his seed for ever* — is the seed that is gathered. The Hebrew library names the gathering of the sent-away sons; the Magnificat names the oath-to-the-seed that grounds that gathering. The two songs sing one architecture.

7895.new_note: *For Yahuah (God) has appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Yashar'el (Israel) may go safely in the glory of Yahuah (God),* (Baruch 5:7). *Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth;* (Luke 3:5). Baruch gives the reason the hills come down and the valleys fill: so that Yashar'el (Israel) may walk home safely in the glory of Yahuah (God). The leveled road is a road for the gathering. John the Baptist preached from Isaiah 40, every valley filled, every mountain brought low, the rough ways made smooth, and Luke tells us who was walking that road: the people coming out to him to be baptized, the house of Yashar'el (Israel) being called back. Baruch read Isaiah's highway as the road the scattered seed comes home on; John stood at the head of that road and opened it.
7895.member_note: Baruch 5:7 — *every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up.* The leveled road is for Yashar'el (Israel) to walk home; John opened it (Luke 3:5).
7895.old_note: *For Yahuah (God) has appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Yashar'el (Israel) may go safely in the glory of Yahuah (God).* Baruch 5:7 names the every-high-hill-cast-down and the valleys-filled-up as the making-even-of-the-ground so that Yashar'el may go safely home in the glory of Yahuah — the gathering-highway. Luke 3:5's *every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low... and the rough ways shall be made smooth* (Yochanan/John quoting Yeshayahu/Isaiah 40) walks the same valleys-filled / hills-low architecture. The Hebrew library reads the Yeshayahu-40 highway explicitly as the gathering-road of the scattered seed; Yochanan's preaching opens that same road.

7896.new_note: *For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.* (Baruch 5:9). *And all flesh shall see the salvation of Elohim (God).* (Luke 3:6). Baruch ends his gathering song with Yahuah (God) himself leading Yashar'el (Israel) home with joy, in the light of his glory, in mercy and righteousness. Luke ends his quotation of Isaiah 40 with all flesh seeing the salvation of Elohim (God). The two endings belong together: the road is leveled so Yashar'el (Israel) can walk it, and when Yahuah (God) leads them home in his glory the whole earth watches. The salvation all flesh sees is the gathering of the scattered seed; the nations see it done, and Yashar'el (Israel) walks it.
7896.member_note: Baruch 5:9 — *Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory.* Where the road ends; all flesh sees the salvation of Elohim (God) (Luke 3:6).
7896.old_note: *For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.* Baruch 5:9 names Yahuah leading Yashar'el home with joy in the light of his glory. Luke 3:6's *and all flesh shall see the salvation of Elohim (God)* names the salvation-of-Elohim seen at the end of the leveled highway. The Hebrew library names the glory-led homecoming the gathering-road opens onto; Yochanan (John) names the all-flesh-seeing-the-salvation the same road arrives at. The road in Baruch and the road in Luke 3 lead to the same glory.

7909.new_note: *Yet they that received it perished, because they kept not the thing that was sown in them.* (2 Esdras 9:33). *But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.* (Luke 8:15). Ezra says why the fathers perished: they received what was sown and did not keep it. The good ground in the parable is the opposite in every word, an honest and good heart that hears the word, keeps it, and brings forth fruit with patience. Receiving is not the dividing line; keeping is. The fruit is the keeping, and the perishing is the not keeping.
7909.member_note: 2 Esdras 9:33 — *they that received it perished, because they kept not the thing that was sown in them.* The good ground of Luke 8:15 hears the word and keeps it; the fruit is the keeping.
7909.old_note: *Yet they that received it perished, because they kept not the thing that was sown in them.* (2 Esdras 9:33) The Hebrew library names the keeping-of-the-sown-word as the dividing line — those who received the law-seed but kept it not perished. Luke 8:15's good-ground hearers are the inverse: *that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.* The fruit is the keeping; the perishing is the not-keeping. The wisdom-apocalyptic stream named the keep-it-or-perish architecture that Luke 8:15 lands as the good-ground verdict.

7910.new_note: *For as the husbandman sows much seed upon the ground, and planteth many trees, and yet the thing that is sown good in his season comes not up, neither does all that is planted take root: even so is it of them that are sown in the world; they shall not all be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:41). *They on the rock are they, which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.* (Luke 8:13). Ezra is told the husbandman's experience: much seed sown, many trees planted, and not all of it comes up or takes root. Yahusha (Jesus) names the rocky ground the same way: hearers who receive the word with joy, have no root, believe for a while, and fall away when tried. Springing up is not the same as taking root. Ezra's not all saved and the parable's fall away are the same plant dying for the same reason.
7910.member_note: 2 Esdras 8:41 — *neither does all that is planted take root.* The rock hearers of Luke 8:13 spring up with no root and fall away.
7910.old_note: *For as the husbandman sows much seed upon the ground, and planteth many trees, and yet the thing that is sown good in his season comes not up, neither does all that is planted take root: even so is it of them that are sown in the world; they shall not all be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:41) The Hebrew library names the not-all-the-seed-takes-root architecture explicitly — the husbandman sows much, but not all comes up. Luke 8:13's rock-ground hearers — *which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away* — walk the same architecture: the seed sprang up but had no root, and what has no root does not endure. The wisdom-apocalyptic stream had named the no-root failure as the not-all-saved diagnostic before the parable named it in the King's own grammar.

7911.new_note: *For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honoured in it for ever.* (2 Esdras 9:31). *Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of Elohim (God).* (Luke 8:11). When Yahusha (Jesus) explains the parable, he says the seed is the word of Elohim (God). Ezra had already heard the Most High say what that seed is: I sow my law in you. The law is the word sown, and it is sown into the hearer to bring fruit there, not handed to him as a weight to carry. There is no gap between the word of Elohim (God) in the gospel and the law in Ezra; they are one seed.
7911.member_note: 2 Esdras 9:31 — *I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you.* The seed is the word of Elohim (God) at Luke 8:11, and the word sown is the law.
7911.old_note: *For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honoured in it for ever.* (2 Esdras 9:31) The Hebrew library names the seed as the law (the word) of Yahuah (God) sown INTO the hearer to bring fruit — the precise architecture Luke 8:11 names: *Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of Elohim (God).* The sower does not sow grain into ground only; the Father sows His word-law into the heart, and the bringing-forth-of-fruit is the heart's keeping of what was sown. The wisdom-apocalyptic stream had named the word-sown-to-bring-fruit register before the King spoke the parable.

7912.new_note: *Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.* (Ecclesiasticus 22:18). *But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.* (Luke 6:49). Sirach says pales set on a high place never stand against the wind, and the fool's fearful heart stands against nothing. Luke names the fool: he heard and did not do, and built his house on the earth with no foundation, and when the stream beat on it the house fell at once and the ruin was great. Hearing without doing is the house without a foundation. The wind finds it, and there is nothing underneath to hold.
7912.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 22:18 — *Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind.* The hearer who does not do, *without a foundation*, falls and the ruin is great (Luke 6:49).
7912.old_note: *Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.* (Sirach 22:18) The Hebrew library names the inverse — the unstablished heart that cannot stand against the wind. Luke 6:49 names the foolish builder: *he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.* The wisdom-stream had named the no-foundation collapse; the King walks the same architecture — the hearer-without-the-doing is the house without a foundation, and the ruin is great.

7913.new_note: *As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.* (Ecclesiasticus 22:16). *He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.* (Luke 6:48). Sirach's picture is timber bound together in a building that cannot be loosed with shaking; the heart established by counsel is like that. Luke adds a detail Matthew does not: the wise builder dug deep and laid his foundation on a rock, and when the flood beat on the house it could not shake it. The digging deep is the doing — the hearer who does the sayings is driving his foundation down to rock. That is how a heart is established so that it fears at no time.
7913.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 22:16 — *As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking.* Luke 6:48's builder *digged deep*, and the stream *could not shake* the house.
7913.old_note: *As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.* (Sirach 22:16) The Hebrew library names the heart-stablished-by-counsel architecture as the building that cannot be shaken. Luke 6:48 names the wise builder uniquely with the DEEP: *he is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it.* The wisdom-stream had named the unshakeable-because-stablished architecture; the King walks it at the hearer-and-doer level — the doing IS the digging-deep that stablishes the heart against the flood.

7915.new_note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:6). *For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.* (Luke 6:43). Sirach says the fruit tells whether the tree was dressed and the speech tells what the heart has conceived. Luke's record of Yahusha (Jesus) holds both together: a good tree does not bear corrupt fruit, a corrupt tree does not bear good, and two verses later, of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks. The fruit is the tree's utterance and the mouth is the heart's. The wise had named the test long before; the King made it the way his disciples would know one another and know a teacher.
7915.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed.* Good tree, good fruit; corrupt tree, corrupt fruit (Luke 6:43), and the mouth is the heart's fruit.
7915.old_note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Sirach 27:6) The Hebrew library names the fruit-declares-the-tree / utterance-declares-the-heart architecture directly. Luke 6:43-45 walks the same: *for a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit ... for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.* The fruit is the tree's utterance; the mouth is the heart's. The wisdom-stream named the diagnostic before the King bound it.

7918.new_note: *If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add to it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:15). *Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.* (Luke 11:52). Sirach describes two hearers: the skilful man hears a wise word and commends it and adds to it, while the man of no understanding is displeased by it and throws it behind his back. The lawyers in Luke are the second man — they heard the Word, refused it, and then took the key away so that those entering were hindered too. Casting the word behind your back is bad enough; shutting the door from the outside against others is what draws the woe. The system that does this is what Yahusha (Jesus) names; the people kept from the door are the ones he came for.
7918.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 21:15 — *it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.* The word cast behind the back, then the key of knowledge taken away from those entering (Luke 11:52).
7918.old_note: *If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add to it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.* (Sirach 21:15) The wisdom-stream names the man-of-no-understanding who casts the wise word behind his back. *Ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered* (Luke 11:52): the lawyers' taking-away-the-key is the casting-the-word-behind-the-back Sirach names — the leadership-substance that hears the Word and refuses it, then locks the door from the outside against those entering. The system-not-people diagnostic holds: the woe falls on the leadership-substance, not on the people it kept from the door.

7919.new_note: *The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he lives.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:14). *Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.* (Luke 11:52). Sirach pictures the fool's inward parts as a broken vessel: pour knowledge in and it runs out, so he holds none his whole life. Yahusha (Jesus) says the lawyers had taken away the key of knowledge — they had not entered themselves and were hindering those who were entering. A man who holds no knowledge cannot open the door for anyone else. The key that was taken away is the Torah read plainly, and the fences the office built around it are what kept the people outside; the woe is on the office that did it, not on the people it shut out.
7919.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 21:14 — *The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel.* The lawyers who took away the key of knowledge held none themselves (Luke 11:52).
7919.old_note: *The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he lives.* (Sirach 21:14) The wisdom-stream names the heart that holds no knowledge. *Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered* (Luke 11:52): the lawyers who took away the key are the broken-vessel hearts Sirach names — they hold no knowledge themselves and so cannot open the door, and they hinder those who would enter. The key-of-knowledge taken away is the Torah-read-plainly the system replaced with its own fences.

7920.new_note: *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:12). *And he said, Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.* (Luke 11:46). Sirach locates the beginning of pride in a heart turned away from its Maker. The lawyers Yahusha (Jesus) rebukes have built a weight of rules on top of the Torah and will not lift a finger under it themselves; the hand that adds to the commandment has already turned from the one who gave it. Voiding the commandment by addition is as much a departure as voiding it by subtraction, and both wear the robe of the law while they do it.
7920.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 10:12 — *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God).* The heart turned from its Maker is the lawyer lading burdens at Luke 11:46.
7920.old_note: *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.* (Sirach 10:12) The wisdom-stream names pride as the heart turned away from its Maker. *Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers* (Luke 11:46): the burden-lading lawyers build their parallel-Torah on top of the Torah and refuse to bear it — the heart-turned-away-from-the-Maker Sirach names, walking itself out as the Judaizer-system that voids the commandment by addition while keeping the robe of the law.

7921.new_note: *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:13). *Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.* (Luke 11:43). Sirach traces sin to pride, and the overthrow of nations to the abomination pride pours out. The woe Yahusha (Jesus) pronounces falls on the love of the uppermost seats and the greetings in the markets — pride in a religious dress. The library had named the disease centuries before the Pharisee's table; the King names it at the table. The woe is on the man who loves the seat; the love of the uppermost place is the pride Sirach said sin begins in.
7921.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 10:13 — *pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination.* The pride that begins sin is the love of the uppermost seats at Luke 11:43.
7921.old_note: *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* (Sirach 10:13) The wisdom-stream names pride as the beginning of sin and the overthrow it brings. *Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets* (Luke 11:43): the love-of-the-uppermost-seats the King names is the pride Sirach had already diagnosed as sin's beginning — the religious-status-architecture the woe falls on, named by the Hebrew library centuries before the Pharisee's table.

7922.new_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). *And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.* (Luke 10:18). The one whose envy let death into the world is the one Yahusha (Jesus) saw fall like lightning. When the seventy came back rejoicing that the devils were subject to them, he told them what they had been watching: the enemy who brought death in was being thrown down, and in the next verse he gives them power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy. Wisdom names the door death came through; Luke shows the one who opened it losing his footing.
7922.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 — *through envy of the devil came death into the world.* The one who let death in is the one Yahusha (Jesus) saw fall like lightning (Luke 10:18).
7922.old_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24) The wisdom-stream names the devil as the envy-source through which death entered the world — the seed-war origin behind the fallen-power the King names at Luke 10:18. *I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven. Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy* (Luke 10:18-19): the enemy whose power the seventy are given authority over is the same devil whose envy Wisdom names as the door death came through; the authority-to-tread is the inaugurated reversal of his administration.

7925.new_note: *Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of the sides of the earth, and shew mercy to them: for I am merciful, says Yahuah (God) Almighty.* (2 Esdras 2:31). *For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.* (Luke 15:24). Yahuah (God) tells the mother to remember her children that sleep, because he will bring them out of the sides of the earth and show them mercy. The father in the parable says of his returned son, this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. The son came out of a far country, and the children in 2 Esdras come out of the sides of the earth, and in both the mercy belongs to the father and the merriment follows the return. The ones who sleep are brought out because he is merciful; that is the resurrection hope, and the prodigal's homecoming is a picture of it, the lost child of the house gathered home and counted alive.
7925.member_note: 2 Esdras 2:31 — *Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of the sides of the earth.* The son who was dead and is alive again (Luke 15:24) is that mercy in a parable.
7925.old_note: *Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of the sides of the earth, and shew mercy to them: for I am merciful, says Yahuah (God) Almighty.* 2 Esdras 2:31 names the bring-out-the-children-and-show-mercy promise — the Father bringing his scattered children home with mercy. Luke 15:24's *for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found* walks the same architecture: the son brought out of the far country, the dead made alive, the lost found, the mercy shown. The prodigal's homecoming is the Father's own *I will bring them out... and shew mercy to them* in parable-form — the scattered child of Yashar'el (Israel) gathered home.

7926.new_note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.* (Luke 15:6). The sheep in the parable was lost, and the shepherd went after it until he found it, then called his neighbours to rejoice. Ezra was told who the lost are: the ten tribes carried over the waters into another land, where they dwelt until the latter time, *and now when they shall begin to come* (2 Esdras 13:46). The joy Yahusha (Jesus) describes is the joy of that homecoming. A lost sheep is still the shepherd's sheep the whole time it is lost; the ten tribes were still the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in the far country, and the finding is the gathering the prophets promised.
7926.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:40 — *carried away prisoners out of their own land.* The lost sheep whose finding the shepherd rejoices over at Luke 15:6.
7926.old_note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* 2 Esdras 13:40 names the ten tribes carried away into the land of their scattering — the lost-of-the-house-of-Yashar'el (Israel) the framework holds. Luke 15:6's *Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost* names the recovery of exactly this lost: the scattered northern house regathered. 2 Esdras names them lost in the further country; the gospel names the joy when the lost is found. *Now when he shall begin to come* (2 Esdras 13:46) is the regathering the parable rejoices over.

7927.new_note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:13). *And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.* (Luke 15:5). Sirach says the mercy of Yahuah (God) does what a shepherd does: it reproves, it nurtures, it teaches, and it brings the flock back again. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the same thing as a story — one sheep lost, the shepherd going after it until he finds it, and the sheep carried home on his shoulders with rejoicing. The bringing again is the gathering of the lost, and the mercy that gathers is wider than the mercy of man, which reaches only as far as his neighbour.
7927.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 18:13 — *he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* The bringing again is the lost sheep carried home on the shepherd's shoulders (Luke 15:5).
7927.old_note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 18:13 names the shepherd-who-brings-again-his-flock architecture in the Hebrew library. Luke 15:5's *and when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing* is the same shepherd-brings-again substance walked into the lost-sheep parable. The wisdom-stream names the mercy that *brings again, as a shepherd his flock*; the gospel names the shepherd going after the one lost until he finds it and carries it home. The bringing-again is the gathering of the lost.

7928.new_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).* (Luke 13:29). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says they will come from east, west, north and south and sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God). Four directions is where the tribes went; four directions is where they come back from. The ones sitting down are the tribes Sirach prayed for, the firstborn his next verse names, not a substitute people set at their table.
7928.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together.* From east, west, north and south (Luke 13:29) the scattered tribes sit down at home.
7928.old_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:11 names the gathering as a prayer — *gather all the tribes of Jacob together* — the petition for the regathering of the twelve tribes *as from the beginning.* Luke 13:29's come-from-the-four-quarters to sit down in the kingdom is the answer to this prayer: the scattered tribes of Jacob gathered home. The wisdom-stream prays the gathering the gospel announces; the firstborn Yashar'el (Israel) whom Yahuah named (Sirach 36:12) is the people gathered, not a substitute people installed in their place.

7929.new_note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God). For they departed from you on foot, and were led away of their enemies: but Yahuah (God) brings them to you exalted with glory, as children of the kingdom.* (Baruch 5:5–6). *And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).* (Luke 13:29). Jerusalem is told to stand up high and watch her children come home from the west to the east, and the next verse says who they are: the ones who left her on foot, led away by their enemies, now brought back by Yahuah (God) exalted with glory as children of the kingdom. Yahusha (Jesus) says they shall come from the east and the west and the north and the south and sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God). The ones who come from every quarter in Luke 13 are the same children of the kingdom Baruch watches return, not strangers streaming in, but Jerusalem's own sons who were led away and are being brought home.
7929.member_note: Baruch 5:5 — *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east.* Jerusalem's own children brought home as children of the kingdom; they come from east and west to sit down in it (Luke 13:29).
