7929.reason: Old note leaned on 5:6 (children of the kingdom) for its point, so 5:5-6 are quoted together and cited as Baruch 5:5-6; no move, 5:5 is still the card's verse.
7929.old_note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).* Baruch 5:5 names the gathering-from-the-quarters in the same register Luke 13:29 walks: *your children gathered from the west to the east.* The children gathered are Jerusalem's own — *they departed from you on foot, and were led away of their enemies: but Yahuah (God) brings them to you exalted with glory, as children of the kingdom* (Baruch 5:6). The come-from-east-and-west of the gospel IS this prophetic-gathering of the scattered covenant-children home as children of the kingdom.

7933.new_note: *Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:11). *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* (Luke 12:33). Sirach says lay up your treasure the way the commandments of the Most High direct, and it will profit you more than gold; two verses earlier he said help the poor for the commandment's sake. Yahusha (Jesus) says sell, give alms, and provide yourselves bags that do not wear out, a treasure in the heavens that does not fail. The treasure of the man who opens his hand because the commandment says so is laid up where gold cannot go and thieves cannot follow. That is why it outlasts gold.
7933.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 29:11 — *Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High.* The commandment keeper's treasure is the *treasure in the heavens that faileth not* of Luke 12:33, laid up by alms.
7933.old_note: *Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 29:11 names the lay-up-treasure-by-the-commandments architecture explicitly — the treasure laid up by the commandment-keeper who helps the poor for the commandment's sake (Sirach 29:9). Luke 12:33's *provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not* is the gospel-form of the wisdom-stream's same teaching: the treasure of the open-handed commandment-keeper outlasts gold because it is laid up where gold cannot reach.

7934.new_note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* (Tobit 4:10). *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* (Luke 12:33). Tobit says alms deliver from death and keep the giver out of darkness; the open hand protects the one who opens it. Yahusha (Jesus) says to sell, give alms, and have a treasure in the heavens that does not fail, where no thief approaches and no moth corrupts. Both are saying that what is given away is the one thing that cannot be taken away. The library names the deliverance; the gospel names the storehouse no thief can reach.
7934.member_note: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The open hand delivers from death; its treasure is in the heavens where no thief approacheth (Luke 12:33).
7934.old_note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Tobit 4:10 names the alms-as-deliverer-from-death architecture — the treasure laid up by the open hand protects the giver. Luke 12:33's *a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth* walks the same protection-against-loss architecture at the heavenly-treasure level. The Hebrew library names the deliverance the open hand purchases; the gospel names the storehouse no thief can reach and no moth can corrupt.

7935.new_note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* (Tobit 4:9). *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* (Luke 12:33). Tobit's charge to give alms comes with a reason: the giver is laying up a good treasure against the day of necessity. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same thing with a picture — sell, give alms, and you have bags that do not wear out, a treasure in the heavens that does not fail. What is given now is what is stored for then. The library names the treasure the open hand lays up; the gospel names where it is kept and why no thief or moth can reach it.
7935.member_note: Tobit 4:9 — *a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The alms given now are the bags that wax not old, the treasure that faileth not (Luke 12:33).
7935.old_note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Tobit 4:9 names the lay-up-treasure-against-the-day architecture directly in the Hebrew library — the verse stands inside Tobit's charge to give alms (Tobit 4:7-8). Luke 12:33's *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not* walks the same architecture: the alms given now is the treasure laid up against the day. The wisdom-stream names the treasure laid up by the open hand; the gospel names the heaven-bag that faileth not.

7936.new_note: *There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:* (Ecclesiasticus 11:18). *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). Sirach describes the man who grows rich by wariness and pinching and says, dryly, that this is the portion of his reward — the heap is all he gets. Yahusha (Jesus) gives the same man his night: the soul is required, and the goods pass to someone else. Hoarding is not a sin with no consequence. The consequence is that the hoard was the whole reward.
7936.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 11:18 — *waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward.* The hoarder's whole reward is the heap left behind when the soul is required at Luke 12:20.
7936.old_note: *There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11:18 names the portion-of-the-reward of the man who waxes rich by hoarding — the verse that sets up the verdict of v.19. Luke 12:20's *Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* lands the same reckoning: the wariness-and-pinching gain is no portion at all when the soul is required. The wisdom-stream names the hollow reward; the gospel names the night it comes due.

7937.new_note: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.* (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). *And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.* (Luke 12:19). Sirach writes the rich fool's speech before the parable: I have found rest, I will eat continually of my goods. Yahusha (Jesus) puts nearly the same words in his mouth — take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. Sirach had also named the two things the man never reckons with: he does not know what time is coming on him, and he must leave it all to others and die. The barns come down the same night.
7937.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 11:19 — *I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods.* Sirach's rich man speaks the rich fool's line of Luke 12:19 centuries early.
7937.old_note: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11:19 names the rich-fool architecture word-for-word in the Hebrew library, centuries before the King speaks the parable. The man who says *I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods* is the man of Luke 12:19 who says to his soul *take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry* — and the wisdom-stream had already named the two things he does not reckon with: *he knoweth not what time shall come upon him,* and *he must leave those things to others, and die.* The barns get pulled down; the soul gets required this night; the goods get left to another. The gospel walks the architecture the wisdom-stream already carried.

7939.new_note: *O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:12). *For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.* (Luke 19:10). Sirach asks mercy for Yashar'el (Israel), the firstborn called by the name of Yahuah (God). Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam came to seek and to save that which was lost. The firstborn had been scattered until he was lost, Hosea's not my people, and the mercy Sirach prayed for arrived as a Shepherd out looking for him. The one sought is the firstborn; the seeking is the mercy.
7939.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:12 — *whom you have named your firstborn.* The lost whom the Son of Adam seeks (Luke 19:10) is the firstborn scattered.
7939.old_note: *O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn* (Sirach 36:12). The wisdom-stream names the object of the gathering: Yashar'el, the firstborn called by the Name. Luke 19:10's lost-that-must-be-sought is this firstborn-people scattered and gone Lo-Ammi; the Son of Adam comes to seek and save precisely *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el.* The mercy the wisdom-stream prays for the firstborn is the mercy the King enacts in seeking the lost.

7940.new_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.* (Luke 19:10). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam came to seek and to save that which was lost. What was lost was the house, the tribes scattered until they forgot who they were, and seeking them is the gathering Sirach prayed for. He said it in the house of Zacchaeus, a son of Abraham his neighbours had written off, which is what a found tribe looks like one man at a time.
7940.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *inherit you them, as from the beginning.* To seek and save the lost (Luke 19:10) is to gather the tribes Sirach prayed for.
7940.old_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 36:11). The wisdom-stream's explicit prayer for the gathering of ALL the tribes of Ya'aqov (Jacob) — not Yahudah (Judah) alone, but all the scattered houses, *as from the beginning.* Luke 19:10's *the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost* names the King's own programmatic statement of that same gathering-mission: the seeking-and-saving of the lost is the gathering of the scattered tribes the Hebrew library had been praying for, not a categorical-nations inclusion.

7945.new_note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). *And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.* (Luke 16:31). Ezra names where the dead wait: asleep in the earth, in the dust, in secret places that hold the souls committed to them until the day they are delivered. When Abraham tells the rich man that his brothers would not be persuaded even if one rose from the dead, he is speaking from inside that same expectation: the dead are held, and one coming back from among them is a thing that could happen. What the brothers have now is Moses and the prophets. If those are not heard, a voice come back from the secret places will not be heard either.
7945.member_note: 2 Esdras 7:32 — *the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* The one who might rise from the dead at Luke 16:31 would come from that same holding place.
7945.old_note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them* (2 Esdras 7:32). The secret-places-deliver-the-committed-souls register — the chambers of the dead give back what was entrusted to them at the resurrection. Luke 16:31's *neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead* assumes the same resurrection-from-the-holding-state architecture: the souls held in the secret places are restored at the appointed day, the resurrection the rich man's brothers must be persuaded toward before it comes.

7949.new_note: *It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:7). *No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* (Luke 16:13). Sirach calls gold a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it. He is describing worship, an offering brought and a devotion given, and he says that devotion takes its devotee. Yahusha (Jesus) names the same thing when he calls mammon a master. To serve mammon is to sacrifice to the stumblingblock; the servant does not own it, it owns him, and Sirach had already said where that ends.
7949.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 31:7 — *them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.* To serve mammon (Luke 16:13) is to sacrifice to the stumblingblock.
7949.old_note: *It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it* (Sirach 31:7). The wisdom-stream identifies gold as an object of worship that captures its devotees — *them that sacrifice to it.* Luke 16:13's *Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon* treats mammon as a competing master for exactly this reason: the wisdom-stream had already named gold as the master that takes those who sacrifice to it. To serve mammon is to sacrifice to the stumblingblock.

7950.new_note: *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:6). *No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* (Luke 16:13). Sirach had already watched gold ruin many before Yahusha (Jesus) said no servant can serve two masters. The ruin Sirach names is what happens to the man who takes mammon for a master; it does not share him, it destroys him, and the destruction is already present while he thinks he is being served. The steward in the parable just before this verse was called wise because he treated money as a thing that perishes and used it, instead of bowing to it.
7950.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 31:6 — *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present..* The servant of mammon in Luke 16:13 walks into the ruin Sirach names.
7950.old_note: *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present* (Sirach 31:6). The wisdom-stream's gold-as-ruin diagnostic stands behind Luke 16:13's either/or. The mammon-servant at Luke 16:13 walks toward the same ruin the wisdom-stream had named; the steward of the parable just before (vv.1-8) is shrewd precisely because he treats mammon as the perishing thing it is, not the master.

7951.new_note: *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:5). *No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* (Luke 16:13). Sirach says the man who loves gold will not be justified. Luke sets the King's verdict at the end of the parable of the unjust steward, a story about using mammon shrewdly before the books are called, and then closes it: you cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon. The divided heart that holds to gold has chosen its master, and Sirach already said where that leaves it. The setting is different from the Sermon on the Mount, but the verdict is the same, and it was the wisdom of Yashar'el (Israel) before the King spoke it.
7951.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 31:5 — *he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.* Gold-love disqualifies; at Luke 16:13 the King closes the steward parable with *ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon*.
7951.old_note: *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 31:5). The Lukan placement seals the unjust-steward parable with the mammon-verdict: *Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon* (Luke 16:13). The wisdom-stream had already named the disqualification at the gold-love level — the gold-lover *shall not be justified.* The King names the same architecture as a forced-choice of masters: the divided heart that holds to mammon cannot stand justified before the Father whose service is whole-heart. The Lukan setting is distinct from the Sermon — here the verdict closes a steward-parable about deploying mammon shrewdly before the books are called.

7952.new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?* (Luke 24:26). On the road to Emmaus the King asks the two disciples whether the Messiah (Christ) ought not to have suffered these things and then enter his glory. Wisdom had already written the glory half: the righteous man, condemned in chapter 2 to a shameful death, now standing in great boldness before the faces of the men who did it. Suffering first, then the standing, is the shape he then shows them in Moses and all the prophets, and the Hebrew library had the same shape in Solomon's hand long before Luke wrote it down.
7952.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The glory the Messiah (Christ) enters after suffering (Luke 24:26) is this standing in boldness before those who afflicted him.
7952.old_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1) The Hebrew library names the glory-half — the righteous man, condemned with a shameful death in chapter 2, now standing in great boldness before those who afflicted him, vindicated and numbered among the children of Yahuah (God). *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?* (Luke 24:26): the enter-into-his-glory the King names is this standing-in-boldness Wisdom names — the suffering-then-vindication arc the wisdom-stream chronicled and the prophets spoke, the reading-method the King opens to the disciples beginning at Mosheh (Moses) and all the prophets.

7953.new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?* (Luke 24:26). On the road to Emmaus Yahusha (Jesus) asked the slow of heart why they were surprised. Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered? The suffering was written — in Moses, in the prophets, and here in Wisdom, where the just man who calls Yahuah (God) his father is sentenced to a shameful death by the men who lay in wait for him. The disciples had read the glory and skipped the suffering. The whole library had both halves on the page, and the King opened their eyes to read them together.
7953.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* The suffering half the Emmaus disciples could not read — *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things* (Luke 24:26).
7953.old_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20) The Hebrew library names the righteous-one-condemned-with-a-shameful-death architecture — the just man, who calls himself the child of Yahuah (God), condemned to a shameful death by those who lie in wait for him. *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?* (Luke 24:26): the suffering-half of the King's reading-method to the Emmaus disciples is the shameful-death Wisdom names — the righteous one delivered to condemnation, the very pattern the prophets and the wisdom-stream had been carrying that the slow-of-heart disciples could not read.

7960.new_note: *And of all lands of the whole world you have chosen you one pit: and of all the flowers thereof one lily:* (2 Esdras 5:24). *He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, Elohim (God) forbid.* (Luke 20:16). Ezra's prayer counts the Most High's choices one by one: one vine, one pit, one lily, one river, one city, one dove, one sheep, and at last one people (2 Esdras 5:23–27). When the parable ends with the vineyard given to others, those who heard it cried out against it, as though the chosen vine itself were being handed to a different people. But it is the husbandmen who are destroyed, not the vineyard. What passes to others is the keeping of the one vine; the vine the Most High chose out of all the lands of the whole world remains the one he chose.
7960.member_note: 2 Esdras 5:24 — *of all lands of the whole world you have chosen you one pit.* At Luke 20:16 the keeping passes to others; the chosen vine stays the Most High's own.
7960.old_note: *And of all lands of the whole world you have chosen you one pit: and of all the flowers thereof one lily.* (2 Esdras 5:24) Ezra's litany of the one-chosen-out-of-all continues — one vine, one pit, one lily, one river, one city, one dove, one sheep, one people. *He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, Elohim (God) forbid* (Luke 20:16): the vineyard given to others is not the chosen-vine replaced by a different people; it is the keeping of the one-only-vine taken from the failed husbandmen and given to faithful keepers. The vine remains the one Yashar'el (Israel) the Most High chose; the stewardship of it changes hands.

7961.new_note: *And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.* (2 Esdras 5:27). *Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.* (Luke 20:9). The vineyard a certain man plants and lets out is the one people Ezra names, loved out of all the multitudes and given a law that is approved of all. The fruit the owner later sends his servants to collect is the fruit that law was given to bring, a people keeping what they were given. The husbandmen hold the vineyard while refusing its fruit; that is a leadership that keeps the title to the people while setting aside the law the people were planted under. The prayer and the parable agree on what the vineyard is and what it was planted for.
7961.member_note: 2 Esdras 5:27 — *to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.* The vineyard let out at Luke 20:9 is this people, and the fruit sought is the law kept.
7961.old_note: *And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.* (2 Esdras 5:27) The wisdom-stream names the one-people-given-the-law substance behind the vineyard-parable: the vine is the one people the Most High loved and to whom He gave the Torah. *A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen* (Luke 20:9): the vineyard let out is this one beloved people; the fruit the lord of the vineyard sends his servants to gather is the covenant-keeping the law was given for. The husbandmen who refuse the fruit and kill the heir are the leadership that holds the vine while voiding the law it was planted under.

7980.new_note: *Then said Judas and his brothers, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.* (1 Maccabees 4:36). *And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.* (John 2:16). Judas and his brothers, with the enemy beaten back, go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary the heathen had defiled. Generations later Yahusha (Jesus) walks into the same house and drives out the sellers, saying make not my Father's house an house of merchandise. The Maccabees cleansed what Antiochus had polluted with his idol; the King cleansed what the priests had polluted with their market. It is the same motion, the house of Yahuah (God) purged of what does not belong in it, and the second time it is done by the Son whose Father's house it is.
7980.member_note: 1 Maccabees 4:36 — *let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.* The King cleansed the same house: make not my Father's house an house of merchandise (John 2:16).
7980.old_note: *Then said Judas and his brothers, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.* (1 Maccabees 4:36) The Hebrew library carries the prior cleansing of the defiled house — the Hasmonean *go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.* *Make not my Father's house an house of merchandise* (John 2:16) is the same purging-of-the-defiled-house motion, now in the hand of the One whose house it is. The Maccabees cleansed the sanctuary the heathen profaned; the Formed one cleanses the court the traders profaned, the Lord of the house returning to purge His own.

7983.new_note: *They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:21). *But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.* (John 4:14). Wisdom tells the truth about herself: the one who drinks of her will be thirsty again, and the student goes back to the well as long as he lives. The woman at the well was told of water that would end that going back, because the well itself would be set inside the one who drank it. Yahusha (Jesus) is not the abolition of the wisdom that left the drinker thirsty; he is what that wisdom was drawing the thirsty toward, the Word the Torah kept sending a man back to, now a spring in him that does not run dry.
7983.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:21 — *they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.* The thirst that keeps a man coming back to Wisdom; at John 4:14 that same Wisdom in flesh sets the well inside him, *a well of water springing up into everlasting life*.
7983.reason: Reworded the old note's point. It had Wisdom confessing a limit that Yahusha answers, which sets the Wisdom of Ecclesiasticus 24 below him; by the skill that Wisdom is the Formed one himself, so the note now reads the thirst as the appetite for more of the same Word, with John 4:14 as that Word dwelling within.
7983.old_note: *They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 24:21) Wisdom names her own limit in the Hebrew library: the one who drinks of her *shall yet be thirsty* — the study returns one again and again to the well. *Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life* (John 4:14) is the answer to the wisdom-stream's own confession. The Formed one is not the abolition of the wisdom that left the drinker thirsty; He is the well springing up within, the substance the Torah-wisdom drew the thirsty toward.

7985.new_note: *Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.* (Baruch 3:37). *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* (John 3:13). Baruch closes his search for wisdom with a sentence most Bibles no longer carry: afterward he shewed himself upon earth, and conversed with men. The one who alone knows the way of knowledge came down and walked among men. John 3:13 is the same event from the inside; the Son of Adam who came down from heaven is the only one who was ever up there. Baruch said the descent would come; Nicodemus was sitting across from it. The wisdom no man could fetch down from the clouds was in the room, talking with him.
7985.member_note: Baruch 3:37 — *Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.* The descent John 3:13 names: the Son of Adam who came down from heaven.
7985.old_note: *Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.* (Baruch 3:37) The Hebrew library closes the wisdom-search by naming the descent: the One who alone knows wisdom *shewed himself upon earth, and conversed with men.* This is the substance of John 3:13 — the Son of Adam who *came down from heaven* is the One Baruch says shewed himself on earth and walked among men, the wisdom no man could fetch down now standing in flesh in front of Nicodemus.

7986.new_note: *Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?* (Baruch 3:30). *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* (John 3:13). Baruch piles up the impossibility. No one has gone up to heaven to bring wisdom down, and no one has crossed the sea to find her and buy her with pure gold; *No man knoweth her way, nor thinketh of her path* (Baruch 3:31). Yahusha (Jesus) tells Nicodemus that no man has ascended to heaven but the one who came down from it. The reaching Baruch rules out, upward or outward, is answered from the other direction. The Son of Adam did not have to search for wisdom over the sea, because he came down from where she dwells, and he sat in front of Nicodemus as the thing no gold could buy.
7986.member_note: Baruch 3:30 — *Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold.* Wisdom past man's reach; the Son of Adam came down from where she dwells (John 3:13).
7986.old_note: *Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?* (Baruch 3:30) The wisdom-stream stacks the impossibility — wisdom cannot be reached over the sea any more than up to heaven; she is past the searching of the son of Adam. John 3:13's *no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven* names the One who did not have to search for her because He came down from where she dwells. The reaching the Hebrew library forecloses to man is answered by the descent of the Son of Adam.

7987.new_note: *Who has gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?* (Baruch 3:29). *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* (John 3:13). Baruch asks a question meant to have no answer: who has gone up into heaven and taken wisdom and brought her down? No one, is the expected reply; wisdom is beyond the reach of any son of Adam. Then Yahusha (Jesus) tells Nicodemus that no man has ascended to heaven except the one who came down from it, the Son of Adam. He is the answer Baruch's question was waiting for. The wisdom no man could climb to fetch came down herself, in flesh; Wisdom of Solomon 9 and Ecclesiasticus 24 had already set her beside the Maker, and John 3:13 names the one who was there and came down.
7987.member_note: Baruch 3:29 — *Who has gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds.* The question John 3:13 answers: the Son of Adam came down.
7987.old_note: *Who has gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?* (Baruch 3:29) The Hebrew library asks the rhetorical question — no son of Adam can ascend to heaven to fetch the wisdom of Elohim (God) down. *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven* (John 3:13) is the answer the question waited for: the One who came down is the only One who was ever up there to bring it. The ascent the wisdom-stream says no man can make is the descent the Formed Son already made.

7994.new_note: *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels’ bread.* (2 Esdras 1:19). *For the bread of Elohim (God) is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.* (John 6:33). The manna was angels' bread, 2 Esdras says, given out of the Father's pity. In John, Yahusha (Jesus) tells the crowd that the bread of Elohim (God) is he which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world, and a few verses on he says it outright, I am the bread of life. The fathers ate angels' bread in the wilderness and died; the bread the Father sends now is a person, and the life he gives does not end at the edge of the wilderness. The manna was real bread and a real sign, and the one it signified stood in the synagogue at Capernaum and said so.
7994.member_note: 2 Esdras 1:19 — *so you did eat angels’ bread.* The bread of Elohim (God) that comes down from heaven is the one the manna pointed to (John 6:33).
7994.old_note: *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels' bread.* 2 Esdras 1:19 names the wilderness manna as *angels' bread* given out of the Father's pity on the hungry people — the same heaven-sent provision John 6:33 walks: *the bread of Elohim (God) is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.* The Hebrew library names the bread the fathers ate as angels' bread; the Formed one names himself as the bread of Elohim (God) come down from heaven, the substance the angels' bread of the wilderness was prefiguring.

7995.new_note: *That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:26). *Then Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.* (John 6:32). The manna was teaching that it is the word of Yahuah (God), not the harvest, that keeps his children alive. Yahusha (Jesus) says Moses did not give the bread from heaven; the Father did, and the Father is now giving the true bread. The word that preserved the wilderness generation is standing in front of the crowd in flesh, the Word made flesh who is himself the bread. What the manna said in a picture, he says in person.
7995.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* The word that preserved the wilderness is the true bread the Father now gives (John 6:32).
7995.old_note: *That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 names the substance the manna was teaching — *it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man, but thy word* — the wisdom-stream's reading of the manna as a sign pointing to the word that sustains. John 6:32-33's *my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven ... the bread of Elohim (God) is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world* lands that word on the Formed one in flesh: the Word made flesh is the word the manna pointed toward, taken into the inward man.

7996.new_note: *Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20). *Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.* (John 6:31). The crowd at Capernaum quotes the manna back at him as the high mark of what heaven has ever given. The library agrees with them about the manna: it was angels' food, sent from heaven without their labour, fitted to every taste. Yahusha (Jesus) does not take a word of it back; he says the Father who sent that bread is now giving the true bread, and the true bread is himself (John 6:32, 35). The manna was real and it was heaven's, and it was pointing past itself to the one who came down.
7996.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *you feddest your own people with angels’ food.* The crowd cites the same wilderness bread, *He gave them bread from heaven to eat* (John 6:31).
7996.old_note: *Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels' food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 names the manna as *angels' food ... bread prepared without their labour ... agreeing to every taste* — the Hebrew library's register for the wilderness bread the crowd cites at John 6:31: *our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.* The wisdom-stream had already named the manna heaven-sent and labourless, serving every taste; the Formed one takes the same bread-from-heaven tradition and lands it on his own body as the true bread the manna prefigured.

8003.new_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* (John 11:52). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. John says Yahusha (Jesus) would die not for that nation only but to gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad. The scattered children are Jacob's tribes among the nations; the one nation in the land was Yahudah (Judah). Sirach prayed for the gathering, and John names the death that pays for it; Caiaphas said more than he knew.
8003.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together.* The children of Elohim (God) scattered abroad (John 11:52) are the tribes this prayer asks home.
8003.old_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:11 names the gather-all-the-tribes-of-Jacob prayer in the Hebrew library's wisdom-stream — the explicit petition for the gathering of the scattered tribes back into the inheritance, *as from the beginning.* John 11:52's *gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad* walks the same architecture: the gathering Caiaphas prophesies without understanding is the gathering of all the tribes of Jacob the Hebrew library was already praying for. The wisdom-stream prays it; the gospel names the death that accomplishes it.

8004.new_note: *For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.* (Baruch 5:9). *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* (John 11:52). Baruch's song ends with the gathering complete: Yahuah (God) leads Yashar'el (Israel) home with joy in the light of his glory. John names what the death of Yahusha (Jesus) accomplished in the same terms, gathering into one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad. The scattered children and Yashar'el (Israel) led home are one people; John's into one is Baruch's led with joy. The mercy and righteousness that come from him in Baruch came in the flesh in John, and the gathering they promised runs through the cross.
8004.member_note: Baruch 5:9 — *with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.* Yashar'el (Israel) led home with joy is the scattered children gathered into one (John 11:52).
8004.old_note: *For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.* Baruch 5:9 names the leading-home-of-Yashar'el (Israel) — the gathering completed, the scattered led home in the light of the glory. John 11:52's gathering of the scattered children into one is the gospel-form of the same homecoming the Hebrew library names: Yashar'el (Israel) led home with joy in the glory, the children scattered abroad gathered into one.

8005.new_note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 5:5). *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* (John 11:52). Baruch says it twice, once in chapter 4 and again here, so no one misses it: Jerusalem's children are gathered by the word of the Holy One, from the east and from the west. John says the death of Yahusha (Jesus) was to gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad. Scattered abroad is where Baruch's children went; gathered into one is where they are going. The homecoming Baruch sang from the captivity is the homecoming John says the cross was for.
8005.member_note: Baruch 5:5 — *your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One.* The scattered children gathered into one (John 11:52).
8005.old_note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).* Baruch 5:5 names the children-gathered-from-the-west-to-the-east architecture again, doubled with Baruch 4:37 for emphasis — the scattered children brought home by the word of the Holy One. John 11:52's *gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad* walks the same Hebrew library gathering: the scattered children of the covenant brought home into one.

8006.new_note: *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 4:37). *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* (John 11:52). Baruch sees the sons Jerusalem sent away coming gathered from east to west by the word of the Holy One. John explains the death of Yahusha (Jesus) in the same terms: not for that nation only, but to gather into one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad. The scattered children are not the nations; they are Jerusalem's own sons, sent away in the scattering, the ones Hosea said would be called sons of the living Elohim (God) in the very place they were called not his people (Hosea 1:10). Baruch names the gathering by the word of the Holy One; John names the death that does the gathering.
8006.member_note: Baruch 4:37 — *they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One.* The scattered children of Elohim (God) gathered into one (John 11:52).
8006.old_note: *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).* Baruch 4:37 names the gathering-of-the-scattered-children architecture — the sons sent away in the scattering, gathered home from east to west by the word of the Holy One. John 11:52's *and not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad* walks the same architecture: the death of the Formed one gathers the scattered children home. The Hebrew library names the children gathered by the word of the Holy One; the gospel names the One whose death gathers them into one.

8009.new_note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). *Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.* (John 11:24). Martha, grieving, says what the Hebrew library had taught her: her brother will rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Ezra was told the same thing in fuller words, that the earth will restore those asleep in her and the secret places will deliver the souls committed to them. Martha's hope is not a vague comfort; it is this promise. And the one standing in front of her is about to call Lazarus out of the grave (John 11:43–44), a first sign of the day Ezra was shown.
8009.member_note: 2 Esdras 7:32 — *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her.* Martha's resurrection at the last day (John 11:24) is this promise, and Lazarus is its first sign.
8009.old_note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* 2 Esdras 7:32 names the resurrection-at-the-last-day architecture — the earth restoring the sleeping, the dust giving back those in silence. Martha's *I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day* (John 11:24) names the same Hebrew library hope. The earth giving back its dead is the resurrection the Hebrew library held; the raising of Lazaros at John 11:43-44 is the firstfruit-sign of it — *Lazarus, come forth.*

8010.new_note: *And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another.* (2 Esdras 13:33). *My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:* (John 10:27). When the Son is declared, Ezra is told, all the people hear his voice and every man leaves his battle in his own land. Yahusha (Jesus) says his sheep hear his voice, and he knows them, and they follow him. The hearing is what shows who they are; the ones who leave their fighting when he speaks are the ones who were his. His voice does not make sheep; it calls the sheep out of the battle they were in.
8010.member_note: 2 Esdras 13:33 — *when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land leave the battle.* My sheep hear my voice (John 10:27); the hearing shows who they were.
8010.old_note: *And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another.* 2 Esdras 13:33 names the hearing-of-the-voice of the Son who is declared — the people hearing his voice and turning. John 10:27's *my sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me* walks the same architecture: the hearing reveals the sheep. The Hebrew library names the voice of the declared Son that the people hear; the gospel names the same voice the sheep hear and follow, because the hearing discloses what they already were.

8020.new_note: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:23). *I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.* (John 15:5). A few verses earlier Wisdom said she brought forth pleasant savour as the vine, and now Sirach tells us plainly what that vine is: the book of the covenant, the law Moses commanded as the inheritance of Jacob. When Yahusha (Jesus) says he is the vine and his disciples are the branches, he is not planting a new vine beside the old one. To abide in him is to abide in the Word the Father spoke, the same covenant Torah Sirach named as Wisdom. A branch cut from the vine bears nothing, and a man cut off from the Word bears nothing, because the vine and the Word are one.
8020.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:23 — *the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded.* Wisdom's vine named as the Torah itself; to abide in the true vine of John 15:5 is to abide in the Word the Father spoke.
8020.old_note: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 24:23 names the Wisdom-vine of the hymn as the Torah itself — the book of the covenant, the law Moses commanded as the inheritance of Jacob. John 15:5's *I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing* walks the same architecture: to abide in the true vine is to abide in the Word the Father spoke, the covenant-Torah the wisdom-stream named as the vine — for the branch bears nothing severed from the vine, as the keeper bears nothing severed from the Word.

8021.new_note: *As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:17). *I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.* (John 15:1). In the great hymn of Wisdom she calls herself a vine, bringing forth pleasant savour, her flowers the fruit of honour and riches — the same Wisdom the Creator commanded to take root in Jacob, and whom Sirach goes on to name as the book of the covenant, the law Moses commanded. Yahusha (Jesus) says I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. The Wisdom planted as a vine in Yashar'el (Israel) is the one who stood on the earth and said so; the Word that became flesh is the vine the branches abide in and bear from. The husbandman is the Father, and the vine is his Formed one.
8021.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:17 — *As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour.* The vine of Wisdom planted in Jacob is the true vine of John 15:1.
8021.old_note: *As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.* Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 24:17 names Wisdom-as-the-vine in the great Wisdom-hymn — the same Wisdom who, commanded by the Creator, took root in Jacob and Yashar'el (Israel): *Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel)* (24:8). John 15:1's *I am the true vine* gathers this figure: the Wisdom-vine planted in Jacob, which the wisdom-stream then names outright as the Torah (24:23), is the vine the Formed one declares himself to be — the Word made flesh, the true vine in whom the branches abide and bear.

8028.new_note: *He has mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:14). *He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Adonai (Lord), thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, Feed my sheep.* (John 21:17). Sirach says mercy falls on the one who receives discipline. Peter was grieved at the third asking — three questions answering three denials — and he did not turn away from it; he received it, and the mercy landed not as condemnation but as a charge to feed the sheep. That is the pattern Sirach names: the discipline is received, the judgments of Yahuah (God) are sought, and the mercy follows.
8028.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 18:14 — *He has mercy on them that receive discipline.* Peter, grieved at the third asking, receives the discipline and the mercy lands as *Feed my sheep* (John 21:17).
8028.old_note: *He has mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 18:14) The wisdom-stream names the mercy-on-the-disciplined register the restoration of Peter walks: Yahuah (God) *has mercy on them that receive discipline.* Peter, grieved at the third asking, receives the discipline of the threefold question that answers his threefold denial, and the mercy lands not in condemnation but in the threefold charge to *feed my sheep.* The wisdom-stream had already named the architecture: the mercy of the Father falls on the one who receives the discipline and seeks his judgments.

8029.new_note: *Up then, and eat bread, and forsake us not, as the shepherd that leaveth his flock in the hands of cruel wolves.* (2 Esdras 5:18). *So when they had dined, Yahusha (Jesus) saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Adonai (Lord); thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.* (John 21:15). Phaltiel the captain finds Ezra fasting in the field and begs him not to leave the people the way a shepherd leaves his flock to the wolves, because Yashar'el (Israel) in the land of their captivity had been committed to him. The risen Yahusha (Jesus) sets bread before Peter and then asks him three times whether he loves him, once for each denial, and every answer comes back as a charge to feed the flock. Peter had forsaken his Master on the night of the trial; now he is told plainly what love looks like in a shepherd: eat the bread set before you, and do not leave the lambs to the wolves. The picture Phaltiel used as a warning is the very failure the threefold charge turns around.
8029.member_note: 2 Esdras 5:18 — *forsake us not, as the shepherd that leaveth his flock in the hands of cruel wolves.* Peter, who forsook three times, is charged three times to feed the flock (John 21:15).
8029.old_note: *Up then, and eat bread, and forsake us not, as the shepherd that leaveth his flock in the hands of cruel wolves.* (2 Esdras 5:18) The wisdom-stream names the failure the restoration of Peter answers: the shepherd who *leaveth his flock in the hands of cruel wolves* is the shepherd who forsakes. Peter, who forsook and denied his Master three times, is here charged three times — *feed my lambs ... feed my sheep ... feed my sheep* — not to be the shepherd who leaves the flock to the wolves, but the one who eats the bread the risen Messiah set before him and does not forsake. The negative image of the abandoning shepherd is the exact ground the threefold recommission reverses.

8030.new_note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:13). *He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Adonai (Lord); thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.* (John 21:16). The shepherd Sirach describes is Yahuah (God) himself — reproving, nurturing, teaching, bringing the flock back again. On the shore Yahusha (Jesus) does exactly that to Peter: the second asking is the reproof, the answer is the nurture, and the charge to feed my sheep is the bringing again. Then he hands that same work to the man he has just restored. The one who was brought back is sent to bring back the flock.
8030.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 18:13 — *he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* The Father's own shepherding, handed to the restored Peter in *Feed my sheep* (John 21:16).
8030.old_note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 18:13) The wisdom-stream names the shepherd-architecture John 21:16's *feed my sheep* commission walks: Yahuah (God) *reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* The risen Messiah hands the shepherd-charge to Peter — to nurture and bring again the flock the way the wisdom-stream names the Father himself shepherding. The reproof-and-restoration the wisdom-stream names of the Father is the very pattern enacted on Peter (reproved by the threefold question, restored by the threefold charge) and then committed to him for the sheep.

8031.new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *When Yahusha (Jesus) therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.* (John 19:30). The ungodly set the terms: if he is the son, his Father will pull him out of their hands. On the cross the terms were met in a way they never imagined. Yahusha (Jesus) did not come down; he finished the work and gave up the ghost. The deliverance came on the third day, not by escape but by resurrection — exactly where Wisdom goes next, when the chapter turns: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1).
8031.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* The deliverance came through *It is finished* (John 19:30) and the third day, not by coming down from the cross.
8031.old_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18) The wisdom-stream put the mocking test in the mouth of the ungodly: if the just man is truly the son of Yahuah (God), let his Father deliver him from his enemies' hand. John 19:30's *it is finished* answers the test not by escape but by completion — the just man who is the Son does not come down from the cross; he finishes the work, and the vindication the ungodly demanded as proof comes in the resurrection the wisdom-stream itself names three verses on, *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God).*

8032.new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *When the chief priests therefore and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Take ye him, and crucify him: for I find no fault in him.* (John 19:6). Wisdom gives the resolve; John gives the shout. Let us condemn him with a shameful death becomes Crucify him, crucify him in the mouths of the chief priests and officers. Pilate found no fault in him, and still the death was demanded — not for any crime, but because he called Yahuah (God) his father and his life exposed theirs. The crucifixion is the shameful death Wisdom said the ungodly would lay on the just man.
8032.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* The resolve that became *Crucify him, crucify him* at John 19:6.
8032.old_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20) This is the wisdom-stream's framework-bearing sentence for the crucifixion: the ungodly resolve to *condemn him with a shameful death.* John 19:6's *crucify him, crucify him* is that resolve enacted — the shameful death the wisdom-stream named, demanded by the chief priests against the righteous one who called Yahuah (God) his father. The crucifixion is the shameful death the wisdom-stream foretold the ungodly would impose on the just man.

8033.new_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). *Then came Yahusha (Jesus) forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them, Behold the man!* (John 19:5). Here is the program the ungodly lay out: despitefulness and torture, to see what the righteous man's meekness and patience are made of. John 19 shows it carried out to the letter — Pilate scourged him, the soldiers wove him a crown of thorns and dressed him in purple and struck him, and then he was led out before the crowd. Behold the man. He came forth meek and patient under the very test Wisdom said the ungodly would devise, and the test proved what they refused to see.
8033.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 — *that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* The scourging and the crown of thorns at John 19:1–5 are this test carried out, and *Behold the man* is the answer.
8033.old_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19) The wisdom-stream names the scourging-and-mockery program the ungodly devise for the righteous one: *examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* John 19:1-5 walks the same — Pilate scourges him, the soldiers crown him with thorns and smite him, and he is brought forth meek and patient under the *despitefulness and torture* the wisdom-stream had already named as the test the ungodly impose on the just.

8034.new_note: *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16). *Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Yahudim (Jews), and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all.* (John 18:38). Pilate looked for a crime and found none. The men pressing for his death had no crime to show either, only what Wisdom had already named: a man whose life rebuked theirs and who made his boast that Yahuah (God) was his father. That was the whole charge — he claimed the Father as his own, and his righteousness made their religion look like counterfeit. The fault the ungodly find in the just is never a crime; it is the reproof they feel just by standing near him.
8034.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* Pilate found no fault at all (John 18:38); the only charge was the one Wisdom named.
8034.old_note: *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16) The righteous one of the wisdom-stream is grievous to the ungodly precisely because his life is of *another fashion* and he *makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* John 18:38's Pilate finds *no fault at all* in him, yet the chief priests press for his death on exactly the ground the wisdom-stream named — that he claims the Father as his own. The fault the ungodly find is not a crime; it is the righteousness that reproves them.

8035.new_note: *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13). *The Yahudim (Jews) answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of Elohim (God).* (John 19:7). The charge the accusers bring to Pilate, *by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of Elohim (God)*, is word for word the complaint Wisdom of Solomon put in the mouth of the ungodly against the righteous one: he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God). What the plotters of Wisdom 2 treat as the offence worth killing for is what the chief priests treat as the capital offence at the trial. They did not invent the charge; they inherited it from men who had been laying in wait for the righteous since before there was a Pilate to bring it to. And the law they appealed to was the law his life had been reproving them with.
8035.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The capital charge of John 19:7, he made himself the Son of Elohim (God), is the complaint Wisdom 2:13 gives the ungodly.
8035.old_note: *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13) The charge the Yahudim (Jews) bring at John 19:7 — *we have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of Elohim (God)* — is the exact accusation the wisdom-stream put in the mouth of the ungodly against the righteous one: that *he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The self-designation that the ungodly treat as the capital offence in Wisdom 2 is the self-designation the chief priests treat as the capital offence at the trial.

8036.new_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.* (John 18:3). The arrest at night is the lying in wait. Judas comes with a band of men and officers sent by the chief priests and Pharisees, with lanterns and torches and weapons, for one unarmed man in a garden. Wisdom of Solomon had already named the motive: the righteous one is clean contrary to their doings and upbraids them with their offending the law. The plot against the righteous one is not a New Testament novelty; the ungodly had been lying in wait for the just man who reproves them for as long as there have been just men, and the torches in Gethsemane are that old resolve carried out.
8036.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous.* The band with lanterns and torches at John 18:3 is the lying in wait of the ungodly for the righteous one who reproves them.
8036.old_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12) The Hebrew library's wisdom-stream names the architecture the arrest at John 18:3 walks: the band of men and officers from the chief priests *lie in wait for the righteous* one because he is *clean contrary* to their doings and *upbraideth* them with their offending the law. The plot against the righteous one is not a New Testament novelty; the wisdom-stream had already named the lying-in-wait of the ungodly against the just man who reproves them.

11561.new_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). *By one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin* (Romans 5:12). The older witness names the deeper root: death came into the world *through envy of the devil* — for *Yahuah (God) created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:23). The serpent of the garden is the envy behind the one man's fall; death is the intruder, not the Maker's design.

12154.new_note: *And when we were carried away captives to Nineve, all my brothers and those that were of my kindred did eat of the bread of the Gentiles.* (Tobit 1:10). *For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs* (Romans 14:2). The weak brother who *eateth herbs* is doing in Rome what Tobit did in the captivity — refusing the meat of the heathen table, whose slaughter and offering could not be trusted. The abstaining is a conscience guarding itself from defilement by association, not a verdict that the Torah's own clean food had changed.

12188.new_note: *And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.* (Tobit 14:6). *It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.* (Romans 15:27). Paul is carrying a collection from the assemblies among the Gentiles to the poor saints at Jerusalem, and he calls it a debt: they received spiritual things from Jerusalem, so they owe carnal things back. The Gentiles Paul writes to are, for the most part, the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) living as Gentiles among the nations, the people Tobit said would be gathered home. Tobit saw two things coming: his people gathered home, and the nations turning to fear Yahuah (God) truly and burying their idols, with his own people confessing him and being exalted in the next line. The collection belongs to the first of those. It is the gathering made tangible in one generation: the scattered children of Yashar'el (Israel), who had lived among the idols, sending back to Jerusalem what they owed for the spiritual things that came out of it, the idols left behind and the debt of love paid.
12188.member_note: Tobit 14:6 — *all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.* The collection for Jerusalem is the turning made tangible, carnal things paid back for spiritual things received (Romans 15:27).

12213.new_note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). *Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;* (Hebrews 1:3). A pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: Wisdom describes something that comes out of the glory without lessening it. Hebrews puts a person where Wisdom put a picture. The Son is the brightness of his glory and the express image of his person, the way light shining is of the light and yet is not the lamp. He proceeds from the Father as brightness proceeds from light, the Formed shining out from the Formless: Elohim (God) who has a Father, the one who upholds all things by the word of his power and then sat down at the right hand of the one he came from.
12213.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 — *a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.* What flows out from the glory without lessening it is a person in Hebrews 1:3, the brightness of his glory.
12213.old_note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). *A pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty* — the older book describes what flows out from the glory without diminishing it, and Hebrews fastens that same picture to a person: *the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person* (Hebrews 1:3). The Son proceeds from the Father as brightness proceeds from light, the same in substance, distinct in standing — Elohim who has a Father, the Formed who shines out the Formless.

13139.new_note: *He answered and said to me, These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of Yahuah (God): now are they crowned, and receive palms.* (2 Esdras 2:45). The white-robed palm-bearers of Revelation 7 are named in the restored library: *now are they crowned, and receive palms.* The elder asks *what are these which are arrayed in white robes?* (Revelation 7:13) and answers *these are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes* (Revelation 7:14). Esdras tells the same: they that *put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal,* who *confessed the name of Yahuah (God)* — the same company, robed and palm-bearing, who came through tribulation into glory.

14230.new_note: *Therefore the righteous spoiled the ungodly, and praised your holy name, O Yahuah (God), and magnified with one accord yours hand, that fought for them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:20). The Hebrew library remembers the same scene: the righteous *Brought them through the Red sea* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:18), their enemies drowned, and then *with one accord* they praise the holy name of the One *that fought for them.* This is exactly the posture of those who *had gotten the victory... having the harps of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 15:2), who *glorify thy name* (15:4). The redeemed praising with one accord after the sea is the song of Moses; the seer sees it sung again, the same hand that fought at the Red Sea fighting still.

15208.new_note: *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). The library tells what the eye of the ungodly cannot see: *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God)... yet is their hope full of immortality* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1–4), a reward the ungodly *neither hoped... nor discerned* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:22). This is the unseen thing Paul means — *the things which Elohim (God) hath prepared for them that love him* (1 Corinthians 2:9), which *eye hath not seen.* The reward hidden from the world's wisdom is the immortal hope kept for the righteous, prepared before the world and disclosed by the Spirit.

15943.new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die... but they are in peace... yet is their hope full of immortality* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:2–4): the library holds that what looks like death and dishonour to the world is, for the righteous, the threshold of immortality. 39109.new_note: *Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:19). *For the ear of jealousy heareth all things: and the noise of murmurings is not hid.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:10). Sirach describes the man who fears only the eyes of men and forgets that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, searching out the most secret places. The Wisdom of Solomon says the same of his hearing — the ear of jealousy hears everything, and murmuring is not hidden. Nothing done in the dark and nothing muttered under the breath escapes him. The two books together close every hiding place: he sees what the walls cover and hears what the voice keeps low.

39384.new_note: *When the ungodly perished, she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:6). *And, in like manner, Elohim (God) will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites, like to the judgment of Sodom.* (Jubilees 16:6). Jubilees goes on in the next verse to tell how Lot was saved because Elohim (God) remembered Abraham and sent him out of the midst of the overthrow; Wisdom names the same deliverance from the other side — the righteous man delivered from the fire that fell on the five cities. The judgment on Sodom and the rescue of the righteous out of it are one act, told in both books.
