44777.new_note: *That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth;* (2 Maccabees 4:14). *But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* (Malachi 2:8). Under Jason the priests lost their stomach for the altar. They despised the temple, neglected the sacrifices, and ran to the Greek gymnasium when the discus called, taking their share of what the Torah forbade. Malachi had already said what that is: priests departed out of the way, causing many to stumble at the law, corrupting the covenant of Levi. The threat to the temple in these chapters did not begin with Antiochus; it began at the altar, with the men set apart to serve there. The covenant of Levi was broken from the inside before any king broke in.

44786.new_note: *Promising to the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents:* (2 Maccabees 4:8). *The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon Yahuah (LORD), and say, Is not Yahuah (LORD) among us? none evil can come upon us.* (Micah 3:11). Jason did not inherit the high priesthood; he bought it. He went to Antiochus behind his brother Onias and promised three hundred and sixty talents of silver, with eighty more from another revenue, to be made high priest. Micah had already named that transaction: heads who judge for reward, priests who teach for hire, prophets who divine for money, all of them still saying Yahuah (LORD) is among us and no evil can come. The office was turned into a purchase, and the chapters that follow show how much evil did come. A priesthood bought for silver is the thing the prophet condemned, in whatever age it appears.

44866.new_note: *Nevertheless upon the fifth day early twenty young men of Maccabeus’ company, inflamed with anger because of the blasphemies, assaulted the wall manly, and with a fierce courage killed all that they met withal.* (2 Maccabees 10:35). *Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.* (Numbers 25:11). The men inside the city trusted their walls and blasphemed from them, and on the fifth day twenty of Judas's young men, inflamed by the blasphemies, went up the wall. The book names the cause of their anger: not the siege, not the plunder, but the blasphemies. That is the zeal of Phinehas. Yahuah (God) said Phinehas turned his wrath away from Yashar'el (Israel) because he was zealous for his sake, and for that zeal gave him a covenant of peace (Numbers 25:12–13). 45038.new_note: *And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, making merry before Yahuah (God),* (1 Esdras 7:14). *Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us:* (1 Corinthians 5:7). The exiles had come up out of Babylon, and the first thing they did after the Passover was keep the seven days of unleavened bread, glad before Yahuah (God). Paul writes to an assembly far from Jerusalem and tells them to purge out the old leaven for the same reason, because Messiah (Christ) our Passover has been slain, and the next line says it plainly, let us keep the feast. The lamb being slain did not end the feast; it is the reason the feast is kept. The returned remnant and the assembly at Corinth are keeping the same appointed days, and the one the days point to is Yahusha (Jesus).

45051.new_note: *O Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), you are true: for we are left a root this day.* (1 Esdras 8:89). *O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), thou art righteous: for we remain yet escaped, as it is this day: behold, we are before thee in our trespasses: for we cannot stand before thee because of this.* (Ezra 9:15). These are the same prayer told twice, once by Ezra and once by Esdras. In both, the man kneels with torn garments and confesses that Yahuah (God) is righteous and the people are not, that they are a root left this day, a remnant yet escaped, and that they cannot stand before him because of what they have done. The confession does not plead the people's merit; it pleads his faithfulness, you are true. A root left and a remnant escaped is how Yahuah (God) keeps his word to the fathers when the sons have broken theirs.

45054.new_note: *For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.* (1 Esdras 8:70). *But yet in it shall be a tenth, and it shall return, and shall be eaten: as a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance is in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.* (Isaiah 6:13). Both verses call the people the holy seed, and both mean a bloodline. Esdras rends his garment because the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) has been mixed with the strange people of the land, and the rulers led the way in it. Isaiah had already said what would become of that seed: the tree is cut down to a stump, a tenth returns, and the holy seed is what remains alive in the stump when everything else is eaten away. The grief in Esdras and the promise in Isaiah are about the same seed, and the promise is that Yahuah (God) keeps it through the cutting.

45078.new_note: *And that whoever met not there within two or three days according as the elders that bare rule appointed, their cattle should be seized to the use of the temple, and himself cast out from them that were of the captivity.* (1 Esdras 9:4). *And that whosoever would not come within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and the elders, all his substance should be forfeited, and himself separated from the congregation of those that had been carried away.* (Ezra 10:8). Ezra and 1 Esdras record the same proclamation. Everyone of the captivity was to gather at Jerusalem within three days, and whoever stayed away forfeited his goods and was cut off from the congregation of the returned. The matter was the strange wives, and the remedy began with the whole remnant standing together in one place before anything was decided. The two accounts agree on the terms, the goods seized for the temple and the man put out, so the reader can watch one event through two witnesses.

45181.new_note: *And when the world, that shall begin to vanish away, shall be finished, then will I shew these tokens: the books shall be opened before the firmament, and they shall see all together:* (2 Esdras 6:20). *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12). Ezra is told the order of the end: when this vanishing world is finished, the books are opened before the firmament and all see together. John sees the same moment from the other side of it, the dead small and great standing before Elohim (God), the books opened, and another book opened with them, the book of life. Both witnesses put the opening of the books after the world's course is run, not before it. What Ezra was told would be shown as a token, John watched being done.

45212.new_note: *In that you have humbled thyself, as it becometh you, and have not judged thyself worthy to be much glorified among the righteous.* (2 Esdras 8:49). *I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.* (Luke 18:14). The Most High tells Ezra that what is marvellous in him is that he humbled himself and did not judge himself worthy to be much glorified among the righteous. The publican in the temple does the same, standing afar off and asking for mercy, and he goes home justified while the one who exalted himself does not. The rule Yahusha (Jesus) states, that the humble are exalted, is the rule by which Ezra is commended. Ezra's not counting himself worthy is exactly what the Most High counts worthy.

45221.new_note: *And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.* (2 Esdras 8:1). *Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* (Matthew 7:13). Ezra is told that this world was made for many and the world to come for few. Yahusha (Jesus) draws the same two ways on the ground: a wide gate and a broad way crowded with the many, and a strait gate that few find (Matthew 7:14). The many of the broad way are the many of this world; the few of the narrow way are the few of the world to come. The numbers match because the two men are describing the same thing.

49190.new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you. If you have abundance give alms accordingly: if you have but a little, be not afraid to give according to that little:* (Tobit 4:7–8). *Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for Elohim (God) loveth a cheerful giver.* (2 Corinthians 9:7). Tobit's son is told to give without an envious eye, out of abundance or out of a little. Paul says the same to Corinth: not grudgingly, not of necessity, each as he purposes in his heart, for Elohim (God) loves a cheerful giver. The heart that gives gladly is the heart the library had been shaping for generations before the letter. Paul was not writing a new ethic for a new people; he was writing Tobit's charge to the scattered children of Yashar'el (Israel) who had grown up among the nations and forgotten it.
49190.member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *when you give alms, let not your eye be envious.* Give of abundance or of little, without the envious eye; *not grudgingly, or of necessity* (2 Corinthians 9:7).
49190.old_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you. If you have abundance give alms accordingly: if you have but a little, be not afraid to give according to that little.* (Tobit 4:7-8). Tobit's charge to his son is the cheerful giver before the letter: give *let not your eye be envious* — the opposite of *grudgingly, or of necessity* — and give *according as he purposeth in his heart,* whether of abundance or of little. This is the heart-posture Paul commands and Elohim (God) loves (2 Corinthians 9:7), with the same promise that the giver's own face is not turned away from the favour of the Most High.

52030.new_note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). *Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):* (Philippians 2:6). The Hebrew library saw Wisdom as the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty. Brought forth from him, carrying his glory, and not a second god standing beside him. Paul describes the same one as being in the form of Elohim (God) and counting it no robbery to be equal with Elohim (God), and then in the next breath emptying himself. What flows from the glory is of the glory, so the equality is no theft; and what flows has a source, so he has a Father and takes the lower place freely. The Formed is not a rival to the Formless; he is what the Formless breathed out.
52030.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 — *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.* The breath of the power flowing from the glory is the one in the form of Elohim (God) (Philippians 2:6), brought forth, not a rival.
52030.old_note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* (Wisdom 7:25). The Hebrew library beheld Wisdom as *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty* — brought forth from the One, sharing his glory, yet not a second God beside him. This is the same posture as the Formed who was *in the form of Elohim (God)* (Philippians 2:6): the glory flows out FROM the Almighty into the One brought forth. Read as the Formed, Wisdom's breath-of-the-power is the Son who carries the Father's glory as the One emptied and exalted, not a co-equal rival to the Father.

55059.new_note: *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:9). *For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:* (Colossians 1:16). Wisdom says she was brought forth from the beginning, before the world, and that she will never fail. Paul says of the Son that all things in heaven and earth were created by him and for him — he is before all things, and everything holds together in him. These are one and the same: the Wisdom beside the Maker before the world is the Formed one through whom the all things were made, the Son who has a Father and is before every creature. Not a second co-equal Elohim (God) beside the Father, but the Word the Father brought forth, who came in flesh as Yahusha (Jesus).
55059.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:9 — *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.* Wisdom before the world is the Son by whom all things were created (Colossians 1:16).
55059.old_note: *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.* (Sirach 24:9). The library's Wisdom speaks of being *created from the beginning before the world* — brought forth before the ages, present when *the Creator of all things gave me a commandment* (Sirach 24:8). It is the same pre-creation pre-eminence the hymn ascribes to the Son: *by him were all things created... and he is before all things, and by him all things consist* (Colossians 1:16-17). Read as the Formed (not a second co-equal Elohim), this Wisdom-before-the-world is the firstborn-Heir brought forth before the works, through whom the all-things were made.

56814.new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *If any man or woman that believeth have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.* (1 Timothy 5:16). Tobit's charge is to turn his face from no poor man. Paul orders the believing household to relieve its own widows, so that the assembly's care is kept for the widows who have no one. Both put the first duty of mercy at home, in the household, before it goes out the door. The face never turned from the poor begins with the poor who are nearest.
56814.member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor.* The household relieves its own widows first (1 Timothy 5:16), the face never turned from the nearest poor.
56814.old_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you* (Tobit 4:7). Tobit's charge to give alms and *turn not your face from any poor* is the open-handed care Paul orders the believing household to extend to its widows: *If any man or woman that believeth have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed* (1 Timothy 5:16). The believer relieves his own widows so the assembly's care is kept for the truly desolate — the same generosity the library blesses, the face never turned from the poor.

56890.new_note: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:23). *Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.* (Psalm 19:11). David spent a whole psalm praising the law of Yahuah (God), sweeter than honey, warning his servant, holding great reward for the one who keeps it. Sirach names what David was praising: the Wisdom whose memorial is sweeter than honey is *the law which Moses commanded for an heritage*. The Torah is the inheritance of the congregations of Jacob, the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God). It is the heritage, not the curse, and the one who keeps it finds the great reward the psalmist promised.
56890.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:23 — *the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* The Wisdom sweeter than honey is the Torah, the inheritance whose keeping holds *great reward* (Psalm 19:11).
56890.old_note: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob* (Sirach 24:23). Here the restored witness names plainly what Psalm 19 has been praising: the Wisdom sweeter than honey IS *the law which Moses commanded for an heritage*. The Torah whose keeping holds *great reward* (Psalm 19:11) is *the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah*, the inheritance of the congregations — Red Line #6 spoken outright: the law is the heritage, never the curse.

57479.new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.* (Titus 3:14). Paul tells Titus to teach the believers a settled habit of usefulness: maintain good works for necessary uses, and so bear fruit. Tobit's charge is one of those works named exactly — give alms of what you have, turn your face from no poor man. This is the doing of mercy the Torah commands and the new heart loves, and the library had been teaching it to sons in exile long before Paul wrote to Crete.
57479.member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* The good work for necessary uses that keeps the believer from being unfruitful (Titus 3:14).
57479.old_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). Paul tells Titus to teach the believers a settled habit of usefulness: *let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful* (Titus 3:14). Tobit's charge — *Give alms of your substance... turn not your face from any poor* — is the same fruitful, neighbour-serving good work, the doing of mercy that the law commands and the new heart loves.

57480.new_note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* (Tobit 4:9). *This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in Elohim (God) might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.* (Titus 3:8). Tobit's son is told to give alms as treasure laid up against the day of need, out of a heart that fears Yahuah (God) and keeps his commandments (4:5). Paul tells Titus to affirm constantly that those who have believed be careful to maintain good works, good and profitable to men. The two are one posture: believing and doing are not rivals, and the open hand is what a believing heart does. The library had been teaching that to sons in exile long before the letter.
57480.member_note: Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Alms as good works laid up, the fruit of a believing heart careful to maintain them (Titus 3:8).
57480.old_note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* (Tobit 4:9). Tobit charges his son to do good works as a treasure laid up: *Give alms of your substance... If you have abundance give alms accordingly: if you have but a little, be not afraid to give... For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity* (Tobit 4:7-9). This is the very posture Paul commends — *that they which have believed in Elohim (God) might be careful to maintain good works... good and profitable unto men* (Titus 3:8) — the obedient, open-handed life that flows from a heart that fears Yahuah (God) and keeps his commandments (Tobit 4:5).

58679.new_note: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:23). *He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Yashar'el (Israel).* (Psalm 147:19). Sirach says it without a veil: Wisdom is the book of the covenant, the law Moses commanded as the heritage of Jacob. The psalmist had already sung that Yahuah (God) shows his word to Jacob and his statutes and judgments to Yashar'el (Israel), and the next verse of that psalm says he did not deal so with any nation. The Torah is an inheritance handed to one family, the congregations of Jacob, and an inheritance is a gift to a son, not a burden laid on a slave. The law is the heritage of Yashar'el (Israel), never the curse.
58679.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:23 — *the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* Wisdom named as the Torah, the heritage of Jacob; the word, statutes and judgments shown to Yashar'el (Israel) at Psalm 147:19.
58679.old_note: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob* (Sirach 24:23). Wisdom is named outright as the Torah, the heritage of Jacob — the same word *shewed unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Yashar'el (Israel)* (Psalm 147:19). The law Moses commanded is *an heritage to the congregations of Jacob*: the covenant inheritance no other nation received, Red Line #6 spoken plainly.

58818.new_note: *Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.* (Sirach 23:9). The Hebrew wisdom-library says it almost in James's own words: *Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One* (Sirach 23:9), for *he that sweareth and nameth Yahuah (God) continually shall not be faultless* (Sirach 23:10). This is the reverence James commands — *swear not... but let your yea be yea* (James 5:12). Not the abolition of the lawful oath, but the refusal to make the Holy Name a habit of the careless tongue.

58822.new_note: *My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* (Sirach 38:9). The Hebrew wisdom-library already directed the sick to prayer: *in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole,* and *Leave off from sin, and order yours hands aright, and cleanse your heart from all wickedness* (Sirach 38:9–10). James says the same — *Is any sick among you? let him... pray... and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him* (James 5:14-15). Prayer to Yahuah and the leaving of sin are the wisdom-library's medicine of the soul, which James lays on the assembly.

60259.new_note: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:7). *But if he be shameless and persisteth in his wrong-doing, even so forgive him from the heart, and leave to Elohim (God) the avenging.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:7). Sirach says remember the commandments and bear no malice to your neighbour, and overlook what was done in ignorance. The patriarch's testament goes further down the same road: even if the man is shameless and keeps on in his wrong, forgive him from the heart and leave the avenging to Elohim (God). Both are the commandment of Leviticus 19:18 lived out, no vengeance and no grudge. Forgiving the shameless is simply bearing no malice when it costs the most.
60259.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 28:7 — *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour.* No malice rooted in the commandments; the Testaments say *even so forgive him from the heart, and leave to Elohim (God) the avenging*.
60259.old_note: Sirach 28:7 — *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.* To forgive even the shameless and bear no grudge is Ben Sira's no-malice-to-thy-neighbour, rooted in the commandments.

65423.new_note: *Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:6). *Trust in Yahuah (LORD), and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed.* (Psalm 37:3). Sirach is repeating David. Believe in him, order your way aright, trust in him, is the same counsel as trust in Yahuah (LORD) and do good, the trusting and the doing bound together in one breath. Neither verse lets a man trust Yahuah (God) while walking however he pleases, and neither lets him order his way as if his own ordering were what held him up. The whole life leans on his help, and the leaning shows up as a way set aright.
65423.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 2:6 — *Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.* David's *Trust in Yahuah (LORD), and do good* (Psalm 37:3), repeated.
65423.old_note: *Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him* (Sirach 2:6). *Trust in Yahuah (LORD), and do good* (Psalm 37:3): the son of Sirach repeats the psalm's counsel — believe, order the way aright, trust — the same trust-and-do-good walk that leans the whole life on Yahuah's help.

71513.new_note: *Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:8). *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:* (Proverbs 3:9). Sirach is repeating Solomon almost word for word. Honour Yahuah (LORD) with what you have and with your firstfruits, Solomon says; give Yahuah (God) his honour and do not diminish the firstfruits of your hands, says Sirach, and he adds the good eye, the ungrudging eye, as the manner of it. The first and the best belong to Yahuah (God), and they are not to be cut short. The proverb came down whole, and Sirach handed it on whole.
71513.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:8 — *diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands.* Proverbs 3:9's firstfruits, kept whole and given with a good eye.
71513.old_note: *Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands* (Sirach 35:8). The restored witness keeps the proverb exactly: *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits* (Proverbs 3:9) is *Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands*. The firstfruits are not to be cut short; the honour of Yahuah is shown in the unstinted giving of the first and best.

71554.new_note: *And wisdom was with you: which knoweth your works, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your commandments.* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9). When Wisdom says *When he prepared the heavens, I was there* (Proverbs 8:27), the restored witness agrees: she *was present when you madest the world*. The Formed Son was there at the making — present at the founding, the workman who knew the Father's works because he wrought them with him.
71554.member_note: *was present when you madest the world* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9) — *When he prepared the heavens, I was there* (Proverbs 8:27): the Formed Son present at the making.

71934.new_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.* (Isaiah 55:1). Wisdom calls everyone who wants her to come and fill themselves; the prophet calls everyone who thirsts to come to the waters and eat without money. Both invitations go out to the desirous and the thirsty, and both offer what satisfies for nothing but the coming. There is no price at the door in either verse, only the call to come and be filled.
71934.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me.* Wisdom's invitation stands beside Isaiah 55:1, *come ye, buy, and eat*; the same free call to come and be filled.
71934.old_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits* (Sirach 24:19). Wisdom's invitation parallels the prophet's: *Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters... come ye, buy, and eat* (Isaiah 55:1) — the same come-and-be-filled call, all the desirous bidden to come and eat freely of what satisfies.

90159.new_note: *And left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she shewed them to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:14). *He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance:* (Psalm 105:21). Joseph was sold, went down into the pit, and was not left in bonds. Wisdom says she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom and power against those that oppressed him, showed his accusers to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory. The psalm tells it as history: Pharaoh made him lord of his house and ruler of all he had, and the next verse adds that he bound Pharaoh's princes at his pleasure and taught his senators wisdom (Psalm 105:22). The bound man binds the princes; the man accused as a liar is the one who ends up teaching the court. Wisdom went down into the pit with him and came up with him to the throne.
90159.member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 10:14 — *left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom.* Joseph, not left in bonds but made lord of Pharaoh's house (Psalm 105:21), is the sold man raised to the sceptre.
90159.old_note: *And left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she shewed them to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:14). *He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance: To bind his princes at his pleasure; and teach his senators wisdom* (Psalm 105:21-22): the same exaltation — not left in bonds but brought the sceptre of the kingdom, given power over his oppressors; the sold-and-bound one raised to rule and to teach wisdom.

103290.new_note: *O blessed are they which love you, for they shall rejoice in your peace: blessed are they which have been sorrowful for all your scourges; for they shall rejoice for you, when they have seen all your glory, and shall be glad for ever.* (Tobit 13:14). *Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee* (Psalm 122:6): Tobit, praying from captivity, sings the same blessing — they that love Jerusalem rejoice in her peace; the prosperity promised to her lovers in the psalm is the everlasting gladness Tobit foresees when her glory is restored.

108669.new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him: for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.* (Exodus 22:21). Tobit lives in Nineveh, a stranger among the nations, and he teaches his son the open hand to the poor. The Torah had told Yashar'el (Israel) not to vex or oppress the stranger, because they had been strangers in Egypt. Tobit is now the stranger, and he keeps the commandment from the other side of it, showing mercy where he might have asked for it. The promise mirrors the warning: turn not your face from the poor, and Yahuah (God) turns not his from you.
108669.member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The stranger in Nineveh keeps the mercy Torah commanded toward the stranger (Exodus 22:21).
108669.old_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you* (Tobit 4:7). The exile-righteous Tobit lives the Mishpat among the nations: the open hand to the poor is the same mercy the Torah commands in *Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him* (Exodus 22:21). The promise mirrors the warning — turn not thy face from the poor, and Yahuah turns not His from thee.

119997.new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 6:1). Tobit ties alms to one face, the face of Yahuah (God) turned toward the giver. Yahusha (Jesus) warns against alms done to be seen of men, because a gift aimed at men's eyes has already had its reward and the Father's is lost. Both are saying whose face the giver should be looking for. Tobit never mentions secrecy, but he sets the giver before the Father's face and no one else's, and that is the whole of the warning in Matthew.
119997.member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* Alms given for the Father's face, not for men's eyes (Matthew 6:1).
119997.reason: Corrected the old note: it called Tobit 4:7 'secret-handed giving', but the verse says nothing about secrecy. The real link is whose face the giver seeks (the Father's, not men's).
119997.old_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7) — old Yashar'el (Israel) taught its sons this very secret-handed giving.

122689.new_note: *That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:26). *Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father* (Matthew 10:29). The same Father who numbers the hairs and marks the sparrow's fall preserves His own — not the world's provision but His word keeps them.

122693.new_note: *Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother. Remember that you were begotten of them; and how can you recompense them the things that they have done for you?* (Ecclesiasticus 7:27–28). 135262.new_note: *Many have sinned for a small matter; and he that seeks for abundance will turn his eyes away.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:1). *And Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich, I have found me out substance: in all my labours they shall find none iniquity in me that were sin.* (Hosea 12:8). Ephraim had grown rich and could find no sin in any of his labours, and Sirach tells you how that happens: the one who is chasing abundance turns his eyes away from the small matters he sinned in to get it. The gain does not remove the sin. It hides the sin from the man who did it, until he can stand in the prophet's hearing and swear his hands are clean. That blindness is what Hosea is prophesying against, and it is what Sirach is warning the reader of before it sets in.

147791.new_note: *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:1). *Now therefore, my lord, as Yahuah (LORD) liveth, and as thy soul liveth, seeing Yahuah (LORD) hath withholden thee from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand, now let thine enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.* (1 Samuel 25:26). Abigail met David on the road while he was riding to shed Nabal's blood, and she told him plainly that Yahuah (LORD) had held him back from avenging himself with his own hand. Sirach says why that mattered: the man who takes his own vengeance finds vengeance from Yahuah (God), and his sins are kept in remembrance. David was one hour from writing that sentence against himself, and a wise woman turned him from it. He blessed her for it, and Nabal died by the hand of Yahuah (God) ten days later without David lifting a finger.

177372.new_note: *And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.* (3 Maccabees 1:11). *Therefore thou and thy sons with thee shall keep your priest’s office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail; and ye shall serve: I have given your priest’s office unto you as a service of gift: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.* (Numbers 18:7). Ptolemy saw the temple, admired it, and decided he would walk into the sanctuary itself. The priests told him the rule: no one of the nation, not even the priests, only the high priest, and he only once a year. The king called that an honour he was being denied; the Torah calls it a death sentence for anyone else who comes near. Yahuah (God) gave the priesthood to Aaron and his sons as a gift, within the vail as well as at the altar, and said the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. The high priest's one entry a year on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:2) was not a privilege to be extended; it was the boundary Yahuah (God) set on his own dwelling, and Ptolemy was pressing against the boundary and its penalty.

177475.new_note: *And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.* (2 Esdras 7:30). *I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light.* (Jeremiah 4:23). Esdras is told the world returns to the old silence for seven days, no man remaining. Jeremiah was shown the like: the earth *without form, and void,* the heavens without light, and, as he goes on, *lo, there was no man* (Jeremiah 4:25). These are the words of the earth before the first day, when *the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep* (Genesis 1:2); the old silence is the earth returned to that first stillness, no man remaining, before *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her* (2 Esdras 7:32).
